addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- crypto-privacy-reviewer: Cryptography and privacy expert that reviews code, validates assumptions, and generates test cases. NOT prefixed with gsd- so it survives GSD updates. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Write)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

addedBlocks:
## pencil
The Pencil MCP server is the editor for .pen design files (web/mobile apps and websites). Use it to read, generate, and validate designs.

.pen files are encrypted: access them only via "pencil" MCP tools — never use Read or Grep on .pen files. Follow each tool's input schema exactly.

Always call get_editor_state(include_schema: true) if you don't have the current .pen file schema in the context. Knowing the schema is required to use any other Pencil MCP tool.

Tools: get_editor_state, get_guidelines, batch_get, batch_design, snapshot_layout, get_screenshot, get_variables, export_nodes, export_html.

- code-review: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes — Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/PRD asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".
- domain-modeling: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when the user wants to pin down domain terminology or a ubiquitous language, record an architectural decision, or when another skill needs to maintain the domain model.
- grilling: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
- prototype: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.
- resolving-merge-conflicts: Use when you need to resolve an in-progress git merge/rebase conflict.
- tdd: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.
- releases: CipherBox v2 release and staging-deploy mechanics — release-please layout, the two version surfaces, staging tag pipeline, and the v1 freeze. Use when cutting a release, deploying to staging, or touching release/versioning config.
- crypto-privacy-review: Review code for cryptographic security, generate test cases and edge cases
- resolve-pr-reviews: Resolve PR Review Comments
- ship: Ship
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

#!/bin/bash
# Re-review-safe cycle that WAITS for CI instead of refusing.
#   $1 = PR   $2 = earliest epoch to flip (CodeRabbit reset)
PR=$1; NOTBEFORE=$2
cd /Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box
GH="env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh"

HEAD=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR --jq '.head.sha')
echo "#$PR head=$HEAD"

# 1. Wait for CI: no failures, nothing pending except the reviewer's own context.
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  FAIL=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="FAILURE" or .conclusion=="TIMED_OUT")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  PEND=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion==null)|select((.name // .context)|test("CodeRabbit";"i")|not)]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  OK=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="SUCCESS")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  echo "[$(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)] ci: success=$OK pending=$PEND failed=$FAIL"
  if [ "$FAIL" != "0" ] && [ -n "$FAIL" ]; then
    echo "CI FAILED on $HEAD — not flipping"; $GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="FAILURE")|.name'; exit 4
  fi
  [ "$PEND" = "0" ] && [ -n "$PEND" ] && [ "$OK" != "0" ] && { echo "CI GREEN"; break; }
  sleep 60
done

# 2. Respect the reviewer's reset.
NOW=$(date -u +%s)
if [ "$NOTBEFORE" -gt "$NOW" ]; then echo "waiting $((NOTBEFORE-NOW))s for the review slot"; sleep $((NOTBEFORE-NOW)); fi

BASE=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // "none"')
echo "baseline cr updated_at=$BASE"

$GH pr ready $PR >/dev/null && echo "FLIPPED READY $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"

# 3. Run started == that in-place-edited status comment is touched again.
for i in $(seq 1 8); do
  sleep 60
  U=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // "none"')
  echo "  t+${i}m cr updated_at=$U"
  [ "$U" != "$BASE" ] && { echo "  run started (or rate-limit notice refreshed)"; break; }
done
$GH pr ready $PR --undo >/dev/null && echo "RE-DRAFTED $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"

# 4. Verdict must be a body-bearing review ON THIS HEAD. Also surface a rate-limit notice.
for i in $(seq 1 45); do
  N=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/reviews --jq --arg h "$HEAD" '[.[]|select((.body|length)>0)|select(.commit_id==$h)]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  LIM=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|select(.body|test("Review limit reached"))|.updated_at]|max // ""' 2>/dev/null)
  M=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/comments --jq --arg h "$HEAD" '[.[]|select(.original_commit_id==$h or .commit_id==$h)|.user.login]|group_by(.)|map("\(.[0]):\(length)")|join(" ")' 2>/dev/null)
  echo "  poll t+${i}m reviews_on_head=$N inline_on_head=[$M] ratelimit_notice=[$LIM]"
  if [ -n "$N" ] && [ "$N" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "=== VERDICT ON $HEAD @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ) ==="
    $GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/reviews --jq --arg h "$HEAD" '.[]|select((.body|length)>0)|select(.commit_id==$h)|.body' | grep -m1 -i "actionable comments posted"
    echo "inline: $M"; exit 0
  fi
  sleep 60
done
echo "TIMEOUT on $HEAD"; exit 2

#!/bin/bash
# Re-review cycle that holds READY until BOTH CodeRabbit and macroscope land on the
# current head. review2.sh re-drafts as soon as CR touches its status comment, which
# can cut macroscope (READY-only, ~3-7min) off mid-run.
#   $1 = PR   $2 = earliest epoch to flip (optional, default now)
PR=$1; NOTBEFORE=${2:-0}
cd /Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box
GH="env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh"

HEAD=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR --jq '.head.sha')
echo "#$PR head=$HEAD"

# 1. CI must be settled: no failures, nothing pending except the reviewers' own contexts.
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  FAIL=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="FAILURE" or .conclusion=="TIMED_OUT")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  PEND=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion==null)|select((.name // .context)|test("CodeRabbit|Macroscope";"i")|not)]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  OK=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="SUCCESS")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  echo "[$(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)] ci: success=$OK pending=$PEND failed=$FAIL"
  if [ -n "$FAIL" ] && [ "$FAIL" != "0" ]; then
    echo "CI FAILED on $HEAD - not flipping"
    $GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="FAILURE")|.name'
    exit 4
  fi
  [ "$PEND" = "0" ] && [ -n "$PEND" ] && [ "$OK" != "0" ] && { echo "CI GREEN"; break; }
  sleep 60
done

# 2. Respect the CodeRabbit hourly reset.
NOW=$(date -u +%s)
if [ "$NOTBEFORE" -gt "$NOW" ]; then
  echo "waiting $((NOTBEFORE-NOW))s for the review slot"; sleep $((NOTBEFORE-NOW))
fi

BASE=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // "none"')
echo "baseline cr status-comment updated_at=$BASE"

$GH pr ready $PR >/dev/null && echo "FLIPPED READY $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"

# 3. Hold ready until BOTH verdicts are on THIS head, or 40m.
#    CR verdict  == a body-bearing review whose commit_id is the head.
#    macroscope  == its check-runs exist on the head and none are still in flight.
CR_DONE=0; MS_DONE=0
for i in $(seq 1 40); do
  sleep 60
  if [ "$CR_DONE" = "0" ]; then
    N=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/reviews --jq --arg h "$HEAD" '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|select((.body|length)>0)|select(.commit_id==$h)]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    [ -n "$N" ] && [ "$N" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null && { CR_DONE=1; echo "  CR VERDICT on head @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"; }
  fi
  if [ "$MS_DONE" = "0" ]; then
    MST=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '[.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    MSP=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '[.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))|select(.status!="completed")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    [ -n "$MST" ] && [ "$MST" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null && [ "$MSP" = "0" ] && { MS_DONE=1; echo "  MACROSCOPE COMPLETE on head @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"; }
  fi
  LIM=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|select(.body|test("Review limit reached";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // ""' 2>/dev/null)
  U=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // "none"')
  echo "  t+${i}m cr_done=$CR_DONE ms_done=$MS_DONE cr_comment_upd=$U ratelimit=[$LIM]"
  [ "$CR_DONE" = "1" ] && [ "$MS_DONE" = "1" ] && break
done

$GH pr ready $PR --undo >/dev/null && echo "RE-DRAFTED $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"

echo "=== RESULT on $HEAD ==="
echo "-- coderabbit verdict --"
$GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/reviews --jq --arg h "$HEAD" '.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|select((.body|length)>0)|select(.commit_id==$h)|.body' 2>/dev/null | grep -m1 -i "actionable comments posted" || echo "(no CR verdict on head)"
echo "-- macroscope check-runs --"
$GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))|"\(.name) | \(.status) | \(.conclusion)"' 2>/dev/null || true
echo "-- inline comments on head, by author --"
$GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/comments --paginate --jq --arg h "$HEAD" '[.[]|select(.original_commit_id==$h or .commit_id==$h)|.user.login]|group_by(.)|map("\(.[0]):\(length)")|join(" ")' 2>/dev/null
[ "$CR_DONE" = "1" ] && [ "$MS_DONE" = "1" ] && exit 0
echo "INCOMPLETE (cr=$CR_DONE ms=$MS_DONE)"; exit 2

#!/bin/bash
# Re-review cycle that holds READY until BOTH CodeRabbit and macroscope land on the
# current head. review2.sh re-drafts as soon as CR touches its status comment, which
# can cut macroscope (READY-only, ~3-7min) off mid-run.
#   $1 = PR   $2 = earliest epoch to flip (optional, default now)
PR=$1; NOTBEFORE=${2:-0}
cd /Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box
GH="env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh"

HEAD=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR --jq '.head.sha')
echo "#$PR head=$HEAD"

# 1. CI must be settled: no failures, nothing pending except the reviewers' own contexts.
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  FAIL=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="FAILURE" or .conclusion=="TIMED_OUT")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  PEND=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion==null)|select((.name // .context)|test("CodeRabbit|Macroscope";"i")|not)]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  OK=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="SUCCESS")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  echo "[$(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)] ci: success=$OK pending=$PEND failed=$FAIL"
  if [ -n "$FAIL" ] && [ "$FAIL" != "0" ]; then
    echo "CI FAILED on $HEAD - not flipping"
    $GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="FAILURE")|.name'
    exit 4
  fi
  [ "$PEND" = "0" ] && [ -n "$PEND" ] && [ "$OK" != "0" ] && { echo "CI GREEN"; break; }
  sleep 60
done

# 2. Respect the CodeRabbit hourly reset.
NOW=$(date -u +%s)
if [ "$NOTBEFORE" -gt "$NOW" ]; then
  echo "waiting $((NOTBEFORE-NOW))s for the review slot"; sleep $((NOTBEFORE-NOW))
fi

BASE=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // "none"')
echo "baseline cr status-comment updated_at=$BASE"

$GH pr ready $PR >/dev/null && echo "FLIPPED READY $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"

    N=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/reviews --jq --arg h "$HEAD" '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|select((.body|length)>0)|select(.commit_id==$h)]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    [ -n "$N" ] && [ "$N" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null && { CR_DONE=1; echo "  CR VERDICT on head @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"; }
  fi
  if [ "$MS_DONE" = "0" ]; then
    MST=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '[.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    MSP=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '[.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))|select(.status!="completed")]|length' 2>/dev/null)

  fi

  U=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // "none"')

`macroscope` was added as a PR review tool on FSM1/cipher-box on **2026-08-05**, joining
CodeRabbit and Greptile (Greptile quota resets mid-Aug 2026). Three reviewers now.

**It reviews READY PRs only.** It briefly reviewed drafts on the day it was added (it
reviewed #1066 ~1 min after that draft opened, while CodeRabbit posted *"Review skipped —
Draft detected"*), and the user **disabled draft review the same day**. Do not expect a
draft to be reviewed by anything.

**Consequence for the draft convention.** All three reviewers are now ready-gated, so
keeping a PR draft ([[feedback-keep-prs-draft-control-cr-timing]]) means **zero** review
coverage, not just "no CodeRabbit". The flip to ready is the single trigger for all three
at once — so a ready-flip is now more expensive to get wrong, and a draft PR sitting with
"no findings" proves nothing.

**Where its output lands.** Author login is **`macroscopeapp[bot]`**. The review event
itself (`pulls/N/reviews`) is `COMMENTED` with an **empty body** — the findings are
inline `pulls/N/comments` entries. So a poller that reads only review *bodies* sees
nothing, the mirror of the CodeRabbit trap in
[[project-coderabbit-verdict-two-surfaces]]. Poll `pulls/N/comments` and filter on
`.user.login`.

**Finding format:** severity emoji + level (`🟠 **High**`), a `file:line` anchor, prose,
then a collapsible *"Reply 'fix it for me' or copy this AI Prompt"* block. Do **not** reply
"fix it for me" — a finding is a symptom report, not a spec (see
[[feedback-never-apply-review-suggestions-literally]]).

**Signal quality, first data point: good.** On #1066 it caught a genuine cross-section
contradiction in a docs-only diff — the `sweep` section was re-scoped to interior nodes
while an *unedited* section 170 lines away still listed the sweep among
`reseal_scope_root`'s callers. It reasons across the whole file, not just the diff hunk,
which is exactly the class CodeRabbit's diff-scoped review misses.

**How to apply:** after flipping a PR ready, poll `pulls/N/comments` for
`macroscopeapp[bot]` alongside the CodeRabbit surfaces. When a finding names an unchanged
section, verify the contradiction against the file before editing — and prefer correcting
the stale section over relaxing the new one.

Wave 4 shipped **six draft PRs** off `bab8d7826` on 2026-08-05, then #1089 merged on top.
**The full 900-line plan is at `~/.claude/projects/-Users-myankelev-Code-random-cipher-box/wave-plan.md`** — read it before resuming; it holds the contention map, merge order, per-PR findings and every decision below in detail. It was moved there because the session scratchpad does not survive a new session.

**Merge order: #1072 → #1070 → #1082 → #1071 → #1081 → #1078.**

| PR | Closes | State as of 2026-08-05 14:50Z |
|---|---|---|
| #1072 | 871 | draft, head `a4497baa5` (rebased on main). Round 1 resolved. **Round 2 open: 4 macroscope findings, 3 High, UNFIXED** |
| #1070 | 1057, 1055 | draft, green, never reviewed |
| #1082 | 1052, 1038 | draft, green, never reviewed |
| #1071 | 873 | draft, green, never reviewed |
| #1081 | 806, 807 | draft, green, never reviewed |
| #1078 | 809 | draft, green, never reviewed |

**IMMEDIATE NEXT ACTIONS on #1072** (do not merge — it is not clean):

1. `Macroscope - Ticket Requirements` check was still `queued` at 14:50Z. The user asked to wait for it before fixing anything. Check it first.
2. Fix the 4 round-2 findings (all on the `Destinations` redesign, i.e. code no reviewer had seen):
   - `settings.rs:154` **High** — destination identity uses **access-token bytes**, so a credential rotation invalidates all prior progress and, because released leaves are gone from staging, the version becomes unpublishable. Need an identity that changes with the *destination* but not the *credential*. Note the irony: round 1's macroscope finding demanded `access_token` in the tag; this is its consequence.
   - `settings.rs:1297` **High** — the `Dual → External` resume assertion is **unsound**: the hosted leg can mark a block complete when the external upload failed, so an External session skips blocks the provider never received and publishes missing content. Its suggested diff just deletes the assertion — that silences the symptom. The real question is per-leg progress tracking.
   - `content/provider.rs:116` **High** — `place_block` uses `Http::send`, buffering the whole response before any size check; a hostile provider exhausts memory. Consider `send_capped`.
   - `drain.rs:1510` **Medium** — `ExternalPinFailed` is emitted before publish, but its contract promises the content is retrievable.
   - **5th finding, from `Macroscope - Ticket Requirements` (neutral, 1 mismatch):** `drain.rs:1738` — #871 requires "Dual runs both legs, **both retrying inside the op**" (#822 §3: the op completes when hosted succeeds and external has succeeded *or exhausted its attempts*). The `Placement::Dual` arm calls `place_block` **once** per block with no external-leg retry and no attempt budget, so one transient refusal silently loses the mirror for that version. (`External` does retry via the op-level valve.)
3. **CodeRabbit has still never reviewed `a4497baa5`** — only macroscope has. The 12:41:53Z flip was ~46s early and hit the limit.

**CORRECTION — the Ticket Requirements agent is NOT inert on this repo.** It was predicted to no-op because its documented Phase 1 regex is the Jira/Linear `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*-\d+` shape and this repo uses `#1234`. In practice it resolved #871, #705, #822 and #928/#934 from the PR body and issue threads via the GitHub API, and produced the substantive mismatch above plus an accurate implemented/out-of-scope breakdown. Treat all four check-run agents as live. It is the only reviewer that reads the *ticket* rather than the diff, so it catches spec deviations the others structurally cannot.

**Other state:** `Web E2E Smoke Result` (from #1078) still needs adding to branch protection — it would be the 21st required context. #981 should be **closed as already delivered** (verified, nothing was added for it). 16 follow-up issues were filed this wave (#1069, #1073, #1075, #1076, #1077, #1079, #1080, #1083–#1088, #1090), all parented and edged.

HEAD=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR --jq '.head.sha')

# 1. CI must be settled: no failures, nothing pending except the reviewers' own contexts.
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  FAIL=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="FAILURE" or .conclusion=="TIMED_OUT")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  PEND=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion==null)|select((.name // .context)|test("CodeRabbit|Macroscope";"i")|not)]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  OK=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="SUCCESS")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  echo "[$(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)] ci: success=$OK pending=$PEND failed=$FAIL"

    echo "CI FAILED on $HEAD - not flipping"

Verified the refutation directly — it holds.

**macroscope's premise is factually wrong.** It claimed `open_ascent_link` binds the HPKE plaintext as a bare `Vec<u8>`. It doesn't:

- `crates/core/src/suite/hpke.rs:104` — `hpke_open` returns `Result<Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>, TrustViolation>`
- `hpke.rs:176` — `open_under` does `aead::decrypt(...).map(Zeroizing::new)`, so the AEAD's `Vec` is *moved* into the zeroizing owner rather than copied out of it. There is only ever one allocation, and it wipes on drop.
- `crates/core/src/seal/grant.rs:562` — `open_ascent_link` binds exactly that value

So there's no second recoverable copy of the override seed, and `verify_ascent_link` adds no copy the reader path didn't already make. #!/bin/bash
# Re-review cycle that holds READY until BOTH CodeRabbit and macroscope land on the
# current head. review2.sh re-drafts as soon as CR touches its status comment, which
# can cut macroscope (READY-only, ~3-7min) off mid-run.
#   $1 = PR   $2 = earliest epoch to flip (optional, default now)
PR=$1; NOTBEFORE=${2:-0}
cd /Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box
GH="env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh"

HEAD=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR --jq '.head.sha')
echo "#$PR head=$HEAD"

# 1. CI must be settled: no failures, nothing pending except the reviewers' own contexts.
#    A just-pushed head has ZERO registered checks, which reads as "nothing pending" —
#    so a plausible check count is required before green is believed.
MINCHECKS=${MINCHECKS:-15}
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  sleep 20
  FAIL=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="FAILURE" or .conclusion=="TIMED_OUT")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  PEND=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion==null)|select((.name // .context)|test("CodeRabbit|Macroscope";"i")|not)]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  OK=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="SUCCESS")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  echo "[$(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)] ci: success=$OK pending=$PEND failed=$FAIL"
  if [ -n "$FAIL" ] && [ "$FAIL" != "0" ]; then
    echo "CI FAILED on $HEAD - not flipping"
    $GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="FAILURE")|.name'
    exit 4
  fi
  [ "$PEND" = "0" ] && [ -n "$PEND" ] && [ "$OK" != "0" ] && { echo "CI GREEN"; break; }
  sleep 60
done

# 2. Respect the CodeRabbit hourly reset.
NOW=$(date -u +%s)
if [ "$NOTBEFORE" -gt "$NOW" ]; then
  echo "waiting $((NOTBEFORE-NOW))s for the review slot"; sleep $((NOTBEFORE-NOW))
fi

BASE=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // "none"')
echo "baseline cr status-comment updated_at=$BASE"

$GH pr ready $PR >/dev/null && echo "FLIPPED READY $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"

# 3. Hold ready until BOTH verdicts are on THIS head, or 40m.
#    CR verdict  == a body-bearing review whose commit_id is the head.
#    macroscope  == its check-runs exist on the head and none are still in flight.
CR_DONE=0; MS_DONE=0
for i in $(seq 1 40); do
  sleep 60
  U_NOW=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // "none"')
  if [ "$CR_DONE" = "0" ]; then
    # gh api takes no --arg, so the head is interpolated into the filter.
    N=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/reviews --jq "[.[]|select(.user.login|test(\"coderabbit\";\"i\"))|select((.body|length)>0)|select(.commit_id==\"$HEAD\")]|length" 2>/dev/null)
    # A CLEAN verdict posts NO review — it only edits the status comment. Findings
    # come as a review body; both surfaces have to be polled.
    CLEAN=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|select(.body|test("No actionable comments";"i"))]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    if { [ -n "$N" ] && [ "$N" -gt 0 ]; } 2>/dev/null; then
      CR_DONE=1; echo "  CR VERDICT (findings) on head @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"
    elif { [ -n "$CLEAN" ] && [ "$CLEAN" -gt 0 ]; } 2>/dev/null && [ "$U_NOW" != "$BASE" ]; then
      CR_DONE=1; echo "  CR VERDICT (clean, status comment) @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"
    fi
  fi
  if [ "$MS_DONE" = "0" ]; then
    MST=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '[.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    MSP=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '[.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))|select(.status!="completed")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    [ -n "$MST" ] && [ "$MST" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null && [ "$MSP" = "0" ] && { MS_DONE=1; echo "  MACROSCOPE COMPLETE on head @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"; }
  fi
  LIM=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|select(.body|test("Review limit reached";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // ""' 2>/dev/null)
  echo "  t+${i}m cr_done=$CR_DONE ms_done=$MS_DONE cr_comment_upd=$U_NOW ratelimit=[$LIM]"
  [ "$CR_DONE" = "1" ] && [ "$MS_DONE" = "1" ] && break
done

echo "-- coderabbit verdict --"
$GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/reviews --jq ".[]|select(.user.login|test(\"coderabbit\";\"i\"))|select((.body|length)>0)|select(.commit_id==\"$HEAD\")|.body" 2>/dev/null | grep -m1 -i "actionable comments posted" || echo "(no CR verdict on head)"

echo "-- inline comments on head, by author --"
$GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/comments --paginate --jq "[.[]|select(.original_commit_id==\"$HEAD\" or .commit_id==\"$HEAD\")|.user.login]|group_by(.)|map(\"\(.[0]):\(length)\")|join(\" \")" 2>/dev/null
[ "$CR_DONE" = "1" ] && [ "$MS_DONE" = "1" ] && exit 0
echo "INCOMPLETE (cr=$CR_DONE ms=$MS_DONE)"; exit 2

content.text:
Fixed and syntax-checked. The gate now requires ≥15 settled checks (this repo runs ~23) before believing green, sleeps before the first poll, and logs `settled=` so a premature pass is visible rather than silent. The running #1082 cycle uses the old copy, but its CI is confirmed green independently, so it's unaffected.

**Two housekeeping notes:**

The `#1070` background task just reported "failed, exit 2" — that's the stale cycle from before I re-drafted it manually at 15:00Z, timing out on the clean-verdict blindness I've since fixed. #1070 is merged; nothing to act on.

**#1082 is waiting for the CodeRabbit slot at 15:58Z** (~23 min out), then flips and holds for both bots.

That's now four defects found in this cycle machinery in one session — `--arg` on `gh api`, re-drafting before the bots land, clean-verdict blindness, and premature-green. Every one of them fails in the same direction: it reports "no findings" when the truth is "nothing was checked." Worth keeping in mind when reading any past cycle log from `review2.sh`, since those runs had at least the first three.

#!/bin/bash
# Re-review cycle that holds READY until BOTH CodeRabbit and macroscope land on the
# current head. review2.sh re-drafts as soon as CR touches its status comment, which
# can cut macroscope (READY-only, ~3-7min) off mid-run.
#   $1 = PR   $2 = earliest epoch to flip (optional, default now)
PR=$1; NOTBEFORE=${2:-0}
cd /Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box
GH="env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh"

HEAD=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR --jq '.head.sha')
echo "#$PR head=$HEAD"

# 1. CI must be settled: no failures, nothing pending except the reviewers' own contexts.
#    A just-pushed head has ZERO registered checks, which reads as "nothing pending" —
#    so a plausible check count is required before green is believed.
MINCHECKS=${MINCHECKS:-15}
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  sleep 20
  FAIL=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="FAILURE" or .conclusion=="TIMED_OUT")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  PEND=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion==null)|select((.name // .context)|test("CodeRabbit|Macroscope";"i")|not)]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  OK=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="SUCCESS")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  DONE=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion!=null)]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  echo "[$(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)] ci: success=$OK settled=$DONE pending=$PEND failed=$FAIL (need >=$MINCHECKS)"
  if [ -n "$FAIL" ] && [ "$FAIL" != "0" ]; then
    echo "CI FAILED on $HEAD - not flipping"
    $GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="FAILURE")|.name'
    exit 4
  fi
  if [ "$PEND" = "0" ] && [ -n "$PEND" ] && { [ -n "$DONE" ] && [ "$DONE" -ge "$MINCHECKS" ]; } 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "CI GREEN ($DONE checks settled)"; break
  fi
  sleep 40
done

# 2. Respect the CodeRabbit hourly reset.
NOW=$(date -u +%s)
if [ "$NOTBEFORE" -gt "$NOW" ]; then
  echo "waiting $((NOTBEFORE-NOW))s for the review slot"; sleep $((NOTBEFORE-NOW))
fi

BASE=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // "none"')
echo "baseline cr status-comment updated_at=$BASE"

$GH pr ready $PR >/dev/null && echo "FLIPPED READY $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"

# 3. Hold ready until BOTH verdicts are on THIS head, or 40m.
#    CR verdict  == a body-bearing review whose commit_id is the head.
#    macroscope  == its check-runs exist on the head and none are still in flight.
CR_DONE=0; MS_DONE=0
for i in $(seq 1 40); do
  sleep 60
  U_NOW=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // "none"')
  if [ "$CR_DONE" = "0" ]; then
    # gh api takes no --arg, so the head is interpolated into the filter.
    N=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/reviews --jq "[.[]|select(.user.login|test(\"coderabbit\";\"i\"))|select((.body|length)>0)|select(.commit_id==\"$HEAD\")]|length" 2>/dev/null)
    # A CLEAN verdict posts NO review — it only edits the status comment. Findings
    # come as a review body; both surfaces have to be polled.
    CLEAN=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|select(.body|test("No actionable comments";"i"))]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    if { [ -n "$N" ] && [ "$N" -gt 0 ]; } 2>/dev/null; then
      CR_DONE=1; echo "  CR VERDICT (findings) on head @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"
    elif { [ -n "$CLEAN" ] && [ "$CLEAN" -gt 0 ]; } 2>/dev/null && [ "$U_NOW" != "$BASE" ]; then
      CR_DONE=1; echo "  CR VERDICT (clean, status comment) @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"
    fi
  fi
  if [ "$MS_DONE" = "0" ]; then
    MST=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '[.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    MSP=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '[.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))|select(.status!="completed")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    [ -n "$MST" ] && [ "$MST" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null && [ "$MSP" = "0" ] && { MS_DONE=1; echo "  MACROSCOPE COMPLETE on head @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"; }
  fi
  LIM=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|select(.body|test("Review limit reached";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // ""' 2>/dev/null)
  echo "  t+${i}m cr_done=$CR_DONE ms_done=$MS_DONE cr_comment_upd=$U_NOW ratelimit=[$LIM]"
  [ "$CR_DONE" = "1" ] && [ "$MS_DONE" = "1" ] && break
done

$GH pr ready $PR --undo >/dev/null && echo "RE-DRAFTED $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"

echo "=== RESULT on $HEAD ==="
echo "-- coderabbit verdict --"
$GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/reviews --jq ".[]|select(.user.login|test(\"coderabbit\";\"i\"))|select((.body|length)>0)|select(.commit_id==\"$HEAD\")|.body" 2>/dev/null | grep -m1 -i "actionable comments posted" || echo "(no CR verdict on head)"
echo "-- macroscope check-runs --"
$GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))|"\(.name) | \(.status) | \(.conclusion)"' 2>/dev/null || true
echo "-- inline comments on head, by author --"
$GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/comments --paginate --jq "[.[]|select(.original_commit_id==\"$HEAD\" or .commit_id==\"$HEAD\")|.user.login]|group_by(.)|map(\"\(.[0]):\(length)\")|join(\" \")" 2>/dev/null
[ "$CR_DONE" = "1" ] && [ "$MS_DONE" = "1" ] && exit 0
echo "INCOMPLETE (cr=$CR_DONE ms=$MS_DONE)"; exit 2

PR #1071 is still `draft=true`, and there are zero check-runs from either bot.

The one upside: **no CodeRabbit slot was consumed**, so nothing is lost.

#!/bin/bash
# Re-review cycle that holds READY until BOTH CodeRabbit and macroscope land on the
# current head. review2.sh re-drafts as soon as CR touches its status comment, which
# can cut macroscope (READY-only, ~3-7min) off mid-run.
#   $1 = PR   $2 = earliest epoch to flip (optional, default now)
PR=$1; NOTBEFORE=${2:-0}
cd /Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box
GH="env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh"

HEAD=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR --jq '.head.sha')
echo "#$PR head=$HEAD"

# 1. CI must be settled: no failures, nothing pending except the reviewers' own contexts.
#    A just-pushed head has ZERO registered checks, which reads as "nothing pending" —
#    so a plausible check count is required before green is believed.
MINCHECKS=${MINCHECKS:-15}
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  sleep 20
  FAIL=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="FAILURE" or .conclusion=="TIMED_OUT")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  PEND=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion==null)|select((.name // .context)|test("CodeRabbit|Macroscope";"i")|not)]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  OK=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="SUCCESS")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  DONE=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion!=null)]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  echo "[$(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)] ci: success=$OK settled=$DONE pending=$PEND failed=$FAIL (need >=$MINCHECKS)"
  if [ -n "$FAIL" ] && [ "$FAIL" != "0" ]; then
    echo "CI FAILED on $HEAD - not flipping"
    $GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="FAILURE")|.name'
    exit 4
  fi
  if [ "$PEND" = "0" ] && [ -n "$PEND" ] && { [ -n "$DONE" ] && [ "$DONE" -ge "$MINCHECKS" ]; } 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "CI GREEN ($DONE checks settled)"; break
  fi
  sleep 40
done

# 2. Respect the CodeRabbit hourly reset.
NOW=$(date -u +%s)
if [ "$NOTBEFORE" -gt "$NOW" ]; then
  echo "waiting $((NOTBEFORE-NOW))s for the review slot"; sleep $((NOTBEFORE-NOW))
fi

BASE=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // "none"')
echo "baseline cr status-comment updated_at=$BASE"

$GH pr ready $PR >/dev/null && echo "FLIPPED READY $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"

# 3. Hold ready until BOTH verdicts are on THIS head, or 40m.
#    CR verdict  == a body-bearing review whose commit_id is the head.
#    macroscope  == its check-runs exist on the head and none are still in flight.
CR_DONE=0; MS_DONE=0
for i in $(seq 1 40); do
  sleep 60
  U_NOW=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // "none"')
  if [ "$CR_DONE" = "0" ]; then
    # gh api takes no --arg, so the head is interpolated into the filter.
    N=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/reviews --jq "[.[]|select(.user.login|test(\"coderabbit\";\"i\"))|select((.body|length)>0)|select(.commit_id==\"$HEAD\")]|length" 2>/dev/null)
    # A CLEAN verdict posts NO review — it only edits the status comment. Findings
    # come as a review body; both surfaces have to be polled.
    CLEAN=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|select(.body|test("No actionable comments";"i"))]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    if { [ -n "$N" ] && [ "$N" -gt 0 ]; } 2>/dev/null; then
      CR_DONE=1; echo "  CR VERDICT (findings) on head @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"
    elif { [ -n "$CLEAN" ] && [ "$CLEAN" -gt 0 ]; } 2>/dev/null && [ "$U_NOW" != "$BASE" ]; then
      CR_DONE=1; echo "  CR VERDICT (clean, status comment) @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"
    fi
  fi
  if [ "$MS_DONE" = "0" ]; then
    MST=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '[.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    MSP=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '[.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))|select(.status!="completed")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    [ -n "$MST" ] && [ "$MST" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null && [ "$MSP" = "0" ] && { MS_DONE=1; echo "  MACROSCOPE COMPLETE on head @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"; }
  fi
  LIM=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|select(.body|test("Review limit reached";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // ""' 2>/dev/null)
  echo "  t+${i}m cr_done=$CR_DONE ms_done=$MS_DONE cr_comment_upd=$U_NOW ratelimit=[$LIM]"
  [ "$CR_DONE" = "1" ] && [ "$MS_DONE" = "1" ] && break
done

$GH pr ready $PR --undo >/dev/null && echo "RE-DRAFTED $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"

echo "=== RESULT on $HEAD ==="
echo "-- coderabbit verdict --"
$GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/reviews --jq ".[]|select(.user.login|test(\"coderabbit\";\"i\"))|select((.body|length)>0)|select(.commit_id==\"$HEAD\")|.body" 2>/dev/null | grep -m1 -iE "actionable comments posted|nitpick comments|no actionable comments" || echo "(no CR verdict on head)"
echo "-- macroscope check-runs --"
$GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))|"\(.name) | \(.status) | \(.conclusion)"' 2>/dev/null || true
echo "-- inline comments on head, by author --"
$GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/comments --paginate --jq "[.[]|select(.original_commit_id==\"$HEAD\" or .commit_id==\"$HEAD\")|.user.login]|group_by(.)|map(\"\(.[0]):\(length)\")|join(\" \")" 2>/dev/null

    $GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="FAILURE")|.name'

content.text:
#1081 rebased onto `c76eb602c` and pushed: `a40fcad53` → `19dbf224d`. Cycle running (CodeRabbit's slot has been free since ~18:52Z).

**The hazard was real and it landed exactly as predicted.** Worth recording what actually happened, because the shape is nastier than "two PRs conflict":

- The rebase stopped on `FileBrowser.tsx` — a *visible* conflict, twice (once per commit).
- `useFolderNavigation.ts` merged **silently** and produced two `folder` declarations and two return entries. Git reported nothing. Neither PR's CI could have caught it, because the duplicate only exists after the merge.
- Had I resolved only what git flagged and pushed, main would have broken on `TS2300`/`TS1117`.

The resolution turned out cleaner than expected: #1081's **second** commit had already converged on destructuring `folder` from `useFolderNavigation()` — the same design #1071 shipped. The two authors independently arrived at the same API. So I dropped #1081's redundant copy and kept main's, and `useFolderNavigation.ts` is now byte-identical to main.

The `FileBrowser.tsx` resolution is the one real judgment call: it composes both PRs rather than picking a side — `UploadPanel` mounted unconditionally with `folder={settled ? folder : null}` (#1071's fix for surviving folder changes), and `FileBrowserActions` replacing the direct `FileList` use (#1081's interaction layer). I dropped the old `(rows.length > 0 || !isRoot)` guard because #1081 deliberately removed it when `FileBrowserActions` took over rendering.

Verified locally rather than trusting CI: typecheck, eslint, tracker-refs, and the full web suite at 164 tests — both PRs' tests passing together.

One thing to watch when the verdicts come in: the reviewers will see `FileBrowser.tsx` as I resolved it, not as either author wrote it. If a finding lands there, it's likely aimed at my merge resolution rather than at #1081's work.

#!/bin/bash
# Re-review cycle that holds READY until BOTH CodeRabbit and macroscope land on the
# current head. review2.sh re-drafts as soon as CR touches its status comment, which
# can cut macroscope (READY-only, ~3-7min) off mid-run.
#   $1 = PR   $2 = earliest epoch to flip (optional, default now)
PR=$1; NOTBEFORE=${2:-0}
cd /Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box
GH="env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh"

HEAD=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR --jq '.head.sha')
echo "#$PR head=$HEAD"

# 1. CI must be settled: no failures, nothing pending except the reviewers' own contexts.
#    A just-pushed head has ZERO registered checks, which reads as "nothing pending" —
#    so a plausible check count is required before green is believed.
MINCHECKS=${MINCHECKS:-15}
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  sleep 20
  FAIL=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="FAILURE" or .conclusion=="TIMED_OUT")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  PEND=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion==null)|select((.name // .context)|test("CodeRabbit|Macroscope";"i")|not)]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  OK=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="SUCCESS")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  DONE=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion!=null)]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  echo "[$(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)] ci: success=$OK settled=$DONE pending=$PEND failed=$FAIL (need >=$MINCHECKS)"
  if [ -n "$FAIL" ] && [ "$FAIL" != "0" ]; then
    echo "CI FAILED on $HEAD - not flipping"
    $GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="FAILURE")|.name'
    exit 4
  fi
  if [ "$PEND" = "0" ] && [ -n "$PEND" ] && { [ -n "$DONE" ] && [ "$DONE" -ge "$MINCHECKS" ]; } 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "CI GREEN ($DONE checks settled)"; break
  fi
  sleep 40
done

# 2. Respect the CodeRabbit hourly reset.
NOW=$(date -u +%s)
if [ "$NOTBEFORE" -gt "$NOW" ]; then
  echo "waiting $((NOTBEFORE-NOW))s for the review slot"; sleep $((NOTBEFORE-NOW))
fi

BASE=""
for a in 1 2 3; do
  BASE=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // "none"' 2>/dev/null)
  [ -n "$BASE" ] && break
  echo "  baseline read failed (attempt $a) - retrying"; sleep 15
done
[ -n "$BASE" ] || { echo "CANNOT READ CR BASELINE - aborting before flipping"; exit 6; }
echo "baseline cr status-comment updated_at=$BASE"

# Flip must be CONFIRMED. A swallowed `gh pr ready` failure (network) leaves the PR
# a draft while the poll loop below waits out its full timeout on verdicts that can
# never arrive - which reads as "no findings" when nothing was ever reviewed.
FLIPPED=0
for a in 1 2 3 4 5; do
  $GH pr ready $PR >/dev/null 2>&1
  sleep 5
  D=$($GH pr view $PR --json isDraft --jq '.isDraft' 2>/dev/null)
  if [ "$D" = "false" ]; then FLIPPED=1; echo "FLIPPED READY $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"; break; fi
  echo "  flip attempt $a did not take (isDraft=[$D]) - retrying"
  sleep 20
done
[ "$FLIPPED" = "1" ] || { echo "COULD NOT FLIP #$PR READY - aborting. No review slot was consumed."; exit 5; }

# 3. Hold ready until BOTH verdicts are on THIS head, or 40m.
#    CR verdict  == a body-bearing review whose commit_id is the head.
#    macroscope  == its check-runs exist on the head and none are still in flight.
CR_DONE=0; MS_DONE=0
for i in $(seq 1 40); do
  sleep 60
  U_NOW=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // "none"')
  if [ "$CR_DONE" = "0" ]; then
    # gh api takes no --arg, so the head is interpolated into the filter.
    N=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/reviews --jq "[.[]|select(.user.login|test(\"coderabbit\";\"i\"))|select((.body|length)>0)|select(.commit_id==\"$HEAD\")]|length" 2>/dev/null)
    # A CLEAN verdict posts NO review — it only edits the status comment. Findings
    # come as a review body; both surfaces have to be polled.
    CLEAN=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|select(.body|test("No actionable comments";"i"))]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    if { [ -n "$N" ] && [ "$N" -gt 0 ]; } 2>/dev/null; then
      CR_DONE=1; echo "  CR VERDICT (findings) on head @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"
    elif { [ -n "$CLEAN" ] && [ "$CLEAN" -gt 0 ]; } 2>/dev/null && [ -n "$U_NOW" ] && [ "$U_NOW" != "$BASE" ]; then
      CR_DONE=1; echo "  CR VERDICT (clean, status comment) @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"
    fi
  fi
  if [ "$MS_DONE" = "0" ]; then
    MST=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '[.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    MSP=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '[.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))|select(.status!="completed")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    [ -n "$MST" ] && [ "$MST" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null && [ "$MSP" = "0" ] && { MS_DONE=1; echo "  MACROSCOPE COMPLETE on head @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"; }
  fi
  LIM=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|select(.body|test("Review limit reached";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // ""' 2>/dev/null)
  echo "  t+${i}m cr_done=$CR_DONE ms_done=$MS_DONE cr_comment_upd=$U_NOW ratelimit=[$LIM]"
  [ "$CR_DONE" = "1" ] && [ "$MS_DONE" = "1" ] && break
done

# Re-draft must be confirmed too: a PR left ready collects an unplanned review.
for a in 1 2 3 4; do
  $GH pr ready $PR --undo >/dev/null 2>&1
  sleep 5
  D=$($GH pr view $PR --json isDraft --jq '.isDraft' 2>/dev/null)
  [ "$D" = "true" ] && { echo "RE-DRAFTED $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"; break; }
  echo "  re-draft attempt $a did not take (isDraft=[$D]) - retrying"; sleep 15
  [ "$a" = "4" ] && echo "WARNING: #$PR MAY STILL BE READY - re-draft it by hand"
done

echo "=== RESULT on $HEAD ==="
echo "-- coderabbit verdict --"
$GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/reviews --jq ".[]|select(.user.login|test(\"coderabbit\";\"i\"))|select((.body|length)>0)|select(.commit_id==\"$HEAD\")|.body" 2>/dev/null | grep -m1 -iE "actionable comments posted|nitpick comments|no actionable comments" || echo "(no CR verdict on head)"
echo "-- macroscope check-runs --"
$GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))|"\(.name) | \(.status) | \(.conclusion)"' 2>/dev/null || true
echo "-- inline comments on head, by author --"
$GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/comments --paginate --jq "[.[]|select(.original_commit_id==\"$HEAD\" or .commit_id==\"$HEAD\")|.user.login]|group_by(.)|map(\"\(.[0]):\(length)\")|join(\" \")" 2>/dev/null
[ "$CR_DONE" = "1" ] && [ "$MS_DONE" = "1" ] && exit 0
echo "INCOMPLETE (cr=$CR_DONE ms=$MS_DONE)"; exit 2

=== v2: version concept in CONTEXT.md ===
10:- **Content key** — a random per-version key stored inline in the sealed read-body. Rotation re-wraps it for free via the metadata re-seal and never re-encrypts content bytes; the next version is fresh-keyed. There is no pending-re-key state.
33:- **Envelope** — the published plaintext wrapper of a node: format version, node id, epoch tag, the sealed bodies, and (at scope roots only) the grant section. Kind-uniform: whether a node is a file or a folder is sealed inside the read-body.
55:- **Op record** — one durable queue entry: `v ‖ ownerTag ‖ contentRootCid? ‖ sealed(op)`. The body seals HPKE-to-self; the header stays clear so a version routes before an open, ownership routes before decryption, and orphan GC expands a staged root keylessly. The clear-header framing is frozen across format versions.
57:- **Retained record** — a durable queue entry this session holds but does not act on: another identity's, one written at a format version this build does not implement, or one whose seal opened but whose intent body is a grammar this build does not implement. Never replayed, never surfaced as this account's, never removed, and its staged root still counts as referenced so orphan GC leaves its bytes alone. Only an _undecodable_ record — one that fails to decode at all — is dead-lettered and removed; retention is what stops a second account's login, a format bump, or a newer build's op from destroying an unpublished queue.

content.text:
Important finding before I file: **v2 has no version-history concept at all.** No `VersionEntry`, no restore/delete-version, nothing in the facade or snapshot. And the content model works against it — a fresh content key per version, with orphan GC reclaiming unreferenced roots, so prior versions aren't merely unsurfaced, they're collected.

So this isn't a UI port. It needs engine work first, then the web surface. Filing it that way.

input.command:
cd /Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box
S=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-myankelev-Code-random-cipher-box/8ed080ed-fffa-498c-9012-8e777bd9ef50/scratchpad
cat > $S/i4.md <<'EOF'
Version history is v2 scope, but **v2 currently has no version concept to surface**. There is no `VersionEntry`, no `restore`/`delete` version command, and no prior-version field anywhere in `crates/engine`, `crates/core`, or `packages/client`. This issue is the engine half; the web surface is tracked separately.

## Why this is not a port

v1 kept a `VersionEntry[]` per file and let the UI download, restore, or delete a past version. v2's content model actively works against that as built:

- Each version is **fresh-keyed** — the content key is random per version and stored inline in that version's sealed read-body (`CONTEXT.md`). A prior version therefore remains openable only while its own read-body is retained.
- **Orphan GC** reclaims staged roots nothing references. A superseded content root has no referent once the node advances, so prior versions are not merely unsurfaced — they are collectable.

So retaining history is a retention and reference-counting decision in the engine, not a rendering gap.

## Scope

- Decide and document the retention rule: how many prior versions a node keeps, and what makes their content roots referenced so orphan GC leaves them alone.
- Expose prior versions on the node in the snapshot — at minimum an identifier, a size, and a timestamp per entry.
- Facade commands to **download**, **restore**, and **delete** a specific prior version.
- Restore must go through the normal write path so it publishes as a new version rather than mutating history.
- Update `CONTEXT.md` with the term, and `blueprint/engine.md` with the retention rule and its interaction with orphan GC.

## Tests

- A superseded content root survives orphan GC while it is within the retention rule, and is collected once it falls outside it.
- Restoring a prior version publishes a new version whose content matches the restored one.
- Deleting a prior version makes it unresolvable and its bytes collectable.
- A version retained across a key-regression epoch still opens.
EOF
env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh issue create --repo FSM1/cipher-box --title "engine: retain prior file versions and expose restore and delete" --label v2-build --body-file $S/i4.md 2>&1 | tail -1

content.text:
# Resolve PR Review Comments

Resolve all open review comments on the current PR from any automated reviewer (CodeRabbit, GitHub Copilot, etc.) or human reviewers.

## Workflow

### 1. Identify the PR

```bash
PR_NUMBER=$(gh pr view --json number --jq '.number')
```

If no PR exists for the current branch, stop and inform the user.

### 2. Fetch all unresolved review threads

Use the GraphQL `reviewThreads` query to get threads with `isResolved` status:

```bash
REPO_OWNER=$(gh repo view --json owner --jq '.owner.login')
REPO_NAME=$(gh repo view --json name --jq '.name')

gh api graphql -f query="
{
  repository(owner: \"$REPO_OWNER\", name: \"$REPO_NAME\") {
    pullRequest(number: $PR_NUMBER) {
      reviewThreads(first: 100) {
        nodes {
          id
          isResolved
          comments(first: 10) {
            nodes {
              id
              author { login }
              body
              path
              line
              createdAt
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}"
```

Filter to only unresolved threads. If none, report "No unresolved review threads" and stop.

### 3. Triage each comment

For each unresolved thread, read the comment and the referenced code. Categorize as:

- **Valid fix needed** — the comment identifies a real bug, security issue, or meaningful improvement
- **Already addressed** — the issue was fixed in a later commit on this branch
- **Not applicable** — the suggestion doesn't apply (explain why)

### 4. Implement fixes

For all "valid fix needed" comments:

1. Read the referenced file and understand the context
2. Implement the fix
3. Track which thread the fix addresses

Do NOT:

- Make unrelated changes or refactors

---
name: project-macroscope-third-pr-reviewer
description: "macroscope is a THIRD PR reviewer on cipher-box — triggering is INCONSISTENT, not strictly ready-only; posts findings as inline comments from macroscopeapp[bot] with an EMPTY review body"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 80d330f6-bcef-42f9-92ad-b3f2dc8fe04e
  modified: 2026-08-05T14:20:03.771Z
---

`macroscope` was added as a PR review tool on FSM1/cipher-box on **2026-08-05**, joining
CodeRabbit and Greptile (Greptile quota resets mid-Aug 2026). Three reviewers now.

**Its triggering is INCONSISTENT — do not model it as strictly ready-only.** The user
disabled draft review on 2026-08-05, and it then skipped several draft heads. But on
**#1072 head `c806df6d5` (2026-08-05 14:05Z) all four agents ran on a PR that was in
draft** — pushed ~8 min after a re-draft. It then ran on *nothing* for the next head
`bc47da7d0`. Working hypothesis (unconfirmed): once a PR has been ready at least once, it
may review later pushes regardless of draft state, but not reliably. **Never infer coverage
from draft state — always query the head's check-runs** (`commits/<sha>/check-runs`,
filter `name|test("macroscope";"i")`) to see whether it actually ran.

`Macroscope - Correctness Check` skips far more often than the other three agents; a
`skipped` conclusion there is normal and is not a pass.

**Consequence for the draft convention.** Coverage is not guaranteed on a draft
([[feedback-keep-prs-draft-control-cr-timing]]) — CodeRabbit is genuinely ready-gated, so a
draft PR sitting with "no findings" still proves nothing. The flip to ready is the reliable
trigger for all three at once. When flipping to collect verdicts, **hold ready until each
reviewer has actually landed on the head**: on #1072 macroscope took ~4 min and CodeRabbit
~8.5 min after the flip, so a script that re-drafts on the first CodeRabbit status-comment
touch (~1 min) cuts both off. See `recycle-both.sh`.

**Where its output lands.** Author login is **`macroscopeapp[bot]`**. The review event
itself (`pulls/N/reviews`) is `COMMENTED` with an **empty body** — the findings are
inline `pulls/N/comments` entries. So a poller that reads only review *bodies* sees
nothing, the mirror of the CodeRabbit trap in
[[project-coderabbit-verdict-two-surfaces]]. Poll `pulls/N/comments` and filter on
`.user.login`.

**Finding format:** severity emoji + level (`🟠 **High**`), a `file:line` anchor, prose,
then a collapsible *"Reply 'fix it for me' or copy this AI Prompt"* block. Do **not** reply
"fix it for me" — a finding is a symptom report, not a spec (see
[[feedback-never-apply-review-suggestions-literally]]).

**Signal quality, first data point: good.** On #1066 it caught a genuine cross-section
contradiction in a docs-only diff — the `sweep` section was re-scoped to interior nodes
while an *unedited* section 170 lines away still listed the sweep among

## Running a review cycle

Use `~/.claude/projects/-Users-myankelev-Code-random-cipher-box/recycle-both.sh <PR> [notbefore-epoch]`. **`review2.sh` and `cycle.sh` are broken — do not use them.**

1. `gh api --jq --arg h "$HEAD"` — `gh api` takes no `--arg`. The filter errors, the count comes back empty, the verdict is never detected. Interpolate the value into the jq string instead.
2. Re-drafting on the first CodeRabbit status-comment touch (~1 min) cuts both bots off — macroscope needs ~4-7 min and CodeRabbit ~8.5 min after the flip. Hold ready until both actually land on the head.
3. A **clean** CodeRabbit verdict posts NO review at all — only an edit to its status comment. Polling review bodies alone hangs to timeout on a passing PR. Poll both surfaces and require the comment's `updated_at` to have moved past a pre-flip baseline.
4. "Nothing pending" is trivially true in the window before GitHub registers any check. Require a plausible settled-check count (this repo runs ~23) before believing green.

## Hard-won rules

- **Verify the COMMITTED tree, never the working tree.** A rebase resolution edited on disk but not committed passed every local gate and pushed the broken commit anyway. Use `git show HEAD:<path>`; require `git status --porcelain` empty *before and after* the gates.
- **Two PRs adding the same field to one interface merge CLEAN into a duplicate.** #1071 and #1081 both added `folder: Uint8Array | null` to `useFolderNavigation.ts` at different offsets: git stopped on `FileBrowser.tsx` (visible) but silently doubled the field (`TS2300` ×2, `TS1117`). `mergeable=CLEAN` proves nothing. Simulate with `git merge-file -p <ours> <base> <theirs>` and grep for a doubled declaration *before* the second PR merges. See [[project-semantic-merge-conflict-shape-change]].
- **Don't let a loose success check stand in for a read-back.** Reporting "parented"/"blocked_by" from a substring match on the API response was wrong in one direction and right in the other; only re-reading the authoritative list caught it. Same class as the six defects above.

The real blocker was that `web-e2e.yml` starts no Kubo, so `KuboPinStore.rpc()` 503s, the engine reads a non-413 as `Halt::Unclassified`, and the op retries forever instead of dead-lettering — a spec would *hang*, not fail. Tracked in #1096.
- CodeRabbit **withdrew** two findings on re-review after being pushed back on with mechanism evidence. Pushing back is worth it; see [[feedback-never-apply-review-suggestions-literally]].
- Resolve agents share the primary checkout unless told otherwise — one left it on a feature branch. Brief them to work in a worktree created from `origin/<branch>` (not local HEAD) and to leave the primary tree on `main`.

content.content:
#981 OPEN [v2-build,comp:engine]
engine: bound and reclaim pinned read streams, and gate the media window against the frozen chunk size
---
## Problem

#948 pinned a content version for the life of a ranged read stream, which made the engine hold state a read never held before: a `LiveStream` per open handle, each pinning a `Version` (its live content key) and a `RootManifest` whose leaf-CID list is bounded only by the 4 MiB root cap. Three gaps were deliberately left out of that PR.

**1. `LiveStreams` has no admission control.** `LiveWrites` is bounded by `StagingLedger::admit` — a write handle costs budget. The read plane has no cap, no per-node dedupe, and no idle eviction, so an open-without-close bug (or a loop against `openContentStream`) grows the worker's heap without limit and extends content-key residency indefinitely. A cap in the low hundreds is far above any legitimate media workload; past it, refuse rather than evict silently.

**2. A dead Service Worker port strands its cursor and its pin.** `MediaBroker.drop` is the only path that closes an engine stream, and it fires on `cb:media:close`, body end, read error, a superseding open, or `broker.close()`. When the SW's pull times out or the worker is killed, `MediaPipe.detachPort` closes its half of the `MessageChannel` and tells its own sinks — the tab-side broker never hears. `MessagePort` has no reliable close event, so the cursor and its pinned stream survive until the tab re-brokers or disposes. Options: have `detachPort` post a final `cb:media:close` for every sink bound to the dying port, and/or arm a per-cursor idle timer longer than the SW pull timeout.

**3. `MEDIA_WINDOW_BYTES` mirrors a Rust constant with no parity gate.** `packages/client/src/media/protocol.ts` hardcodes `1_048_536` to match `ContentProfile::PRODUCTION.chunk_size`. Nothing ties them: if the frozen framing ever moves, every media window straddles two leaves again — a silent 2x fetch amplification with no suite going red. Correctness is unaffected (the reader derives geometry from the manifest), so this is a drift guard, not a bug. Either surface the chunk size across the wasm seam and assert the pairing in the browser suite, or assert it in a KAT.

## Scope

Engine-side cap plus its refusal verdict, the broker/pipe reclamation path, and the constant binding. Each wants its own test: the N+1'th open refused without disturbing live handles; a cursor dropped when its port dies mid-body; the TS window equal to the engine's production chunk size.

Part of #655

**Wave 4 is DONE.** All six PRs merged 2026-08-05 in the planned order — #1072 (`e373a8955`) → #1070 (`04d84c9df`) → #1082 (`21b124db7`) → #1071 (`c76eb602c`) → #1081 (`dca953f71`) → #1078 (`3d087d673`). The 900-line `../wave-plan.md` is now history, not a worklist.

## Running a review cycle

Use `~/.claude/projects/-Users-myankelev-Code-random-cipher-box/recycle-both.sh <PR> [notbefore-epoch]`. **`review2.sh` and `cycle.sh` are broken — do not use them.**

Rebase every PR onto current `main` before its cycle, and re-verify locally; CI otherwise runs against a base that no longer exists.

**Six defect classes, all found in this machinery in one session, every one failing toward a false all-clear.** Any cycle log predating 2026-08-05 may be reporting "no findings" when nothing was reviewed:

1. `gh api --jq --arg h "$HEAD"` — `gh api` takes no `--arg`. The filter errors, the count comes back empty, the verdict is never detected. Interpolate the value into the jq string instead.
2. Re-drafting on the first CodeRabbit status-comment touch (~1 min) cuts both bots off — macroscope needs ~4-7 min and CodeRabbit ~8.5 min after the flip. Hold ready until both actually land on the head.
3. A **clean** CodeRabbit verdict posts NO review at all — only an edit to its status comment. Polling review bodies alone hangs to timeout on a passing PR. Poll both surfaces and require the comment's `updated_at` to have moved past a pre-flip baseline.
4. "Nothing pending" is trivially true in the window before GitHub registers any check. Require a plausible settled-check count (this repo runs ~23) before believing green.
5. `$GH pr ready $PR >/dev/null && echo FLIPPED` swallows a network failure, then polls a still-draft PR for its full timeout. **Confirm the flip by re-reading `isDraft`, and retry.** Same for the re-draft.
6. A timed-out head fetch yields `HEAD=""`, which silently matches nothing everywhere downstream. Retry and validate 40-hex before proceeding.

**The CodeRabbit fence:** 1/hr org-wide, measured from the last CR review's `submitted_at`. Compute it only from GitHub timestamps — `date -u -j -f "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ" "<submitted_at>" +%s` + 3600 + 90. **Never read a local test runner's clock**: vitest prints `Start at HH:MM:SS` in *local* time, and taking it as UTC once burned a cycle on a rate-limit notice.

## Hard-won rules

- **Verify the COMMITTED tree, never the working tree.** A rebase resolution edited on disk but not committed passed every local gate and pushed the broken commit anyway. Use `git show HEAD:<path>`; require `git status --porcelain` empty *before and after* the gates.
- **Two PRs adding the same field to one interface merge CLEAN into a duplicate.** #1071 and #1081 both added `folder: Uint8Array | null` to `useFolderNavigation.ts` at different offsets: git stopped on `FileBrowser.tsx` (visible) but silently doubled the field (`TS2300` ×2, `TS1117`). `mergeable=CLEAN` proves nothing. Simulate with `git merge-file -p <ours> <base> <theirs>` and grep for a doubled declaration *before* the second PR merges. See [[project-semantic-merge-conflict-shape-change]].
- **Don't let a loose success check stand in for a read-back.** Reporting "parented"/"blocked_by" from a substring match on the API response was wrong in one direction and right in the other; only re-reading the authoritative list caught it. Same class as the six defects above.
- **A reviewer's premise can be wrong, not just its fix.** Three findings on #1078 assumed no upload UI existed; it does. **Issues filed this session:** #1091 (selection model), #1092 (text editor dialog), #1093 (current-version details panel), #1094 (engine: retain prior versions) / #1095 (web: version history), #1096 (e2e write-path coverage), #1097 (killed-SW cursor reclamation). All `v2-build`, parented, edged.

## Running a review cycle

Use `~/.claude/projects/-Users-myankelev-Code-random-cipher-box/recycle-both.sh <PR> [notbefore-epoch]`. **`review2.sh` and `cycle.sh` are broken — do not use them.**

Rebase every PR onto current `main` before its cycle, and re-verify locally; CI otherwise runs against a base that no longer exists.

**Six defect classes, all found in this machinery in one session, every one failing toward a false all-clear.** Any cycle log predating 2026-08-05 may be reporting "no findings" when nothing was reviewed:

1. `gh api --jq --arg h "$HEAD"` — `gh api` takes no `--arg`. The filter errors, the count comes back empty, the verdict is never detected. Interpolate the value into the jq string instead.
2. Re-drafting on the first CodeRabbit status-comment touch (~1 min) cuts both bots off — macroscope needs ~4-7 min and CodeRabbit ~8.5 min after the flip. Hold ready until both actually land on the head.
3. A **clean** CodeRabbit verdict posts NO review at all — only an edit to its status comment. Polling review bodies alone hangs to timeout on a passing PR. Poll both surfaces and require the comment's `updated_at` to have moved past a pre-flip baseline.
4. "Nothing pending" is trivially true in the window before GitHub registers any check. Require a plausible settled-check count (this repo runs ~23) before believing green.
5. `$GH pr ready $PR >/dev/null && echo FLIPPED` swallows a network failure, then polls a still-draft PR for its full timeout. **Confirm the flip by re-reading `isDraft`, and retry.** Same for the re-draft.
6. A timed-out head fetch yields `HEAD=""`, which silently matches nothing everywhere downstream. Retry and validate 40-hex before proceeding.

**The CodeRabbit fence:** 1/hr org-wide, measured from the last CR review's `submitted_at`. Compute it only from GitHub timestamps — `date -u -j -f "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ" "<submitted_at>" +%s` + 3600 + 90. **Never read a local test runner's clock**: vitest prints `Start at HH:MM:SS` in *local* time, and taking it as UTC once burned a cycle on a rate-limit notice.

## Hard-won rules

- **Verify the COMMITTED tree, never the working tree.** A rebase resolution edited on disk but not committed passed every local gate and pushed the broken commit anyway. Use `git show HEAD:<path>`; require `git status --porcelain` empty *before and after* the gates.
- **Two PRs adding the same field to one interface merge CLEAN into a duplicate.** #1071 and #1081 both added `folder: Uint8Array | null` to `useFolderNavigation.ts` at different offsets: git stopped on `FileBrowser.tsx` (visible) but silently doubled the field (`TS2300` ×2, `TS1117`). `mergeable=CLEAN` proves nothing. Simulate with `git merge-file -p <ours> <base> <theirs>` and grep for a doubled declaration *before* the second PR merges. See [[project-semantic-merge-conflict-shape-change]].
- **Don't let a loose success check stand in for a read-back.** Reporting "parented"/"blocked_by" from a substring match on the API response was wrong in one direction and right in the other; only re-reading the authoritative list caught it. Same class as the six defects above.
- **A reviewer's premise can be wrong, not just its fix.** Three findings on #1078 assumed no upload UI existed; it does. The real blocker was that `web-e2e.yml` starts no Kubo, so `KuboPinStore.rpc()` 503s, the engine reads a non-413 as `Halt::Unclassified`, and the op retries forever instead of dead-lettering — a spec would *hang*, not fail. Tracked in #1096.
- CodeRabbit **withdrew** two findings on re-review after being pushed back on with mechanism evidence. Pushing back is worth it; see [[feedback-never-apply-review-suggestions-literally]].
- Resolve agents share the primary checkout unless told otherwise — one left it on a feature branch. Brief them to work in a worktree created from `origin/<branch>` (not local HEAD) and to leave the primary tree on `main`.
