name: project-desktop-build-matrix-context-deadlock
description: Requiring per-OS Desktop Build matrix contexts deadlocks pure-TS PRs; require the always-reporting gate instead
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 20e1deea-bb7c-455a-86e2-ae969afb36d2
  modified: 2026-08-05T21:33:49.801Z
---

The `desktop-build` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is a path-filtered matrix (`os: [ubuntu, macos, windows]`, `if: needs.changes.outputs.desktop == 'true'`; the `desktop` filter = `apps/desktop/**`, `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `rust-toolchain.toml`, `.cargo/config.toml`, `ci.yml`). GitHub reports the per-OS contexts `Desktop Build (macos-latest)` / `(ubuntu-latest)` / `(windows-latest)` **only when the matrix actually runs**. A pure-TS PR (e.g. `apps/api` only, no Cargo change) skips the matrix, so those contexts are **never reported** — and if they're registered as required branch-protection checks, the PR sits at `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` forever (`mergeable=MERGEABLE` but blocked). Rust PRs escape it because they touch `Cargo.lock` → `desktop=true` → matrix runs.

**Fix (PR #669):** a `desktop-build-result` gate job — `needs: desktop-build`, `if: always()` — that runs on every PR and passes when the matrix succeeded OR was skipped, failing only on real failure/cancellation. Branch protection requires the single stable `Desktop Build Result` context **instead of** the three matrix legs. Keeps desktop merge-blocking (`blueprint/testing.md` law 1) without the deadlock.

**Why:** I registered the three matrix-leg names as required after #660 merged; #668 (api mailbox) was the first pure-TS PR to hit the deadlock. Skipped path-filtered *non-matrix* jobs report a single skipped context (counts as pass) — but a skipped *matrix* job never emits per-leg contexts at all.

**How to apply:** Never require a per-OS matrix-leg context for a conditionally-skipped matrix job — require an `if: always()` summary/gate job's stable context. Same trap applies to any future path-filtered matrix (web-e2e, etc.). Related: [[feedback-ci-release-work-uses-chore-ci]], [[project-ci-excludes-web-unit-tests]].

**The gate's known blind spot — a skipped job passes it VACUOUSLY (verified 2026-08-05).** These `*-result` gates fail only when the guarded job's result is `failure` or `cancelled`; `skipped` passes, which is exactly what makes them work. But the guarded job carries `needs: [changes, lint]` and `if: !failure() && !cancelled() && <path filter>`, so **if `Detect Changes` itself fails, the job skips and the Result gate reports green having verified nothing.** `Detect Changes` is NOT a required context, so nothing blocks that merge. Confirmed on `ci.yml` for both `web-e2e`/`web-e2e-result` (~lines 857-887) and `desktop-build`/`desktop-build-result` (~lines 955-971) — byte-identical shape, so this already applies to the required `Desktop Build Result` today. **Require `Detect Changes` too**, or the whole result-gate pattern is only as trustworthy as an unguarded job.

**Required contexts as of 2026-08-05 (20):** Lint, Typecheck, Test, Build, Web Bundle, API Unit, API Integration (real Postgres), Migration Drift, OpenAPI Freshness, Cargo Check & Test ×3 (Linux/macOS/Windows), Engine Tests, Core KATs (native + WASM), Client Browser Suite, Contract Suite Result, Desktop Build Result, lint-pr-title, zizmor static audit, Tracker Refs. **Missing and needed: `Web E2E Smoke Result`** (landed with #1078, so the smoke slice currently blocks nothing) **and `Detect Changes`.**

**Sibling deadlock — newly-required gate vs pre-existing open PRs (2026-07-20):** even a correct always-reporting gate only reports on branches whose `ci.yml` CONTAINS its job. Registering a brand-new required check (`Contract Suite Result`, added by #671) blocked every already-open PR that forked BEFORE that job landed (#670, #675 — pre-#671 base) — the job doesn't exist on their branch, so the required context sits `expected` → `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` forever. Fix: merge `origin/main` into each straggler branch (user prefers MERGE, no rebase/force-push) so the job enters their `ci.yml` and reports. So: only require a gate once all open PRs already carry it, OR immediately merge main into the stragglers right after you register it.

name: project-macroscope-third-pr-reviewer
description: "macroscope is a THIRD PR reviewer on cipher-box — triggering is INCONSISTENT, not strictly ready-only; posts findings as inline comments from macroscopeapp[bot] with an EMPTY review body"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 80d330f6-bcef-42f9-92ad-b3f2dc8fe04e
  modified: 2026-08-05T21:30:52.870Z
---

`macroscope` was added as a PR review tool on FSM1/cipher-box on **2026-08-05**, joining
CodeRabbit and Greptile (Greptile quota resets mid-Aug 2026). Three reviewers now.

**Its triggering is INCONSISTENT — do not model it as strictly ready-only.** The user
disabled draft review on 2026-08-05, and it then skipped several draft heads. But on
**#1072 head `c806df6d5` (2026-08-05 14:05Z) all four agents ran on a PR that was in
draft** — pushed ~8 min after a re-draft. It then ran on *nothing* for the next head
`bc47da7d0`. Working hypothesis (unconfirmed): once a PR has been ready at least once, it
may review later pushes regardless of draft state, but not reliably. **Never infer coverage
from draft state — always query the head's check-runs** (`commits/<sha>/check-runs`,
filter `name|test("macroscope";"i")`) to see whether it actually ran.

`Macroscope - Correctness Check` skips far more often than the other three agents; a
`skipped` conclusion there is normal and is not a pass.

**A `success` conclusion does NOT mean that agent posted no findings.** On #1078,
`Language idioms` reported `success` while still having an inline thread open. Its
conclusions describe the agent's run, not the review outcome — always enumerate
`reviewThreads`, and **re-query before concluding you have them all**: a first GraphQL
query returned 3 threads where a second returned 4.

**`Ticket Requirements` verdict grammar.** `neutral` is NOT synonymous with a spec
mismatch — across one wave it meant a real deviation once, a benign harvest-list note
twice, and an unchanged previously-reported item once. Always read the check-run's
`output` field and compare against the previous run; it re-scopes between heads (one PR
went "3 harvest items" → "1 unimplemented item" with no code change). It also declines to
re-post an unchanged finding, saying so explicitly.

**Consequence for the draft convention.** Coverage is not guaranteed on a draft
([[feedback-keep-prs-draft-control-cr-timing]]) — CodeRabbit is genuinely ready-gated, so a
draft PR sitting with "no findings" still proves nothing. The flip to ready is the reliable
trigger for all three at once. When flipping to collect verdicts, **hold ready until each
reviewer has actually landed on the head**: on #1072 macroscope took ~4 min and CodeRabbit
~8.5 min after the flip, so a script that re-drafts on the first CodeRabbit status-comment
touch (~1 min) cuts both off. See `recycle-both.sh`.

**Where its output lands.** Author login is **`macroscopeapp[bot]`**. The review event
itself (`pulls/N/reviews`) is `COMMENTED` with an **empty body** — the findings are
inline `pulls/N/comments` entries. So a poller that reads only review *bodies* sees
nothing, the mirror of the CodeRabbit trap in
[[project-coderabbit-verdict-two-surfaces]]. Poll `pulls/N/comments` and filter on
`.user.login`.

**Finding format:** severity emoji + level (`🟠 **High**`), a `file:line` anchor, prose,
then a collapsible *"Reply 'fix it for me' or copy this AI Prompt"* block. Do **not** reply
"fix it for me" — a finding is a symptom report, not a spec (see
[[feedback-never-apply-review-suggestions-literally]]).

**Signal quality, first data point: good.** On #1066 it caught a genuine cross-section
contradiction in a docs-only diff — the `sweep` section was re-scoped to interior nodes
while an *unedited* section 170 lines away still listed the sweep among
`reseal_scope_root`'s callers. It reasons across the whole file, not just the diff hunk,
which is exactly the class CodeRabbit's diff-scoped review misses.

**How to apply:** after flipping a PR ready, poll `pulls/N/comments` for
`macroscopeapp[bot]` alongside the CodeRabbit surfaces. When a finding names an unchanged
section, verify the contradiction against the file before editing — and prefer correcting
the stale section over relaxing the new one.

#!/bin/bash
# Re-review cycle that holds READY until BOTH CodeRabbit and macroscope land on the
# current head. review2.sh re-drafts as soon as CR touches its status comment, which
# can cut macroscope (READY-only, ~3-7min) off mid-run.
#   $1 = PR   $2 = earliest epoch to flip (optional, default now)
PR=$1; NOTBEFORE=${2:-0}
cd /Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box
GH="env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh"

# The head is the key every later check keys on, so a transient failure here must
# abort rather than proceed with an empty string that silently matches nothing.
HEAD=""
for a in 1 2 3 4 5; do
  HEAD=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR --jq '.head.sha' 2>/dev/null)
  case "$HEAD" in [0-9a-f]*) [ ${#HEAD} -eq 40 ] && break ;; esac
  HEAD=""; echo "  head read failed (attempt $a) - retrying"; sleep 15
done
[ -n "$HEAD" ] || { echo "CANNOT READ HEAD FOR #$PR - aborting, nothing flipped."; exit 7; }
echo "#$PR head=$HEAD"

# 1. CI must be settled: no failures, nothing pending except the reviewers' own contexts.
#    A just-pushed head has ZERO registered checks, which reads as "nothing pending" —
#    so a plausible check count is required before green is believed.
MINCHECKS=${MINCHECKS:-15}
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  sleep 20
  FAIL=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="FAILURE" or .conclusion=="TIMED_OUT")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  PEND=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion==null)|select((.name // .context)|test("CodeRabbit|Macroscope";"i")|not)]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  OK=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="SUCCESS")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  DONE=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion!=null)]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  echo "[$(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)] ci: success=$OK settled=$DONE pending=$PEND failed=$FAIL (need >=$MINCHECKS)"
  if [ -n "$FAIL" ] && [ "$FAIL" != "0" ]; then
    echo "CI FAILED on $HEAD - not flipping"
    $GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="FAILURE")|.name'
    exit 4
  fi
  if [ "$PEND" = "0" ] && [ -n "$PEND" ] && { [ -n "$DONE" ] && [ "$DONE" -ge "$MINCHECKS" ]; } 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "CI GREEN ($DONE checks settled)"; break
  fi
  sleep 40
done

# 2. Respect the CodeRabbit hourly reset.
NOW=$(date -u +%s)
if [ "$NOTBEFORE" -gt "$NOW" ]; then
  echo "waiting $((NOTBEFORE-NOW))s for the review slot"; sleep $((NOTBEFORE-NOW))
fi

BASE=""
for a in 1 2 3; do
  BASE=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // "none"' 2>/dev/null)
  [ -n "$BASE" ] && break
  echo "  baseline read failed (attempt $a) - retrying"; sleep 15
done
[ -n "$BASE" ] || { echo "CANNOT READ CR BASELINE - aborting before flipping"; exit 6; }
echo "baseline cr status-comment updated_at=$BASE"

# Flip must be CONFIRMED. A swallowed `gh pr ready` failure (network) leaves the PR
# a draft while the poll loop below waits out its full timeout on verdicts that can
# never arrive - which reads as "no findings" when nothing was ever reviewed.
FLIPPED=0
for a in 1 2 3 4 5; do
  $GH pr ready $PR >/dev/null 2>&1
  sleep 5
  D=$($GH pr view $PR --json isDraft --jq '.isDraft' 2>/dev/null)
  if [ "$D" = "false" ]; then FLIPPED=1; echo "FLIPPED READY $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"; break; fi
  echo "  flip attempt $a did not take (isDraft=[$D]) - retrying"
  sleep 20
done
[ "$FLIPPED" = "1" ] || { echo "COULD NOT FLIP #$PR READY - aborting. No review slot was consumed."; exit 5; }

# 3. Hold ready until BOTH verdicts are on THIS head, or 40m.
#    CR verdict  == a body-bearing review whose commit_id is the head.
#    macroscope  == its check-runs exist on the head and none are still in flight.
CR_DONE=0; MS_DONE=0
for i in $(seq 1 40); do
  sleep 60
  U_NOW=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // "none"')
  if [ "$CR_DONE" = "0" ]; then
    # gh api takes no --arg, so the head is interpolated into the filter.
    N=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/reviews --jq "[.[]|select(.user.login|test(\"coderabbit\";\"i\"))|select((.body|length)>0)|select(.commit_id==\"$HEAD\")]|length" 2>/dev/null)
    # A CLEAN verdict posts NO review — it only edits the status comment. Findings
    # come as a review body; both surfaces have to be polled.
    CLEAN=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|select(.body|test("No actionable comments";"i"))]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    if { [ -n "$N" ] && [ "$N" -gt 0 ]; } 2>/dev/null; then
      CR_DONE=1; echo "  CR VERDICT (findings) on head @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"
    elif { [ -n "$CLEAN" ] && [ "$CLEAN" -gt 0 ]; } 2>/dev/null && [ -n "$U_NOW" ] && [ "$U_NOW" != "$BASE" ]; then
      CR_DONE=1; echo "  CR VERDICT (clean, status comment) @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"
    fi
  fi
  if [ "$MS_DONE" = "0" ]; then
    MST=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '[.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    MSP=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '[.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))|select(.status!="completed")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    [ -n "$MST" ] && [ "$MST" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null && [ "$MSP" = "0" ] && { MS_DONE=1; echo "  MACROSCOPE COMPLETE on head @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"; }
  fi
  LIM=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|select(.body|test("Review limit reached";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // ""' 2>/dev/null)
  echo "  t+${i}m cr_done=$CR_DONE ms_done=$MS_DONE cr_comment_upd=$U_NOW ratelimit=[$LIM]"
  [ "$CR_DONE" = "1" ] && [ "$MS_DONE" = "1" ] && break
done

# Re-draft must be confirmed too: a PR left ready collects an unplanned review.
for a in 1 2 3 4; do
  $GH pr ready $PR --undo >/dev/null 2>&1
  sleep 5
  D=$($GH pr view $PR --json isDraft --jq '.isDraft' 2>/dev/null)
  [ "$D" = "true" ] && { echo "RE-DRAFTED $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"; break; }
  echo "  re-draft attempt $a did not take (isDraft=[$D]) - retrying"; sleep 15
  [ "$a" = "4" ] && echo "WARNING: #$PR MAY STILL BE READY - re-draft it by hand"
done

echo "=== RESULT on $HEAD ==="
echo "-- coderabbit verdict --"
$GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/reviews --jq ".[]|select(.user.login|test(\"coderabbit\";\"i\"))|select((.body|length)>0)|select(.commit_id==\"$HEAD\")|.body" 2>/dev/null | grep -m1 -iE "actionable comments posted|nitpick comments|no actionable comments" || echo "(no CR verdict on head)"
echo "-- macroscope check-runs --"
$GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))|"\(.name) | \(.status) | \(.conclusion)"' 2>/dev/null || true
echo "-- inline comments on head, by author --"
$GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/comments --paginate --jq "[.[]|select(.original_commit_id==\"$HEAD\" or .commit_id==\"$HEAD\")|.user.login]|group_by(.)|map(\"\(.[0]):\(length)\")|join(\" \")" 2>/dev/null
[ "$CR_DONE" = "1" ] && [ "$MS_DONE" = "1" ] && exit 0
echo "INCOMPLETE (cr=$CR_DONE ms=$MS_DONE)"; exit 2

#!/bin/bash
# Re-review-safe cycle that WAITS for CI instead of refusing.
#   $1 = PR   $2 = earliest epoch to flip (CodeRabbit reset)
PR=$1; NOTBEFORE=$2
cd /Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box
GH="env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh"

HEAD=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR --jq '.head.sha')
echo "#$PR head=$HEAD"

# 1. Wait for CI: no failures, nothing pending except the reviewer's own context.
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  FAIL=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="FAILURE" or .conclusion=="TIMED_OUT")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  PEND=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion==null)|select((.name // .context)|test("CodeRabbit";"i")|not)]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  OK=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="SUCCESS")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  echo "[$(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)] ci: success=$OK pending=$PEND failed=$FAIL"
  if [ "$FAIL" != "0" ] && [ -n "$FAIL" ]; then
    echo "CI FAILED on $HEAD — not flipping"; $GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="FAILURE")|.name'; exit 4
  fi
  [ "$PEND" = "0" ] && [ -n "$PEND" ] && [ "$OK" != "0" ] && { echo "CI GREEN"; break; }
  sleep 60
done

# 2. Respect the reviewer's reset.
NOW=$(date -u +%s)
if [ "$NOTBEFORE" -gt "$NOW" ]; then echo "waiting $((NOTBEFORE-NOW))s for the review slot"; sleep $((NOTBEFORE-NOW)); fi

BASE=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // "none"')
echo "baseline cr updated_at=$BASE"

$GH pr ready $PR >/dev/null && echo "FLIPPED READY $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"

# 3. Run started == that in-place-edited status comment is touched again.
for i in $(seq 1 8); do
  sleep 60
  U=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // "none"')
  echo "  t+${i}m cr updated_at=$U"
  [ "$U" != "$BASE" ] && { echo "  run started (or rate-limit notice refreshed)"; break; }
done
$GH pr ready $PR --undo >/dev/null && echo "RE-DRAFTED $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"

# 4. Verdict must be a body-bearing review ON THIS HEAD. Also surface a rate-limit notice.
for i in $(seq 1 45); do
  N=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/reviews --jq --arg h "$HEAD" '[.[]|select((.body|length)>0)|select(.commit_id==$h)]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  LIM=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|select(.body|test("Review limit reached"))|.updated_at]|max // ""' 2>/dev/null)
  M=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/comments --jq --arg h "$HEAD" '[.[]|select(.original_commit_id==$h or .commit_id==$h)|.user.login]|group_by(.)|map("\(.[0]):\(length)")|join(" ")' 2>/dev/null)
  echo "  poll t+${i}m reviews_on_head=$N inline_on_head=[$M] ratelimit_notice=[$LIM]"
  if [ -n "$N" ] && [ "$N" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "=== VERDICT ON $HEAD @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ) ==="
    $GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/reviews --jq --arg h "$HEAD" '.[]|select((.body|length)>0)|select(.commit_id==$h)|.body' | grep -m1 -i "actionable comments posted"
    echo "inline: $M"; exit 0
  fi
  sleep 60
done
echo "TIMEOUT on $HEAD"; exit 2

skills.name: resolve-pr-reviews
skills.content:
# Resolve PR Review Comments

Resolve all open review comments on the current PR from any automated reviewer (CodeRabbit, GitHub Copilot, etc.) or human reviewers.

## Workflow

### 1. Identify the PR

```bash
PR_NUMBER=$(gh pr view --json number --jq '.number')
```

If no PR exists for the current branch, stop and inform the user.

### 2. Fetch all unresolved review threads

Use the GraphQL `reviewThreads` query to get threads with `isResolved` status:

```bash
REPO_OWNER=$(gh repo view --json owner --jq '.owner.login')
REPO_NAME=$(gh repo view --json name --jq '.name')

gh api graphql -f query="
{
  repository(owner: \"$REPO_OWNER\", name: \"$REPO_NAME\") {
    pullRequest(number: $PR_NUMBER) {
      reviewThreads(first: 100) {
        nodes {
          id
          isResolved
          comments(first: 10) {
            nodes {
              id
              author { login }
              body
              path
              line
              createdAt
            }
          }
        }
```

### 3. Triage each comment

For each unresolved thread, read the comment and the referenced code. Categorize as:

- **Valid fix needed** — the comment identifies a real bug, security issue, or meaningful improvement
- **Already addressed** — the issue was fixed in a later commit on this branch
- **Not applicable** — the suggestion doesn't apply (explain why)

### 4. Implement fixes

For all "valid fix needed" comments:

1. Read the referenced file and understand the context
2. Implement the fix
3. Track which thread the fix addresses

Do NOT:

- Make unrelated changes or refactors
- Add features beyond what the comment requests
- Increase timeouts or add retries as a first approach — fix root causes

### 5. Run tests locally

After ALL fixes are implemented:

```bash
# Type check
pnpm typecheck

# Run relevant unit tests
pnpm test

# If E2E-relevant changes were made, run E2E tests too
cd tests/web-e2e && pnpm exec playwright test
```

Do NOT proceed to commit until tests pass. If tests fail, fix the failures first.

### 6. Commit and push

```bash
git add <specific-files>
git commit -m "fix: address PR review comments"
git push
```

### 7. Reply to and resolve each thread

For each thread, reply explaining what was done, then resolve:

- **Fixed comments**: Reply with what was changed and where, then resolve
- **Already addressed**: Reply explaining which commit addressed it, then resolve
- **Not applicable**: Reply with clear reasoning for not making changes, then resolve

Reply via REST (use `--field` not `-f` for `in_reply_to` — must be integer):

```bash

  --field in_reply_to=COMMENT_ID \
  --raw-field body='...'
```

Resolve via GraphQL (can batch multiple):

```bash

mutation {
  resolveReviewThread(input: {threadId: "THREAD_ID"}) {
    thread { isResolved }
  }
}'
```

### 8. Report summary

Print a summary table:

- Thread count resolved
- Fixes made (with file:line references)
- Comments marked as already addressed or not applicable

### Applying a review suggestion literally made things WORSE — twice

Both times a sub-agent caught it only because it re-ran the review gates on its own fix:

1. **#1049 finding 2.** CodeRabbit asked for `Err` on a history-link chain that will not walk. That
   is a **denial-of-revocation vector**: the gate authenticates each link's signature but nothing
   about their order, so a committed write-grantee publishes an adopted root with reordered links
   and the owner's revocation rotation then fails closed *permanently* — non-retryable on the
   cascade path, leaving a revocation half-applied. Resolution: **truncate to the walkable suffix**
   instead. Nothing unwalkable is published, fail-closed holds, attacker cannot block their own removal.
2. **#1046 finding 2.** CodeRabbit asked for durable in-doubt publish state. That only moves the
   window — any single durable write has a gap after the network ack.

**Rule: never hand a CodeRabbit suggestion straight to an agent as a spec.** Ask what the fix does
to the threat model, especially when the suggestion converts a tolerated input into a hard failure
on a path an adversary can reach.

### Two process lessons from this round

- **Poll BOTH surfaces for a CodeRabbit verdict.** #1046's verdict landed in the **review body**
  (`pulls/N/reviews[].body`), never in the status comment — a comment-only poll reported "still
  waiting" indefinitely. Also filter reviews to non-empty bodies: thread replies create `len=0`
  review events that look like reviews in a naive count.
- **`--no-verify` needs the claim checked, not assumed.** #1046's agent bypassed hooks reasoning
  "the diff is Rust-only"; it was not — `blueprint/engine.md` was in it with 4 real MD049
  violations main did not have. Note `lint:md` is a package script that **no CI workflow runs**, so
  CI would never have caught it.

the five-way merge is green — this order just minimizes rebase churn.

### Applying a review suggestion literally made things WORSE — twice

Both times a sub-agent caught it only because it re-ran the review gates on its own fix:

1. **#1049 finding 2.** CodeRabbit asked for `Err` on a history-link chain that will not walk. That
   is a **denial-of-revocation vector**: the gate authenticates each link's signature but nothing
   about their order, so a committed write-grantee publishes an adopted root with reordered links
   and the owner's revocation rotation then fails closed *permanently* — non-retryable on the
   cascade path, leaving a revocation half-applied. Resolution: **truncate to the walkable suffix**
   instead. Nothing unwalkable is published, fail-closed holds, attacker cannot block their own removal.
2. **#1046 finding 2.** CodeRabbit asked for durable in-doubt publish state. That only moves the
   window — any single durable write has a gap after the network ack.

**Rule: never hand a CodeRabbit suggestion straight to an agent as a spec.** Ask what the fix does
to the threat model, especially when the suggestion converts a tolerated input into a hard failure
on a path an adversary can reach.

### Two process lessons from this round

- **Poll BOTH surfaces for a CodeRabbit verdict.** #1046's verdict landed in the **review body**
  (`pulls/N/reviews[].body`), never in the status comment — a comment-only poll reported "still
  waiting" indefinitely. Also filter reviews to non-empty bodies: thread replies create `len=0`
  review events that look like reviews in a naive count.
- **`--no-verify` needs the claim checked, not assumed.** #1046's agent bypassed hooks reasoning
  "the diff is Rust-only"; it was not — `blueprint/engine.md` was in it with 4 real MD049
  violations main did not have. Note `lint:md` is a package script that **no CI workflow runs**, so
  CI would never have caught it.

4 and 5 are interchangeable and independent of 1-3. No code-level ordering constraint exists —
the five-way merge is green — this order just minimizes rebase churn.

Still held: **856** (unblocked since wave 1, wants the facade slot), **926** (cross-language seam shape — `desktop-seams` + `wasm` + `packages/client`), **1060/1043/1056** (all want the facade slot), **831** (needs an ADR first), the desktop track (**650** is the real blocker on 648→654 — `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs` is 107 lines with no engine bootstrap), and **653** staging cutover. ## Wave 4 — landed PRs and the merge hazard found | PR | Issues | State | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | **#1071** | 873 | draft, 19 green | +1381/-1, 11 files | | **#1070** | 1057, 1055 | draft, green | +236/-39, 3 files | | **#1081** | 806, 807 | draft, CI running | +2060/-8, 27 files | ### SILENT semantic merge conflict — #1071 x #1081 `git merge-tree` reports **one** conflict (`FileBrowser.tsx`, textual, safe — git flags it). But `useFolderNavigation.ts` **auto-merged without a conflict and is broken**: both PRs independently added the same `folder: Uint8Array | null` field at different offsets, so git took both additions. Verified by typechecking the merged file against the real project, not by reasoning: ```text src/vault/useFolderNavigation.ts(23,3): error TS2300: Duplicate identifier 'folder'. src/vault/useFolderNavigation.ts(27,3): error TS2300: Duplicate identifier 'folder'. src/vault/useFolderNavigation.ts(84,5): error TS1117: An object literal cannot have multiple properties with the same name. ``` **Neither PR's CI can catch this** — each is green alone. This is the `project-semantic-merge-conflict-shape-change` pattern again (#779/#782, #944/#946), and it is the *silent* variant: the file git flagged is the harmless one. **Resolution: merge #1071 first** (it introduces `folder`), then rebase #1081 and delete its duplicate declaration and its duplicate return-object line. Do not merge #1081 first — #1081 needs the field, so dropping its copy pre-merge would break #1081 standing alone. `main.tsx` merged cleanly — all nine CSS imports are distinct, no duplicate. ## WAVE 4 COMPLETE — six draft PRs, all CI green | PR | Issues | Files | Diff | CI | |---|---|---|---|---| | **#1072** | 871 | 16 | +1555/-93 | 24 green | | **#1071** | 873 | 11 | +1381/-1 | 19 green | | **#1070** | 1057, 1055 | 3 | +236/-39 | green | | **#1081** | 806, 807 | 27 | +2060/-8 | green | | **#1082** | 1052, 1038 | 12 | +721/-286 | green | | **#1078** | 809 | 26 | +805/-141 | 29 green | **Merge order: #1072 → #1070 → #1082 → #1071 → #1081 → #1078.** #1071 MUST precede #1081 (see the silent conflict above). The rest are file-disjoint. ### New CI gate from #1078 - `Web E2E Smoke` — the job. `Web E2E Smoke Result` — the stable always-reporting context, mirroring `Contract Suite Result`. **Add `Web E2E Smoke Result` to branch protection** (would be the 21st required context). Until then the suite runs but does not block. - Its `!failure() && !cancelled()` guard is fail-closed only if `Lint` and `Detect Changes` are also required — the same assumption `Contract Suite Result` already makes. - **Needs zero secrets and zero repo/environment vars.** `VITE_ENVIRONMENT=ci` names no deployment, so the bundle is exempt from the Web3Auth deploy-env gate. The job never sets `TEST_LOGIN_SECRET`, so the API's test-login bypass stays disabled. `secrets: inherit` was removed from the `web-e2e.yml` call sites in `tag-staging.yml` and `ci-e2e.yml` — verified scoped to those call sites only, and `web-e2e.yml` references no secret at all. - **`TEST_LOGIN_SECRET` is not needed for the web path** — `login_identity` creates the account implicitly at first challenge-signature login, so a fresh 32-byte secret per test IS a fresh vault. The blueprint's "per-test vault isolation via test-login" is a v1 carry-over. ### #981 — CLOSE as already delivered Verified independently by the #871 agent; nothing was added, so `Closes #981` is deliberately NOT in #1072. Evidence: cap at `facade.rs:1349-1375` with RAII release and a single insert path, test `opening_past_the_stream_ceiling_is_refused` (`tests/write_plane.rs:1005`); `detachPort` (`sw/pipe.ts:292-311`) posting `cb:media:close` per bound body before `port.close()`, tested at `pipe.test.ts:379` and `broker.test.ts:257`; `MEDIA_WINDOW_BYTES` parity via a two-hop read of `crates/engine/kat/manifest.json` (`protocol.test.ts:11-25`) pinned to `ContentProfile::PRODUCTION.chunk_size()` at `kat_content.rs:180`. ### Design call needing a second opinion — #1072 **External-only over PSA/Pinata is refused** (`NoExternalIngress`): with no hosted leg, nothing holds the block for the service to fetch. v1 papered over this by relaying through CipherBox then unpinning, which defeats the mode and leaked quota. Deliberate, and worth ratifying. ### Follow-ups filed this wave — 13, all linked, none orphaned | Issue | From | Home | |---|---|---| | 1069 | #1006's unbuilt web half | parent 642; blocks 1064 | | 1073 | over-budget cause flattened at the wasm boundary | parent 992 | | 1075 | `SnapshotDescriptor.blocked` unread in web | parent 642; blocked_by 1073 | | 1076 | authenticate the threaded ancestor seed | blocked_by 1057 | | 1077 | scope root outgrowing its own re-seal | blocked_by 1055 | | 1079 | snapshot store sole ownership of focus | blocked_by 806 | | 1080 | stream preview/download via MediaService | blocked_by 806 | | 1083 | authenticate the leadership rendezvous | parent 993; blocked_by 1052 | | 1084 | withheld settings places a fresh device | blocked_by 871 | | 1085 | placement frozen for the session vs revoked provider | blocked_by 871 | | 1086 | `Http` seam follows redirects, record transport does not | blocked_by 871 | | 1087 | route guard hangs when the session provider stalls | parent 642; blocked_by 809 | | 1088 | wasm built twice per run; host build tree uncached | parent 995; blocked_by 809 | #1074 was a double-file of #1073 (GitHub API retry) and is closed as a duplicate. ### Not filed, recorded here - Move `Plain` / the introspection contract into `packages/client` so `tests/web-e2e` stops path-mapping into `apps/web/src`. Blocked this wave — `packages/client` was another agent's. - The e2e cold start does not arm `LoginSecretSource`, so leader-failover secret re-export is unreachable from that seam. Relevant when the blueprint's leader-failover e2e lands. ### Review-gate note All six PRs ran `/simplify` + `/security-review`, and the three touching crypto/trust boundaries ran `/crypto-privacy-review`. Every agent folded real findings into a second commit. Two agents **correctly refused** a reviewer suggestion: #1070 declined to make `HeadTooLarge`/`Seal` fatal (denial-of-revocation vector — filed #1077 on the size axis instead), and #1072 identified a reviewer false positive about a silent drain-side placement refusal. ## Wave 4 review queue — 70-MINUTE cadence **User directive 2026-08-05: space consecutive ready-flips 70 minutes, not 60.** A flip at exactly +60m has repeatedly been too early — the PR sits ready, receives no review, and the slot is lost. Measure from the PREVIOUS VERDICT's landing time, not from "now" (spacing from "now" is what put wave-3's #1061 back inside the window). Order: **#1072 → #1070 → #1082 → #1071 → #1081 → #1078.** Per-PR sequence, from `project-draft-conversion-aborts-inflight-coderabbit-review`: `gh pr ready` → CR run starts (walkthrough comment appears, ~1m) → **re-draft immediately** → wait for the review to post → push fixes against the draft PR. Re-drafting does NOT cancel an in-flight review; it stops the fix-push triggering a SECOND review and burning the next slot. Poll BOTH surfaces: `pulls/N/reviews[]` filtered to non-empty bodies (the authoritative findings surface) AND the status comment for `Actionable comments posted: N`. CodeRabbit edits ONE status comment in place, so compare `created_at` vs `updated_at`. A walkthrough comment is NOT a review. macroscope posts findings INLINE with an EMPTY review body, so counting review bodies alone misses it entirely. ### #1072 — macroscope verdict: 5 findings (4 High, 1 Medium) | # | Site | Claim | Triage | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | `settings.rs:109` | `Placement::tag` hashes only `mode`+`endpoint`, omitting `ByoIpfsConfig::kind` and `access_token` — two configs on one endpoint collide | **REAL, High.** Defeats the tag's own purpose (it exists to stop a resumed version reading a prior session's progress). Fix must domain-separate and never log the token | | 2 | `content/provider.rs:232` | `kubo_stored_address` rejects a valid non-base32 multibase spelling; the doc claims decoded-byte compare | **REAL** doc/code mismatch. Either widen the decode or narrow the doc — do not assume the suggestion | | 3 | `facade.rs:2438` | `byo_reconciled` flips true before `set_byo` returns, result dropped; one transient PATCH failure wedges every hosted upload until restart | **REAL, High** | | 4 | `sync/drain.rs:643` | Quota check returns false on API error even when placement has no hosted leg, so an external placement blocks forever | **REAL, Medium.** `clear_block()` exists (`drain.rs:657`, used `:507`, `:640`, `:653`) so the suggested diff is plausible — still verify, never apply literally | | 5 | `sync/drain.rs:2272` | Pre-upgrade marks decode as zero progress → `CONTENT_LOST` | **FALSE POSITIVE** — backward-compatibility class. Only release is `v0.45.2` (v1); no `v2*` tag; staging cutover (#653) has not happened. No deployment holds a legacy mark | **Finding 5 found a real mechanism on an unreachable trigger.** `decode_upload_mark` (`drain.rs:2297`) returns 0 on ANY tag mismatch, and if leaves were already released from staging that path reaches `CONTENT_LOST`. Unreachable via upgrade — but reachable via a legitimate **mid-upload placement change**, which is finding 1's exact scenario. Findings 1 and 5 are the same defect from opposite ends: fixing 1 in isolation could convert a silent collision into a hard content loss. The resolver must treat them as one problem. ### Queue re-sequenced 2026-08-05 — #1072 takes a SECOND slot The #1072 fix round was **not cosmetic**: +1555/-93 became **+2169/-108**, and the delta redesigned the upload-mark semantics (single placement tag replaced by a destination *set*, with a new resume rule). Both bot reviews are on the pre-fix head `45c25194f`; every review entry against the new head `4b14d2f7b` has `body_len=0` — thread-reply artifacts, not review passes. So the redesign had zero review coverage. **Decision (user, 2026-08-05): the next CodeRabbit slot goes back to #1072**, not #1070. Revised order: **#1072 (re-review) → #1070 → #1082 → #1071 → #1081 → #1078** — seven cycles, not six. ### `recycle.sh` — why `cycle.sh` was unsafe for a re-review `cycle.sh` detects "run started" by the mere presence of a CodeRabbit comment and "verdict landed" by any body-bearing review. On a **first** review both are correct. On a **re**-review both trip instantly against the previous round's artifacts: it would re-draft ~60s after flipping (possibly before the new run starts) and immediately declare the stale verdict as this round's. `recycle.sh` fixes both by keying off state that cannot be stale: - captures the CR status comment's `updated_at` **before** flipping, and waits for it to change (CodeRabbit edits ONE status comment in place, so a touch is the run-start signal); - treats a verdict as landed only when a body-bearing review carries `commit_id == `. Use `recycle.sh` for every subsequent cycle — first review or not, it is strictly safer. ### #1072 merge-readiness, checked 2026-08-05 All **20 required contexts green**, `mergeable=MERGEABLE`, `mergeStateStatus=CLEAN`. Disjoint from #1070, #1071, #1081, #1078. **One overlap not in the original map: `packages/client/src/testkit.ts` is touched by both #1072 and #1082** — #1072 adds a single enum line (`ExternalPinFailed: 8`). The pairwise `merge-tree` is CLEAN, but the original "engine-only" characterisation of #1072 was wrong. Not merged: a draft cannot be merged, and flipping ready to merge would consume the review slot.

3. Produce the **BLOCKED set**: open issues with at least one OPEN blocker — list issue → its open blockers.
4. **Find circular parent-block artifacts.** This repo has repeatedly accumulated a bug where an issue is `blocked_by` the very umbrella issue it is a sub-issue of. That edge can never clear, because the umbrella closes only when its children do. Detect these by resolving each issue's `parent` and checking whether the parent appears in its `blocked_by`. **Report them; do not delete them.** (4 were stripped in one prior wave, 8 in another — expect more.)
5. **Find prose-only blockers.** Some issue bodies say "blocked by #NNN" in text without a corresponding native edge. Grep issue bodies for "blocked by" / "depends on" / "waiting on" and report every case where the named issue is NOT a native `blocked_by` edge — and say whether the named issue is currently open or closed.
6. Report any issue that is **blocked_by a CLOSED issue only** but whose body still describes itself as blocked — i.e. stale self-description.
7. Report the umbrella/track structure: which issues are the tracks (#989-#996, #655) and how many open children each still has.

Return a COMPACT report. Use issue numbers, not titles, wherever possible. Structure:
- "STARTABLE (no open blockers)" — a plain sorted list of numbers, with a count
- "BLOCKED" — table: issue | open blockers
- "Circular parent-block artifacts" — table: issue | its parent that wrongly blocks it | parent's db id
- "Prose-only blockers" — table: issue | named blocker | open/closed | native edge exists?
- "Stale self-descriptions" — list
- "Track structure" — track | open child count

--- #994 ---
desktop: the apps/desktop and crates/fuse track
Umbrella for the desktop stack — hardware verification gates, the Tauri shell and version surface, the desktop seam set, the `crates/fuse` operation core and host-adapter trait, the FUSE-T SMB, libfuse3, and WinFsp adapters, mount lifecycle and tray, and the mounted e2e matrix.

Normative spec: `blueprint/desktop.md`.

Work is tracked as sub-issues of this one — this body carries no checkbox list.

Part of #655

--- #650 ---
desktop: wire login, mount lifecycle, tray, and the mounted e2e matrix
## Scope

Engine construction in-process at login with the desktop seam set; Web3Auth Core Kit webview handoff — secret crosses once to start(secret) and is zeroized, webview never holds tokens or keys; dev-key mode as the headless e2e seam; mount lifecycle (mount failure never fails login; quiesce adapter, unmount, stop engine; logout = facade logout + unmount + keychain delete, durable stores survive; forget-this-device wipes); tray rendering of the event stream (Synced/Reconciling/Stale/Offline ladder, dead-letter parked-writes with edge-triggered notifications and the recovered-files export, trust-violation/withheld-update escalation warning never conflated with staleness, Sync Now nocache); Tauri updater minisign wiring. Ports tests/desktop-e2e onto the facade: mount round-trip, conflict outcomes, cross-client sync, offline replay, rotation-under-mount. Recycle bin is NOT projected into the mount.

## Blueprint anchors

`blueprint/desktop.md`: Tauri shell; Engine wiring; Conflicts, dead letters, and rotation; Testing hooks

## Gate

desktop mounted matrix (macOS/Linux/Windows) in the main gate, revert-first; the desktop leg of the cross-client e2e matrix; the PR-tier smoke slice's timing-profile cross-client scenario once desktop hosts join it.

## Depends on

- #635 — the desktop-e2e matrix in scope includes rotation-under-mount, which cannot be asserted until rotation primitives (#635) land (not reachable via the #648→#647→#632 chain).



--- #648 ---
desktop: implement fuse read/write paths, journal ack, and freshness
## Scope

Ranged chunk reads (cached-first, CID-verified fetch, first byte before last byte) with the bounded in-memory plaintext LRU chunk cache zeroized on unmount; per-handle sealed spill files under ephemeral XChaCha20 keys; release/create/mkdir/rename/unlink/rmdir each becoming exactly one facade intent op, acked at durable StagingStore journal time (no-false-ack); honest ENOSPC on staging-budget exhaustion or hosted-quota preflight refusal; the scope-exit refusal path rejecting the op at journal time with EIO; dead-letter surfacing hooks; FUSE-op TTL checks + focus-window derivation from the op stream + engine-event-stream-driven push invalidation.
No adapters, no tray UI.

## Blueprint anchors

`blueprint/desktop.md`: Reads, writes, and the never-block law; Conflicts, dead letters, and rotation; Freshness

## Gate

fuse-op-core extended: never-block law, ack-at-journal, ENOSPC, TTL-check/invalidation coverage.

## Depends on

The three originally declared deps have all landed — #647 (PR #885), #632 (PR #706) and #630 (PR #700). Three dependencies this issue's own scope implies, previously undeclared, replace them:

- #884 — the scope requires "release/create/mkdir/rename/unlink/rmdir each becoming exactly one facade intent op". `OperationCore::rename` is today up to three separately-staged ops with a data-loss window, so the ack-at-journal law cannot be honestly implemented until #884 lands.
- #867 — the "dead-letter surfacing hooks" and the honest `ENOSPC` vs `EDQUOT` split are both deliverables of #867 (parts 1 and 4).
- #846 — "honest ENOSPC on staging-budget exhaustion" sits on the host-to-engine measured staging budget that #846 records as missing.



--- #649 ---
desktop: add the FUSE-T SMB, libfuse3, and WinFsp host adapters
## Scope

Three thin adapters behind the trait: FUSE-T >= 1.2.7 SMB backend (macOS, readdir single-pass quirk, SMB-backend invalidation), Linux kernel FUSE via the vendored fuser crate with the MSG_PEEK patch carried plus its committed regression test, and WinFsp (case-insensitive lookup, NTSTATUS mapping, notify API). Errno/status mapping per adapter; kernel entry/attr TTLs set from the sync timing profile per backend capability.
No FSKit adapter (designed-for, deliberately unbuilt), no macFUSE, no File Provider.

## Blueprint anchors

`blueprint/desktop.md`: The FS core and host adapters; Backends; Freshness

## Gate

Windows cargo check + adapter tests (PR tier, authoritative for the WinFsp adapter) + per-adapter errno/status mapping and MSG_PEEK regression tests in the fuse-op-core cargo job.




--- #720 ---
desktop: keyring seam blocks engine executor + real credential backends untested on Windows/Linux
From the retro `/security-review` of #666 (desktop seam set). Both are design/coverage residuals appropriate to a pre-ship desktop slice, not correctness bugs in the shipped code.

**1. [LOW-MED] Keyring seam blocks the single-threaded engine executor.** `crates/desktop-seams/src/credential_store.rs:86-96` (+ helpers `:44-65`). The `CredentialStore` methods are `async fn` but their bodies contain no `.await` — `entry.set_secret()/get_secret()` are synchronous blocking keyring IPC. On the engine's current-thread runtime (`spawn_local`, `!Send` futures) the whole future runs to completion in one poll, blocking the executor thread. Scenario: the first refresh-token load/store after restart on macOS triggers a Keychain "Allow" prompt → the engine event loop (timers, sync ticks) is frozen until the user responds. Infrequent (login/rotation) and a freeze during an explicit prompt is defensible UX, but keyring is uniquely capable of unbounded/UI-gated blocking. Fix (if desired): run keyring ops off the engine thread (dedicated blocking thread + channel), or document that credential access must not occur in latency-sensitive windows.

**2. [LOW] The real credential seam has no automated gate.** `crates/desktop-seams/tests/conformance.rs` runs the kit against the `test-support` `FileCredentialStore` double; the production `KeyringCredentialStore` is only exercised by `#[ignore]`d tests. Only macOS was manually verified this ship — Windows Credential Manager and Linux Secret Service paths are unverified by anyone. Low (thin wrapper, pre-ship), but the production credential path is untested on 2 of 3 platforms.

**Simplify nits:** `staged_keys`/`staged_bytes_total` re-inline the same "strip `.bin` + valid-hex stem" predicate (`staging_store.rs:156-197`) → extract one `sidecar_key(name)`; `RecordTransport::new`/`with_client` duplicate the `base_urls→endpoints` map and mix error models (`new` returns `SeamResult` but `assert!`-panics on empty endpoints while returning `Err` for a client-build failure) → unify; `queued_ops` re-derives `op_path(id)` from a name it already listed.

(Already tracked/acknowledged: `ReqwestHttp` untrusted-read has no total timeout + default redirect-following vs `ReqwestRecordTransport` which disables both — documented rationale in the PR triage; Windows `fsync_dir` no-op durability gap — #665.)

Part of #655

# WAVE 5 PLAN — drafted 2026-08-06

Baseline: `main` @ `3d087d673`, **0 open PRs**, clean primary worktree, no stale worktrees,
22 required status contexts. 103 open `v2-build` issues.

Wave 4 landed +8679/-599 across 97 files (#1072, #1070, #1082, #1071, #1081, #1078).

Recon: four read-only agents (rotation cluster, engine non-rotation, web/client, dependency graph),
every claim verified against code at `3d087d673` rather than taken from issue bodies.

---

## The strategic frame

**#635 is the critical path to a shippable v2.0.0**, and it is not close to done: 18 open children.

The dependency audit gives the chain explicitly:

```text
846 → 648 → 649 → 650 → 654
             635 ↗        651 → 652
                          651 → 653 → 656
```

#635 gates #650 (the mounted desktop e2e matrix asserts rotation-under-mount), which gates #651,
which gates #653 (staging cutover) and #654 (first RC). #635 also directly blocks #876, #953, #962
and, with #642, #643.

**Correction to the desktop story: #846 is NOT a real blocker ahead of #648.** Verified — the
engine and web legs already landed. `RejectedOverBudget` returns **zero hits repo-wide**;
`sync/staging.rs:50-65` has no budget branch; the web measures origin headroom and threads it
through `crates/wasm/src/host.rs:157-161` into `StoragePolicy::measured`. The `1 << 30` lives at
`storage_policy.rs:31`, not `profile.rs:59`. Only the desktop seam assembly remains, and that needs
a desktop `Engine::new` that does not exist yet — so #846's residue belongs **inside** #650, not
ahead of #648. **#648 is startable now.**

So: wave 5 leads with the rotation spine because it is the critical path, not despite it.

## The batch — 6 PRs

Ownership is the batching unit. `facade.rs` is 6195 lines with 13 contenders, `write_plane.rs`
6608 with 4, `drain.rs` 2971 with 7. One PR may own each per wave.

| PR | Track | Issues | Owns | Why here |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | engine | **1054** | `net/adopter.rs`, `gate/floor.rs`, `net/rotation.rs` (`GatedRoots`), `rotation/cascade.rs` | **Shape change**, and both #1025 and #1026 read through `gated_root`. Must land before either |
| **2** | engine | **1026** | `rotation/rotate_write.rs`, `net/rotation.rs`, `net/author.rs`, `net/retire.rs` | The #635 spine. **Shape change** — `RepublishedNode` gains `current_name` per ADR 0004. Gates #1019, #764, #1016 |
| **3** | engine | **1018** | `sync/drain.rs`, `sync/rebase.rs`, `sync/mod.rs`, `rotation/trigger.rs` | Scope-exit trigger consumption. Disjoint from the `rotation/` hot files except `trigger.rs`, which nobody else owns this wave |
| **4** | security | **1034 + 713 + 933 + 1086** | `api/client.rs`, `seams/http.rs`, `desktop-seams/src/http.rs`, `packages/client/src/seams/http.ts`, `content/{provider,read}.rs` | One contiguous auth/transport surface. Carries a **live signing oracle** — see below |
| **5** | web | **1069 + 808 + 1079** | `FileBrowser.tsx`, `snapshotStore.ts`, +`OfflineBanner`, +`NotificationToast`, +`stores/notification.store.ts`, +`hooks/useOnlineStatus.ts`, `AppShell.tsx`, `StatusIndicator.tsx`, `useFolderPicker.ts` | Error classification is the natural home for the notice class #808 introduces |
| **6** | web | **1093 + 1092 + 1080** | `DetailsDialog.tsx`, +`details/*`, +`TextEditorDialog.tsx`, `useFilePreview.ts`, `useFileDownload.ts`, `FilePreviewDialog.tsx`, `FileBrowserActions.tsx`, `media/service.ts` | #1092 and #1080 both rework `useFilePreview.ts`; #1093 is the smallest and lands first inside the PR |

**Merge order: 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 → 6.** PRs 1 and 2 are the shape changes and must merge early
(`project-semantic-merge-conflict-shape-change`; the failure mode hit on #779/#782 and #944/#946).
PRs 3-6 are file-disjoint from each other and from 1-2.

**PR-5 × PR-6 was deliberately split along the `FileBrowser.tsx` / `FileBrowserActions.tsx` seam.**
They are different files. **#1091 is held to wave 6 precisely because it touches BOTH** — scheduling
it would recreate the wave-4 hazard where two PRs edit one interface and merge clean into a
duplicate.

### PR-4 carries a live security defect — #1034

`crates/engine/src/api/client.rs:108-121` takes `body.challenge` straight from the server response
and signs it with the identity key at `:121`. Nothing checks it carries the `cipherbox-login:v2:`
prefix its own test fixture uses (`:709`). A hostile or compromised API returns an arbitrary string
and gets it signed by the identity key — a signing oracle, live today, single-file XS fix.
This is why PR-4 is not deferred despite being the least glamorous batch.

## Held out of wave 5, with the reason

- **#1025** (sweep rewrite, L) — it shares `net/rotation.rs` and `net/author.rs` with PR-2 and both
  are L. Running two large `rotation/` PRs in one wave is the exact shape that produced wave 4's
  silent duplicate. **Wave 6, immediately after #1026 lands.** #1017 and #754 trail it.
- **#1019 + #1020 + #784 + #771** — all four touch `rotation/trigger.rs`, which PR-3 owns this wave.
  Batch as ONE PR in wave 6; splitting them guarantees an enum conflict.
- **#1015 → #1016** — invites then facade arms. Both need body rewrites first (below).
- **#872 + #849/#850/#851** — one PR, and #872 must absorb the other three; they are unreachable
  standalone.
- **#1091** — touches both web hot files. Wave 6.
- **#918, #856, #926, #1059, #1028** — all shape changes needing their own early slot.
- **#648 / #649** — startable, but desktop is a distinct skill surface and #650 still waits on #635.

## Issue bodies that MUST be corrected before dispatch

Every one of these was verified against code at `3d087d673`. An agent handed the body as written
would build the wrong thing.

**Blocking — do not dispatch until rewritten:**

- **#1015** — "invites are 100% greenfield … no invite type, no ephemeral-key blob path, no ledger
  expiry field" is **false**. `grants/invite.rs` is 645 lines (`EphemeralInvitee:49`,
  `mint_invite_grant:154`, exported at `grants/mod.rs:38`); ledger expiry is landed at
  `core/seal/write_body.rs:64` with `entry_is_live` at `grants/ledger.rs:79`. **Only claim-to-grant
  conversion and bearer write-link flagging remain.** As written this causes a re-implementation.
- **#1017** — says the sweep is already built and forbids touching the algorithm. True today, false
  the moment #1025 lands. Must be re-cut against #1025's post-rewrite outcome type. Its cadence
  source does not exist either: `SyncTimingProfile` (`profile.rs:23`) has no sweep-cadence field,
  and adding one ripples to `wasm/host.rs:145` and `fuse/adapter.rs:58`.
- **#1016** — names a `Command::Share` that **does not exist** (it is `Command::Grant`,
  `facade.rs:459`). Every line number is stale: `Revoke:474`, `Downgrade:482`,
  `CreateInviteLink:491`, `AcceptShare:498`, `RotateNow:504`, catch-all `:2278` (not `:1901`).
  Omits `ImportContact` (`:460`), which is equally unwired.
- **#872** — its body names #849/#850/#851 as "three correctness prerequisites first", all three
  OPEN, **none wired as a native edge**. #872 therefore appears in the startable set and is not.
  Either add the edges or fold all three in. Also the constant is `REGISTRY_BATCH_MAX = 1000`
  (`net/mod.rs:25`), not `MAX_BATCH` (that is a load-test constant, `crates/load/src/plan.rs:119`).

**Rescope — partly delivered by wave 4, do not close:**

- **#1069** — "`rg '\.code\b' apps/web/src` returns no hits" is now false: `useDropUpload.ts:237`
  and `UploadListItem.tsx:32` both read it. The core defect stands — `FileBrowser.tsx:14` still
  blanks the listing on any error.
- **#1075** — "nothing in `apps/web` reads `blocked`" is now false (`introspection.ts:84`). The
  error-code path landed; what remains is the snapshot-sourced `blocked.opId`/`neededBytes` match,
  which fires when the drain holds an already-queued op rather than when a command is refused.
- **#808** — the staleness ladder is already bound (`useStaleness.ts` → `StatusIndicator.tsx:13,20`,
  all four rungs) and `DeadLetterNotice.tsx` already renders. Residual: `OfflineBanner`,
  `NotificationToast`, the notification store, `useOnlineStatus`/`useVisibility`, the
  withheld-update/attributable-abuse warning class, and `facade.manualRefresh`
  (`packages/client/src/facade.ts:143`) which has **zero** `apps/web` consumers.
- **#1096** — blockers 1 and 2 are now false (`FileBrowserActions.tsx:63-72` ships the context
  items, `:88` the `new-folder-button` testid; `useFileDownload` is consumed at `:65`). Blocker 3
  **stands**: `web-e2e.yml:29-31` starts Postgres and `mock-ipns-routing` only, no Kubo.
  `tests/web-e2e/README.md:25-28` is stale for the same reason.
- **#846** — rescope to the desktop seam leg only; the engine and web legs have landed.

**Downgrade or drop:**

- **#778** — a wire-format + KAT change to `ChildScopeRef`, self-declared optional, gated on latency
  measurements that do not exist. **Recommend dropping from v2.**
- **#703** — `revive()` (`net/revival.rs:48`) has **zero production callers**; tests only. Also
  misattributes the fix site: the `max()` is `net/publish.rs:190`.
- **#775** — no `Shared` caller exists; only the optional test is real work. Its claimed
  `boot::cold_start` integration test does not exist — coverage is one in-module unit test
  (`sync/boot.rs:590`).
- **#849/#850/#851** — `plan_prune` has **zero production callers**; all three are latent-by-doc.
  Fold into #872. (#851 is also half-refuted: `RetentionPolicy::KeepLatest(NonZeroU64)` already
  exists at `retention.rs:65`; the `usize` hole survives only at `:93-94`.)
- **#831** — perf-only, gated behind five undecided policy questions. Its premise is also refuted:
  `leaf_range_for_byte_range` **is** called in production (`content/mod.rs:281` → `facade.rs:2979`)
  and the record cache is per-name-keyed (`net/resolve.rs:187-203`), not one global slot.

**Blocked in fact by a missing host surface:**

- **#1064** — no media player component exists anywhere in `apps/web` (v1 had
  `AudioPlayerDialog.tsx`/`VideoPlayerDialog.tsx`; v2 has neither). Its premise sentence is also
  false — it asserts the vault browser already renders a recoverable error as a retryable notice,
  which describes the state #1069 creates.
- **#785** — no caller exists to bound. `ConflictingChildLabel` is produced in
  `eager_set.rs`/`cascade.rs` but the retry policy lives in a facade arm still `Unimplemented`.
  Genuinely blocked on #1016, not merely ordered after it.

**Other verified body errors** (correct before the owning issue is scheduled): #1054/#1026 name
`OwnerRotationNet::publish_scope_root` — no such inherent method, it is the `ScopeRootPublisher`
trait impl at `net/rotation.rs:561`. #764 and #785 point at #745/#746 as the future home of
resolver wiring; both closed, wiring landed at `net/rotation.rs:487,502,561`. #1050's constants are
in `core/seal/section.rs:275,272`, not `grant.rs`; the unbounded decode is `grant.rs:754-770`.
#1084 undercounts — seven `DefaultsReason` variants refuse, not six (`FloorUnreadable`,
`settings.rs:375`). #1085's per-tick clone is `facade.rs:1995`, not `sync/tick.rs` (zero
`placement` references there). #1043 is half-refuted — `load_settings` HAS a production caller
(`facade.rs:1638`); only `publish_settings` (`settings.rs:464`) lacks one. #1056's `|_|` is gone —
`net/rotation.rs:608` routes through `author_verdict` (`:325`); the dropped name is still real.
#1059 misses a fourth `leaf_cid_vecs()` caller at `content/write.rs:202`. #860's two claims are
refuted — `remove_staged_bytes` has four production callers and a completion record exists
(`published_op_mark`, `drain.rs:2447`). #933's BYO validation is `is_bearer_byte`
(`provider.rs:469`) applied at config entry, not at the splice. #1067 is stale on every row of
#767's size table. #915 is sharper than filed: `ContentProfile::PRODUCTION.chunk_size = 1_048_536`
(`content/profile.rs:36`) is **40 bytes short of 1 MiB** while `limits.rs:12` calls it "1 MiB" —
likely a digit transposition worth confirming.

## Tracker hygiene — cheap, and it is distorting the plan

1. **30 open issues carry no milestone** — every follow-up from #1037 onward. The v2.0.0 milestone
   reads 73 open when the real number is 103, understating remaining work by ~40%.
2. **24 open issues have no parent** and are invisible in the track rollup: 953, 958, 959, 962,
   1033, 1034, 1037, 1043, 1050, 1051, 1054, 1056, 1059, 1060, 1076, 1077, 1079, 1080, 1084, 1085,
   1086, 1090, 1096. Nearly a quarter of the backlog, so any track-based capacity estimate silently

4. **#872's prose-only prerequisites** — add native edges to #849/#850/#851, or fold them in.
5. **#1087 → #914** is prose-only and phrased "may be subsumed by". Decide dedup vs block before
   either is scheduled; do not run them concurrently.
6. **Stale `## Depends on` sections** naming only closed issues: #860, #913, #914, #958, #959,
   #1084, #1085, #1086. #938's says #910 (closed) but it is genuinely blocked by #752.

**Good news on the dependency graph: zero circular parent-block artifacts.** Every open issue's
`blocked_by` set was checked against its full ancestor chain. The wave-2 (4 stripped) and wave-4
(8 stripped) repairs held. 80 issues are startable, 23 blocked, 90 edges total (30 open, 60 closed).

## Review-queue plan

Unchanged from wave 4, which worked: **70-minute spacing between ready-flips**, measured from the
PREVIOUS VERDICT's landing time, never from "now". Six PRs = six slots ≈ 7 hours.

Use `recycle-both.sh <PR> [notbefore-epoch]`. **`review2.sh` and `cycle.sh` remain broken** — a
`gh api --arg` that errors silently, and a re-draft that fires before either bot lands.

Every PR: DRAFT until its own CI is green → flip exactly one at a time → hold ready until BOTH
CodeRabbit and macroscope land on the head → re-draft → push fixes against the draft.

`/crypto-privacy-review` for anything touching crypto or a trust boundary — which this wave means
PRs 1, 2 and 4.

## Launch preconditions

- Fast-forward local `main` to `origin/main` BEFORE launching — `isolation: worktree` forks LOCAL

name: project-gh-rest-parent-field-false-negative
description: "gh api /issues/N --jq '.parent' ALWAYS returns null — the REST payload has no parent object; every orphan check built on it is a false negative"
metadata:

  type: project

`env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api /repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/<N> --jq '.parent.number'` **always
returns `null`**, whether or not the issue has a parent. The REST issue payload carries no `parent`
object — the field is **`parent_issue_url`**.

GraphQL times out on this repo often enough that REST is the usual path.

artifact of missing parentage, not completeness.** #989 (core) showed 12/12 closed and looked
ready to close — but #1050, live core-track work, was orphaned and therefore invisible in the
rollup. After parenting it read 12/13 with one open child. **Always parent the orphans BEFORE
evaluating any umbrella for closure**, never after. #990 (api) survived the same check and is
genuinely 8/8 — but note that "no open children" only proves no *tracked* work remains.

Related: [[feedback-use-github-native-issue-dependencies]] (the dependency API is keyed by the
database `id`, not the issue number — the same shape of trap one level over).

## Tracker hygiene — DONE 2026-08-06, all verified by read-back

1. **Milestone** — 30 issues PATCHed with the `milestone` field only. v2.0.0 open count
   **73 → 103**, closed unchanged at 137. The burndown had been understating remaining work ~40%.
2. **Parenting** — **23** orphans parented (the count was 23, not 24). #989←1050; #991←962, 1043,
   1084, 1085; #752←1034, 1060; #635←1054, 1076, 1077; #992←1056, 1059, 1090; #993←953, 1033,
   1037, 1051, 1086; #642←1079, 1080; #995←958, 959, 1096.
3. **#989 is NOT complete** — it now reads 12/13 with **#1050** as its one open child. Its
   apparent completeness was purely the missing parentage. **#990 (api) is genuinely 8/8.**
   Neither was closed. **Rule: parent the orphans BEFORE evaluating any umbrella for closure.**
4. **#872** — native `blocked_by` edges added to #849/#850/#851, and its body rewritten to absorb
   all three (they are unreachable standalone).
5. **Edges added** — #1087 `blocked_by` #914; #785 `blocked_by` #1016. Both verified by GET.
6. **Stale `## Depends on` sections** rewritten on #860, #913, #914, #958, #959, #1084, #1085,
   #1086; #938 corrected to name #752 as its real blocker. #860 and #959 needed more than the
   header — both carried scope prose falsified by #1072 (#860: "no production drain path at all"
   and "`remove_staged_bytes` has zero non-test callers", both false — `drain.rs:1653`,
   `staging.rs:90-92`; #959: "nothing ships a byte to an external provider today").
7. **Drop candidates annotated, none closed** — #778, #703, #775, #849, #850, #851, #831 each
   carry an evidence comment. The close decision is the maintainer's.

**Method trap found and recorded** (`project-gh-rest-parent-field-false-negative`):

**Verdict: the change is correct and is a genuine security improvement.** It converts an *unbounded* reader-CPU amplifier into a *bounded* one, with real encode/decode symmetry. No blocking defect. Findings below are one Medium residual (pre-existing, only partly closed here) and a set of Low/Info items.

**1. Is the encode-side check release-active, and does every produce path reach it? — YES, verified empirically.**

```

test result: ok. 1 passed
```

Reachability is total, because every attesting path funnels through `encode_grant_set_commitment` (`crates/core/src/seal/grant.rs:788`):

- `verify_grant_set` (`grant.rs:825`) calls it — so `gate/adoption.rs:517`, `net/author.rs:236`, `rotation/rotate_write.rs:430`, `rotation/trigger.rs:135` all inherit it.
- `encode_grant_section` (`section.rs:397`) calls it — so no section can carry an over-bound commitment.
- Every producer's error path propagates `Err` (`CreateGrantError::CommitmentEncode`, `RevokeError::Sign`, `AuthorError::Seal`); no `unwrap`/`expect` on a production path.

There is no TS/WASM commitment constructor, consistent with "TypeScript has no crypto of its own."

**2. Does the bound change the signed preimage or any wire bytes? — NO. Proven.**

`assert_within_bound` returns before the `Map` is built and mutates nothing; `Vec::with_capacity` in decode is an allocation hint only. Empirical proof: `crates/core/tests/kat_manifest.rs:4337` asserts `hex::encode(encode_grant_set_commitment(&c))` equals committed golden hex for every accept vector, and `git diff main...HEAD --stat -- crates/core/kat/vectors/` shows **only** `grant_set_reject.json` changed (+8 lines, one new reject vector). `for step in 0..n { let i = (self.resume_at + step) % n; ... }` (`gate/adoption.rs:359-360`). Side channel: clean. Every input is public — signatures ride on the wire, pseudonym pks ride in the owner-signed commitment. An observer who could time the scan can trivially recompute "which pseudonym signed" from the same public bytes. The pre-diff always-from-0 scan already leaked list position; `resume_at` changes *which* fact timing reveals (same-signer-as-previous rather than absolute index) but neither is secret. **Location:** `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-abe1b4269f7a3ff37/crates/engine/src/gate/adoption.rs:344-366` (the scan) and `:311-323` (`committed_write_pseudonyms`)

**Issue:** This is a *residual*, not a regression — the diff strictly improves it. Pre-diff, `entries` was unbounded, so the committed write-pseudonym list was unbounded and the amplifier had no ceiling. Post-diff it is bounded, but the ceiling is still large. `resume_at` optimizes the honest case only; the adversarial worst case is unchanged at the product.

Worst case after this diff: pseudonyms `≤ 1 + 1024 = 1025`; structures `= 1 (ownerBlob) + 1 (ownerWriteBlob) + 1024 (grantBlobs) + 256 (historyLinks) + 1 (writeBody) + 1 (ascentLink) = 1284`. Product ≈ **1.32M Ed25519 verifications**, roughly 60 s of single-core CPU, from a record well under the 4 MiB `MAX_RESOLVED_RECORD_BYTES` ceiling.

**Impact:** Reachable by anyone whose owner identity the reader has contact-anchored — i.e. anyone who has ever shared with you. The attacker generates 1024 Ed25519 write-pseudonym keys (free), signs a commitment with their own identity key (passes stage 2), and signs structure *k* with pseudonym `(resume_at - 1) mod n` so the resumed scan is always maximally wrong. Attacker cost ~1284 signs (~50 ms); victim cost ~60 s per adoption, repeated on every focus-window poll. Amplification ~1000×. Note the short-circuit does *not* help: to sustain the product every structure must eventually verify, which the attacker arranges.

**Recommendation:** Exploit the invariant this diff's own comment identifies — a re-seal signs every structure under one pseudonym (verified at `reseal.rs:441-447`). Resolve the signer once on the first structure, then pin it:

```rust
struct StructureAuthenticator {
    committed: Vec<Ed25519Verifier>,
    /// Pinned after the first structure verifies: an honest re-seal signs every
    /// structure under one pseudonym (rotation/reseal.rs), so a section that
    /// switches signers mid-way is an authored anomaly.
    signer: Option<usize>,
}

fn authenticate(&mut self, ...) -> Result<(), CodecError> {
    let input = StructureSigInput::over_ciphertext(...);
    let sig = Ed25519Signature::from_bytes(*signature);
    if let Some(i) = self.signer {
        return verify_structure(&self.committed[i], &input, &sig)
            .map_err(|_| TrustViolation::StructureSignatureInvalid.into());
    }
    for (i, p) in self.committed.iter().enumerate() {
        if verify_structure(p, &input, &sig).is_ok() {
            self.signer = Some(i);
            return Ok(());
        }
    }
    Err(TrustViolation::StructureSignatureInvalid.into())
}
```

If pinning is judged too strict for a future multi-writer shape, the fallback is a per-section trial-verify budget (e.g. `4 * (P + S)`) that fails closed on exhaustion.

<result>Reuse review complete. The consolidation this diff does is sound; the gaps are all **sites the consolidation missed**, not new duplication it introduced.

## Findings

**1. `crates/load/src/runner.rs:91` — a fourth bearer splice site the diff left hand-rolled.**
```rust
.map(|token| vec![("Authorization".to_owned(), format!("Bearer {token}"))])
```
This is the exact code `bearer_header` was created to absorb. The PR's premise is "give the bearer header one home", and after it there are still two homes. Cost: the load harness silently ships an unvalidated bearer (empty token → `Authorization: Bearer `, control char → header injection) while the three engine sites now fail closed — so the harness no longer exercises the shipping client's header path, which is the stated reason `crates/load` exists (`crates/load/Cargo.toml` header comment: "a run measures the shipping client path").
**Use instead:** `cipherbox_engine::seams::bearer_header` — already `pub` via `crates/engine/src/seams/mod.rs:25-28`, and `crates/load` already depends on `cipherbox-engine` and imports from `cipherbox_engine::seams` at `crates/load/src/runner.rs:13`.

**2. `crates/load/src/seams.rs:18-23` — builds its own `reqwest::Client` without the redirect policy this diff just made a seam obligation.**
The diff rewrites the `Http` trait doc (`crates/engine/src/seams/http.rs:182-188`) to say the transport "must not follow a redirect", and adds `.redirect(Policy::none())` to `ReqwestHttp::new()`. But `build_http()` goes through `ReqwestHttp::with_client(client)` with a builder that omits it, so reqwest's default (follow up to 10 hops) applies. Cost: the one obligation the diff writes into the trait contract has no single home — it lives in `ReqwestHttp::new()` and is lost by every `with_client` caller. Either add `.redirect(reqwest::redirect::Policy::none())` at `seams.rs:20`, or better, move the policy into `ReqwestHttp` itself so `with_client` cannot drop it.

**3. `crates/engine/src/facade.rs:3370-3371` — `LOGIN_CHALLENGE` duplicates `challenge()` at `crates/engine/src/api/client.rs:775-777`, and hardcodes the domain tag.**
Same crate, same shape, two independent spellings — and unlike `challenge()`, the facade const does not derive from `IDENTITY_CHALLENGE_PREFIX` (`client.rs:651`). Cost: a v2→v3 tag bump has to be found and fixed in three places (`client.rs:651`, `facade.rs:3371`, `packages/client/test/browser/mockAuth.ts:47`), and only the first is compiler-reachable.
**Fix:** make `IDENTITY_CHALLENGE_PREFIX` `pub(crate)` and put one fixture in `crates/engine/src/testkit/` (there is no existing challenge helper there — I checked all of `testkit/`, `testkit/fakes/`, and `crates/engine/tests/facade.rs`), so both test modules call it. The `mockAuth.ts` copy is a genuine cross-language boundary and has to stay a literal.

**4. Minor — `crates/desktop-seams/src/http.rs:38-45`** states the no-redirect rationale in 8 lines, then ends with "Mirrors `ReqwestRecordTransport`", where `record_transport.rs:46-50` already states it. Per AGENTS.md ("state genuine non-obvious domain rationale once, at its home"), the cross-reference alone would do; the re-derivation is the second copy that will rot.

## Checked and deliberately not worth changing

- **`bearer_header` / `InvalidBearer` / `AUTHORIZATION` (`crates/engine/src/seams/http.rs:27-46`)** — correct consolidation, nothing pre-existing to reuse. `crates/core` has no header or transport surface at all; the deleted `is_bearer_byte` was the only prior helper and is properly subsumed (same `0x21..=0x7e` class, with the empty-token case folded in from `validate_byo_config`). All three engine splice sites now route through it.
- **`is_identity_challenge` (`client.rs:664-673`)** — no existing helper to reuse. `cipherbox_core::hex` (`crates/core/src/hex.rs`) contains only `lower()`, an encoder with no validator counterpart, and nothing else in the workspace validates a lowercase-hex string. `is_eip4361_nonce` (8..=128 alnum), `is_canonical_content_cid_str` (base32-lower + `2-7`, fixed length), and `is_authority_byte`/`is_path_byte` (URL byte classes) each pin a different alphabet for a different reason — factoring them behind a shared "shape validator" would be speculative generality over four one-line predicates. `u8::is_ascii_hexdigit` from std admits uppercase, which case 7 of the new test explicitly rejects, so the hand-roll is deliberate and right.
- **`RefreshLead` (`client.rs:66-95`)** — no generic guard exists to reuse: no `scopeguard` dependency in the workspace, and the only `impl Drop`s are `SecretBytes`, `PreservedFields`, and `StreamSlot`. It follows the same crate-local RAII idiom as `StreamSlot` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:1372-1391`) — acquire-in-constructor, release-in-`Drop`, plus an explicit consuming `finish()`. Consistent, not duplicative.
- **`redirect: 'error'` in `packages/client/src/seams/http.ts:31` vs `endpointPolicy()` in `recordTransport.ts:31-37`** — should not share. `endpointPolicy()` returns a fixed triple (`credentials: 'omit'`, `redirect: 'error'`, a fixed 30s `AbortSignal.timeout`); `requestInit()` takes credentials and the deadline from the request. The only common field is the one literal, so extracting it would leave a shared constant that both sites still have to spell out, and would couple the record-transport's fixed policy to the per-request `Http` seam. The `// Mirrors FetchRecordTransport` comment is the right amount of coupling.</result>

<result>I read the full diff, the signer, all four `sign_detcbor` domains in `crates/core`, the KDF edge catalog, the API's challenge service, and the seam/provider/read splice sites. Verdict up front: **the central fix is correct and sufficient. I found no security defect introduced by this PR.** One real (LOW) privacy regression, and several test/operational gaps.

---

## 1. Is pinning the full shape sufficient to close the oracle? — Yes.

The residual steerable preimage is `sha256("cipherbox-login:v2:" || hex64)`: 83 ASCII bytes, 256 attacker-chosen bits confined to `[0-9a-f]`.

**Every other secp256k1 identity domain is structurally disjoint.** All four `sign_detcbor` call sites sign a det-CBOR *container*, so the first preimage byte is a CBOR major-type-4/5 header, never `0x63` (`'c'`):

| Domain | Site | First preimage byte |
|---|---|---|
| Subkey binding `{encSubkey, identityPk}` | `crates/core/src/suite/contact.rs:26-36` | `0xa2` (map, 2) |
| Grant-set commitment | `crates/core/src/seal/grant.rs:779-792` | `0xa3`+ (map) |
| Re-point object | `crates/core/src/payload/pointer.rs:135` | `0xa?` (map) |
| Mailbox sender sig | `crates/core/src/payload/mailbox.rs:75-85` | `0x85` (array, 5) |

Each also embeds 32/33/64-byte `Value::Bytes` fields, so length alone excludes an 83-byte all-ASCII string. A challenge string can never *be* one of these preimages, and none of these preimages can ever be a challenge string. Every verifier reconstructs its preimage from typed fields, so there is no "loose bytes" acceptance path. **Domain separation is genuinely complete for the identity key.**

Other signing domains are on different keys entirely: IPNS records (`crates/core/src/ipns/record.rs:119`) and structure signatures (`crates/core/src/seal/structure.rs:83`) are Ed25519; EOLs and name registrations ride the Ed25519 write plane. SIWE/EIP-4361 is keccak256 and is signed by the *wallet*, not the engine — `siwe_login`/`siwe_link` (`crates/engine/src/api/client.rs:198,215`) only forward a host-collected `(message, signature)`; the engine never signs an EIP-191 preimage.

**Worth stating explicitly: the pre-existing bug was worse than a same-protocol issue.** `sign_detcbor` is single-SHA256 over caller bytes, and the identity scalar is the raw Web3Auth secp256k1 export (`crates/engine/src/session.rs:78-80`). A Bitcoin sighash is `sha256(sha256(tx))`, so a hostile responder needed only to serve `sha256(tx)` as the challenge — grindable, since the sole constraint was that the 32 bytes be valid UTF-8 (serde `String`). Pre-fix that was plausibly a **transaction-signing oracle on a funded key**, not merely a CipherBox-internal forgery risk. This PR closes it: the responder can no longer place a chosen 32-byte digest into the preimage at all.

**The one thing shape pinning does not close (pre-existing, inherent, not a defect in this PR):** the challenge is not bound to the API origin or channel. A hostile responder at `apiBaseUrl` can proxy a *genuine* challenge from the real API (`/auth/challenge` is unauthenticated and takes any `publicKey`), harvest the victim's signature, and complete the login itself. Shape pinning cannot prevent this; only channel binding or TLS integrity can, and an attacker who controls `apiBaseUrl` already owns the session. Correctly out of scope.

## 2. Cross-protocol / signature reuse — no amplification path, but note the blast radius.

`SessionIdentity::derive` (`crates/engine/src/session.rs:78-83`) adopts the login secret **as** the ECDSA scalar, and passes the same bytes as ikm to `kdf::enc_subkey` and `kdf::owner_pointer_seed`. Per the catalog (`crates/core/src/kdf/mod.rs:94-134`), the login secret is also ikm for `vault-pointer-index` (Ed25519) and `settings-ipns-keypair` (Ed25519).

So the identity *private key* is the root of the entire owner plane. That amplifies the consequence of key compromise to total account compromise — which is precisely why this key must not be a general-purpose signing oracle, and justifies the fix's severity.

Critically, though: **no catalog edge takes a signature as ikm** (I checked all 16 `input_layout` entries), and RFC 6979 ECDSA over chosen messages does not leak the scalar. So an ECDSA oracle never crosses into the X25519 or Ed25519 halves. The X25519 subkey derives *from* the scalar through BLAKE3 `derive_key` with a distinct context — one-way and domain-separated. No finding.

## 3. RFC 6979 determinism — not a problem.

Determinism is the safe property here: same key + same message ⇒ same `k`, so there is no nonce-reuse exposure. Different messages get different `k`. Replay is closed server-side by `ChallengeService.consume` (`apps/api/src/auth/services/challenge.service.ts:63-72`): single-use, `kind`-checked, `publicKey`-bound, TTL-checked, and `delete` happens before the expiry check so a consumed value cannot be re-spent even on the expiry-error path. Ordering in `auth.service.ts:55-56` is `consume` *then* verify — correct.

The client not checking `expiresAt` and having no injected clock is **fine and arguably correct**: the client has no authority over challenge lifetime, and a client-side clock check would only add a determinism seam for no security gain. `expiresAt` is decorative on the client. No finding.
