#!/bin/bash
# Re-review cycle that holds READY until BOTH CodeRabbit and macroscope land on the
# current head. review2.sh re-drafts as soon as CR touches its status comment, which
# can cut macroscope (READY-only, ~3-7min) off mid-run.
#   $1 = PR   $2 = earliest epoch to flip (optional, default now)
PR=$1; NOTBEFORE=${2:-0}
cd /Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box
GH="env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh"

# The head is the key every later check keys on, so a transient failure here must
# abort rather than proceed with an empty string that silently matches nothing.
HEAD=""
for a in 1 2 3 4 5; do
  HEAD=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR --jq '.head.sha' 2>/dev/null)
  case "$HEAD" in [0-9a-f]*) [ ${#HEAD} -eq 40 ] && break ;; esac
  HEAD=""; echo "  head read failed (attempt $a) - retrying"; sleep 15
done
[ -n "$HEAD" ] || { echo "CANNOT READ HEAD FOR #$PR - aborting, nothing flipped."; exit 7; }
echo "#$PR head=$HEAD"

# 1. CI must be settled: no failures, nothing pending except the reviewers' own contexts.
#    A just-pushed head has ZERO registered checks, which reads as "nothing pending" —
#    so a plausible check count is required before green is believed.
MINCHECKS=${MINCHECKS:-15}
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  sleep 20
  FAIL=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="FAILURE" or .conclusion=="TIMED_OUT")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  PEND=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion==null)|select((.name // .context)|test("CodeRabbit|Macroscope";"i")|not)]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  OK=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="SUCCESS")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  DONE=$($GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '[.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion!=null)]|length' 2>/dev/null)
  echo "[$(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)] ci: success=$OK settled=$DONE pending=$PEND failed=$FAIL (need >=$MINCHECKS)"
  if [ -n "$FAIL" ] && [ "$FAIL" != "0" ]; then
    echo "CI FAILED on $HEAD - not flipping"
    $GH pr view $PR --json statusCheckRollup --jq '.statusCheckRollup[]|select(.conclusion=="FAILURE")|.name'
    exit 4
  fi
  if [ "$PEND" = "0" ] && [ -n "$PEND" ] && { [ -n "$DONE" ] && [ "$DONE" -ge "$MINCHECKS" ]; } 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "CI GREEN ($DONE checks settled)"; break
  fi
  sleep 40
done

# 2. Respect the CodeRabbit hourly reset.
NOW=$(date -u +%s)
if [ "$NOTBEFORE" -gt "$NOW" ]; then
  echo "waiting $((NOTBEFORE-NOW))s for the review slot"; sleep $((NOTBEFORE-NOW))
fi

BASE=""
for a in 1 2 3; do
  BASE=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // "none"' 2>/dev/null)
  [ -n "$BASE" ] && break
  echo "  baseline read failed (attempt $a) - retrying"; sleep 15
done
[ -n "$BASE" ] || { echo "CANNOT READ CR BASELINE - aborting before flipping"; exit 6; }
echo "baseline cr status-comment updated_at=$BASE"

# Flip must be CONFIRMED. A swallowed `gh pr ready` failure (network) leaves the PR
# a draft while the poll loop below waits out its full timeout on verdicts that can
# never arrive - which reads as "no findings" when nothing was ever reviewed.
FLIPPED=0
for a in 1 2 3 4 5; do
  $GH pr ready $PR >/dev/null 2>&1
  sleep 5
  D=$($GH pr view $PR --json isDraft --jq '.isDraft' 2>/dev/null)
  if [ "$D" = "false" ]; then FLIPPED=1; echo "FLIPPED READY $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"; break; fi
  echo "  flip attempt $a did not take (isDraft=[$D]) - retrying"
  sleep 20
done
[ "$FLIPPED" = "1" ] || { echo "COULD NOT FLIP #$PR READY - aborting. No review slot was consumed."; exit 5; }

# 3. Hold ready until BOTH verdicts are on THIS head, or 40m.
#    CR verdict  == a body-bearing review whose commit_id is the head.
#    macroscope  == its check-runs exist on the head and none are still in flight.
CR_DONE=0; MS_DONE=0; MS_REVIEWED=0
for i in $(seq 1 40); do
  sleep 60
  U_NOW=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // "none"')
  if [ "$CR_DONE" = "0" ]; then
    # gh api takes no --arg, so the head is interpolated into the filter.
    N=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/reviews --jq "[.[]|select(.user.login|test(\"coderabbit\";\"i\"))|select((.body|length)>0)|select(.commit_id==\"$HEAD\")]|length" 2>/dev/null)
    # A CLEAN verdict posts NO review — it only edits the status comment. Findings
    # come as a review body; both surfaces have to be polled.
    CLEAN=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|select(.body|test("No actionable comments";"i"))]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    if { [ -n "$N" ] && [ "$N" -gt 0 ]; } 2>/dev/null; then
      CR_DONE=1; echo "  CR VERDICT (findings) on head @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"
    elif { [ -n "$CLEAN" ] && [ "$CLEAN" -gt 0 ]; } 2>/dev/null && [ -n "$U_NOW" ] && [ "$U_NOW" != "$BASE" ]; then
      CR_DONE=1; echo "  CR VERDICT (clean, status comment) @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"
    fi
  fi
  if [ "$MS_DONE" = "0" ]; then
    MST=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '[.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    MSP=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '[.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))|select(.status!="completed")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    # "completed" is not "reviewed": a skipped run completes too. Out of credits,
    # macroscope skips all five with "Credit balance exhausted", which the old
    # completed-count test scored as full coverage.
    MSR=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '[.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))|select(.conclusion!="skipped")]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    MSX=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '[.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))|select((.output.title // "")|test("[Cc]redit balance exhausted"))]|length' 2>/dev/null)
    if { [ -n "$MSX" ] && [ "$MSX" -gt 0 ]; } 2>/dev/null; then
      MS_DONE=1; MS_REVIEWED=0
      echo "  MACROSCOPE OUT OF CREDITS on head @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ) - NOT REVIEWED, not waiting"
    elif [ -n "$MST" ] && [ "$MST" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null && [ "$MSP" = "0" ]; then
      MS_DONE=1
      if { [ -n "$MSR" ] && [ "$MSR" -gt 0 ]; } 2>/dev/null; then
        MS_REVIEWED=1; echo "  MACROSCOPE REVIEWED on head @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ) ($MSR of $MST agents ran)"
      else
        MS_REVIEWED=0; echo "  MACROSCOPE ALL SKIPPED on head @ $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ) - NOT REVIEWED"
      fi
    fi
  fi
  LIM=$($GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/$PR/comments --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))|select(.body|test("Review limit reached";"i"))|.updated_at]|max // ""' 2>/dev/null)
  echo "  t+${i}m cr_done=$CR_DONE ms_done=$MS_DONE cr_comment_upd=$U_NOW ratelimit=[$LIM]"
  [ "$CR_DONE" = "1" ] && [ "$MS_DONE" = "1" ] && break
done

# Re-draft must be confirmed too: a PR left ready collects an unplanned review.
for a in 1 2 3 4; do
  $GH pr ready $PR --undo >/dev/null 2>&1
  sleep 5
  D=$($GH pr view $PR --json isDraft --jq '.isDraft' 2>/dev/null)
  [ "$D" = "true" ] && { echo "RE-DRAFTED $(date -u +%H:%M:%SZ)"; break; }
  echo "  re-draft attempt $a did not take (isDraft=[$D]) - retrying"; sleep 15
  [ "$a" = "4" ] && echo "WARNING: #$PR MAY STILL BE READY - re-draft it by hand"
done

echo "=== RESULT on $HEAD ==="
echo "-- coderabbit verdict --"
$GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/reviews --jq ".[]|select(.user.login|test(\"coderabbit\";\"i\"))|select((.body|length)>0)|select(.commit_id==\"$HEAD\")|.body" 2>/dev/null | grep -m1 -iE "actionable comments posted|nitpick comments|no actionable comments" || echo "(no CR verdict on head)"
echo "-- macroscope check-runs --"
$GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/commits/$HEAD/check-runs --jq '.check_runs[]|select(.name|test("macroscope";"i"))|"\(.name) | \(.status) | \(.conclusion)"' 2>/dev/null || true
echo "-- inline comments on head, by author --"
$GH api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/$PR/comments --paginate --jq "[.[]|select(.original_commit_id==\"$HEAD\" or .commit_id==\"$HEAD\")|.user.login]|group_by(.)|map(\"\(.[0]):\(length)\")|join(\" \")" 2>/dev/null
[ "$CR_DONE" = "1" ] && [ "$MS_DONE" = "1" ] && exit 0
echo "INCOMPLETE (cr=$CR_DONE ms=$MS_DONE)"; exit 2

`macroscope` was added as a PR review tool on FSM1/cipher-box on **2026-08-05**, joining
CodeRabbit and Greptile (Greptile quota resets mid-Aug 2026). Three reviewers now.

**Its triggering is INCONSISTENT — do not model it as strictly ready-only.** The user
disabled draft review on 2026-08-05, and it then skipped several draft heads. But on
**#1072 head `c806df6d5` (2026-08-05 14:05Z) all four agents ran on a PR that was in
draft** — pushed ~8 min after a re-draft. It then ran on *nothing* for the next head
`bc47da7d0`. Working hypothesis (unconfirmed): once a PR has been ready at least once, it
may review later pushes regardless of draft state, but not reliably. **Never infer coverage
from draft state — always query the head's check-runs** (`commits/<sha>/check-runs`,
filter `name|test("macroscope";"i")`) to see whether it actually ran.

`Macroscope - Correctness Check` skips far more often than the other three agents; a
`skipped` conclusion there is normal and is not a pass.

**A `success` conclusion does NOT mean that agent posted no findings.** On #1078,
`Language idioms` reported `success` while still having an inline thread open. Its
conclusions describe the agent's run, not the review outcome — always enumerate
`reviewThreads`, and **re-query before concluding you have them all**: a first GraphQL
query returned 3 threads where a second returned 4.

**`Ticket Requirements` verdict grammar.** `neutral` is NOT synonymous with a spec
mismatch — across one wave it meant a real deviation once, a benign harvest-list note
twice, and an unchanged previously-reported item once. Always read the check-run's
`output` field and compare against the previous run; it re-scopes between heads (one PR
went "3 harvest items" → "1 unimplemented item" with no code change). It also declines to
re-post an unchanged finding, saying so explicitly.

**Consequence for the draft convention.** Coverage is not guaranteed on a draft
([[feedback-keep-prs-draft-control-cr-timing]]) — CodeRabbit is genuinely ready-gated, so a
draft PR sitting with "no findings" still proves nothing. The flip to ready is the reliable
trigger for all three at once. When flipping to collect verdicts, **hold ready until each
reviewer has actually landed on the head**: on #1072 macroscope took ~4 min and CodeRabbit
~8.5 min after the flip, so a script that re-drafts on the first CodeRabbit status-comment
touch (~1 min) cuts both off. See `recycle-both.sh`.

**Where its output lands.** Author login is **`macroscopeapp[bot]`**. The review event
itself (`pulls/N/reviews`) is `COMMENTED` with an **empty body** — the findings are
inline `pulls/N/comments` entries. So a poller that reads only review *bodies* sees
nothing, the mirror of the CodeRabbit trap in
[[project-coderabbit-verdict-two-surfaces]]. Poll `pulls/N/comments` and filter on
`.user.login`.

**Finding format:** severity emoji + level (`🟠 **High**`), a `file:line` anchor, prose,
then a collapsible *"Reply 'fix it for me' or copy this AI Prompt"* block. Do **not** reply
"fix it for me" — a finding is a symptom report, not a spec (see
[[feedback-never-apply-review-suggestions-literally]]).

**Signal quality, first data point: good.** On #1066 it caught a genuine cross-section
contradiction in a docs-only diff — the `sweep` section was re-scoped to interior nodes
while an *unedited* section 170 lines away still listed the sweep among
`reseal_scope_root`'s callers. It reasons across the whole file, not just the diff hunk,
which is exactly the class CodeRabbit's diff-scoped review misses.

**How to apply:** after flipping a PR ready, poll `pulls/N/comments` for
`macroscopeapp[bot]` alongside the CodeRabbit surfaces. When a finding names an unchanged
section, verify the contradiction against the file before editing — and prefer correcting
the stale section over relaxing the new one.

before investigating the diff. Re-run before triaging — `gh run rerun <id> --failed`. Note the
called workflow cannot be re-run standalone (`workflow_call` from `ci.yml`); target the parent CI
run id, and expect a misleading "its workflow file may be broken" message even when the rerun does
in fact start.

`macroscope` was added as a PR review tool on FSM1/cipher-box on **2026-08-05**, joining
CodeRabbit and Greptile (Greptile quota resets mid-Aug 2026). Three reviewers now.

## CREDITS EXHAUSTED 2026-08-06 ~00:54Z — it reviews nothing until topped up

All five agents now return `conclusion: skipped` with `output.title == "Credit balance exhausted."`
The last PR it actually reviewed was #1104. Everything after gets **CodeRabbit only**, and with
Greptile quota-locked until mid-August that leaves a single bot reviewer — so the ship agents' own
`/simplify` + `/security-review` + `/crypto-privacy-review` passes carry more weight, not less.

**This silently defeated the obvious "is macroscope done?" test.** A `skipped` run is `completed`,
so a poller that waits for "all macroscope check-runs completed" scores full coverage on a PR
macroscope never looked at — the wave-4 false-all-clear pattern all over again. **Never treat
`completed` as `reviewed`.** Test `conclusion != "skipped"`, and check
`output.title` for `credit balance exhausted` to stop waiting immediately instead of holding the PR
ready for a reviewer that will never answer. `recycle-both.sh` now does both and prints an explicit
`macroscope_reviewed=0` warning.

**Its triggering is INCONSISTENT — do not model it as strictly ready-only.** The user
disabled draft review on 2026-08-05, and it then skipped several draft heads. But on
**#1072 head `c806df6d5` (2026-08-05 14:05Z) all four agents ran on a PR that was in
draft** — pushed ~8 min after a re-draft. It then ran on *nothing* for the next head
`bc47da7d0`. Working hypothesis (unconfirmed): once a PR has been ready at least once, it
may review later pushes regardless of draft state, but not reliably. **Never infer coverage
from draft state — always query the head's check-runs** (`commits/<sha>/check-runs`,
filter `name|test("macroscope";"i")`) to see whether it actually ran.

`Macroscope - Correctness Check` skips far more often than the other three agents; a
`skipped` conclusion there is normal and is not a pass.

**A `success` conclusion does NOT mean that agent posted no findings.** On #1078,
`Language idioms` reported `success` while still having an inline thread open. Its
conclusions describe the agent's run, not the review outcome — always enumerate
`reviewThreads`, and **re-query before concluding you have them all**: a first GraphQL
query returned 3 threads where a second returned 4.

**`Ticket Requirements` verdict grammar.** `neutral` is NOT synonymous with a spec
mismatch — across one wave it meant a real deviation once, a benign harvest-list note
twice, and an unchanged previously-reported item once. Always read the check-run's
`output` field and compare against the previous run; it re-scopes between heads (one PR
went "3 harvest items" → "1 unimplemented item" with no code change). It also declines to
re-post an unchanged finding, saying so explicitly.

**Consequence for the draft convention.** Coverage is not guaranteed on a draft
([[feedback-keep-prs-draft-control-cr-timing]]) — CodeRabbit is genuinely ready-gated, so a
draft PR sitting with "no findings" still proves nothing. The flip to ready is the reliable
trigger for all three at once. When flipping to collect verdicts, **hold ready until each
reviewer has actually landed on the head**: on #1072 macroscope took ~4 min and CodeRabbit
~8.5 min after the flip, so a script that re-drafts on the first CodeRabbit status-comment
touch (~1 min) cuts both off. See `recycle-both.sh`.

**Where its output lands.** Author login is **`macroscopeapp[bot]`**. The review event
itself (`pulls/N/reviews`) is `COMMENTED` with an **empty body** — the findings are
inline `pulls/N/comments` entries. So a poller that reads only review *bodies* sees
nothing, the mirror of the CodeRabbit trap in
[[project-coderabbit-verdict-two-surfaces]]. Poll `pulls/N/comments` and filter on
`.user.login`.

**Finding format:** severity emoji + level (`🟠 **High**`), a `file:line` anchor, prose,
then a collapsible *"Reply 'fix it for me' or copy this AI Prompt"* block. Do **not** reply
"fix it for me" — a finding is a symptom report, not a spec (see
[[feedback-never-apply-review-suggestions-literally]]).

**Signal quality, first data point: good.** On #1066 it caught a genuine cross-section
contradiction in a docs-only diff — the `sweep` section was re-scoped to interior nodes
while an *unedited* section 170 lines away still listed the sweep among
`reseal_scope_root`'s callers. It reasons across the whole file, not just the diff hunk,
which is exactly the class CodeRabbit's diff-scoped review misses.

**How to apply:** after flipping a PR ready, poll `pulls/N/comments` for
`macroscopeapp[bot]` alongside the CodeRabbit surfaces. When a finding names an unchanged
section, verify the contradiction against the file before editing — and prefer correcting
the stale section over relaxing the new one.

`other` is a `Result<AdoptOutcome, GateError>`, so `other.is_ok()` genuinely discarded the verdict. Two problems with the proposed fixes:

- `other.err()` reproduces the defect — `None` for the whole `Ok` half, which is the likeliest regression here (the test exists to prove an impostor identity is rejected).
- `{other:?}` **does not compile.** `AdoptOutcome` (`crates/engine/src/net/resolve.rs:75`) carries `Zeroizing<[u8;32]>` scope seeds and deliberately derives no `Debug`. `GateError` is `Debug`; the `Ok` type is the blocker. `macroscope` was added as a PR review tool on FSM1/cipher-box on **2026-08-05**, joining
CodeRabbit and Greptile (Greptile quota resets mid-Aug 2026). Three reviewers now.

## CREDITS EXHAUSTED 2026-08-06 ~00:54Z — it reviews nothing until topped up

All five agents now return `conclusion: skipped` with `output.title == "Credit balance exhausted."`
The last PR it actually reviewed was #1104. Everything after gets **CodeRabbit only**, and with
Greptile quota-locked until mid-August that leaves a single bot reviewer — so the ship agents' own
`/simplify` + `/security-review` + `/crypto-privacy-review` passes carry more weight, not less.

**This silently defeated the obvious "is macroscope done?" test.** A `skipped` run is `completed`,
so a poller that waits for "all macroscope check-runs completed" scores full coverage on a PR
macroscope never looked at — the wave-4 false-all-clear pattern all over again. **Never treat
`completed` as `reviewed`.** Test `conclusion != "skipped"`, and check
`output.title` for `credit balance exhausted` to stop waiting immediately instead of holding the PR
ready for a reviewer that will never answer. `recycle-both.sh` now does both and prints an explicit
`macroscope_reviewed=0` warning.

**Its triggering is INCONSISTENT — do not model it as strictly ready-only.** The user
disabled draft review on 2026-08-05, and it then skipped several draft heads. But on
**#1072 head `c806df6d5` (2026-08-05 14:05Z) all four agents ran on a PR that was in
draft** — pushed ~8 min after a re-draft. It then ran on *nothing* for the next head
`bc47da7d0`. Working hypothesis (unconfirmed): once a PR has been ready at least once, it
may review later pushes regardless of draft state, but not reliably. **Never infer coverage
from draft state — always query the head's check-runs** (`commits/<sha>/check-runs`,
filter `name|test("macroscope";"i")`) to see whether it actually ran.

`Macroscope - Correctness Check` skips far more often than the other three agents; a
`skipped` conclusion there is normal and is not a pass.

**A `success` conclusion does NOT mean that agent posted no findings.** On #1078,
`Language idioms` reported `success` while still having an inline thread open. Its
conclusions describe the agent's run, not the review outcome — always enumerate
`reviewThreads`, and **re-query before concluding you have them all**: a first GraphQL
query returned 3 threads where a second returned 4.

**Its check-runs complete BEFORE its inline comments post — by many minutes.** On #1104
(2026-08-06) all five agents read `completed`/`success` at 23:40:57Z and a thread on
`net/adopter.rs` appeared at **23:49:52Z**, nine minutes later. Two `reviewThreads` queries at
23:44Z both returned zero, so the PR looked reviewed-and-clean when a finding was still in flight.
**Never treat check-run completion as "all findings are in."** Re-query threads several minutes
after the runs complete, and again before declaring a PR clean.

**Its suggested diff can contradict its own rationale.** Same #1104 finding: it correctly argued
the repo idiom is `panic!("expected …, got {other:?}")`, then suggested
`panic!("…, got {:?}", other.err())` — which prints `None` for the `Ok` case, i.e. exactly the
information loss it was complaining about. Same rule as CodeRabbit
([[feedback-never-apply-review-suggestions-literally]]): take the diagnosis, write the fix.

**`Ticket Requirements` verdict grammar.** `neutral` is NOT synonymous with a spec
mismatch — across one wave it meant a real deviation once, a benign harvest-list note
twice, and an unchanged previously-reported item once. Always read the check-run's
`output` field and compare against the previous run; it re-scopes between heads (one PR
went "3 harvest items" → "1 unimplemented item" with no code change). It also declines to
re-post an unchanged finding, saying so explicitly.

**Consequence for the draft convention.** Coverage is not guaranteed on a draft
([[feedback-keep-prs-draft-control-cr-timing]]) — CodeRabbit is genuinely ready-gated, so a
draft PR sitting with "no findings" still proves nothing. The flip to ready is the reliable
trigger for all three at once. When flipping to collect verdicts, **hold ready until each
reviewer has actually landed on the head**: on #1072 macroscope took ~4 min and CodeRabbit
~8.5 min after the flip, so a script that re-drafts on the first CodeRabbit status-comment
touch (~1 min) cuts both off. See `recycle-both.sh`.

**Where its output lands.** Author login is **`macroscopeapp[bot]`**. The review event
itself (`pulls/N/reviews`) is `COMMENTED` with an **empty body** — the findings are
inline `pulls/N/comments` entries. So a poller that reads only review *bodies* sees
nothing, the mirror of the CodeRabbit trap in
[[project-coderabbit-verdict-two-surfaces]]. Poll `pulls/N/comments` and filter on
`.user.login`.

**Finding format:** severity emoji + level (`🟠 **High**`), a `file:line` anchor, prose,
then a collapsible *"Reply 'fix it for me' or copy this AI Prompt"* block. Do **not** reply
"fix it for me" — a finding is a symptom report, not a spec (see
[[feedback-never-apply-review-suggestions-literally]]).

**Signal quality, first data point: good.** On #1066 it caught a genuine cross-section
contradiction in a docs-only diff — the `sweep` section was re-scoped to interior nodes
while an *unedited* section 170 lines away still listed the sweep among
`reseal_scope_root`'s callers. It reasons across the whole file, not just the diff hunk,
which is exactly the class CodeRabbit's diff-scoped review misses.

**How to apply:** after flipping a PR ready, poll `pulls/N/comments` for
`macroscopeapp[bot]` alongside the CodeRabbit surfaces. When a finding names an unchanged
section, verify the contradiction against the file before editing — and prefer correcting
the stale section over relaxing the new one.

1. **`sync/op.rs:427-458`** — wire round-trip coverage for `ScopeCrossing::Cross`. Labelled Trivial, but this is a *new wire-format variant* from an `Op` schema change; wire coverage for it is exactly what this repo's fail-closed discipline demands. Worth doing.

Evaluate on merit. The current code hard-codes `ScopeCrossing::Intra` at two facade call sites with a comment that this session holds one scope. A helper that *derives* the crossing is better if it cannot be wrong; it is worse if it invents a derivation the session cannot actually perform. _🩺 Stability & Availability_ | _🟡 Minor_ | _⚡ Quick win_

`send_with_token` returns `ApiError::Decode` and leaves the token in `state.access_token`. `request_authed_with` never reaches its 401 refresh path, because the failure happens before the request is sent. Apply the same treatment here. After the token is cleared, the next call goes out unauthenticated and the server's 401 drives a refresh.

-        // Scope the borrow so it never crosses the await below.

  so an `apps/web`-only diff does trigger it. No gap there either.

write coverage that never runs, and it is a different failure from this one.

content.content:
The generalized tell: **the conflict git shows you is not the break.** A deleted definition conflicts
loudly; its new importer merges quietly. Always grep the post-merge tree for users of any symbol the
other side removed.

**How to apply:**
- Verify the PAIRWISE merge, not just each PR against main — two PRs both green against main can
  still break each other. Land the definition-owner first, then rebase the consumer.
- After merging a shape-changing PR, before merging any other in-flight PR that USES the changed type, verify the combined tree COMPILES — don't trust MERGEABLE. Either rebase the in-flight PR onto the new main and let its CI re-run, or `cargo check` the merge locally.
- When fanning out parallel PRs, note which touch a shared type's definition vs its call sites; flag that pair as a semantic-conflict risk even when files are "disjoint".
- A red main from this is a P0 (blocks EVERY open PR's CI, since CI builds the merge-with-main). The break is **main-only** — no open PR branch (all forked pre-merge) contains it, so fix it on a branch cut from CURRENT main, not on an existing PR. Keep that hotfix PR a DRAFT to avoid burning a CodeRabbit slot on a trivial compile fix.
- After the hotfix merges, open PRs' CI won't auto-rerun against fixed main — trigger a rerun (or push) on each. See [[feedback-verify-pr-findings-on-the-pr-branch]].

error[E0004]: non-exhaustive patterns: `ResealError::TooManyCommittedGrants` not covered

#1098 adds that variant; #1101 replaces a blanket `map_err` with an exhaustive match. #1101 also carries two textual conflicts, both pure unions (a module doc and a test `use` list).

**macroscope ran out of credits at 00:54Z.** Only #1104 got its review; the other six carry CodeRabbit alone, and Greptile is quota-locked until mid-August. Worth topping up before merging a wave with two rotation PRs and a signing-oracle fix.

**#1106 filed** — a content write silently clobbers a concurrently published version. `rebase_update_content` never reads `op.base_sequence`, and `publish_head` passes `min_current_sequence: None`. Silent, unrecoverable, and a spec gap too — `blueprint/engine.md` has no edit-vs-edit conflict row.

name: project-semantic-merge-conflict-shape-change
description: Shape-changing PRs semantically conflict with in-flight PRs — textual MERGEABLE does not mean it compiles
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: af9d085f-d8ee-4c7c-a115-037957347414
  modified: 2026-08-06T07:35:06.149Z
---

When PR A changes a shared type's SHAPE (adds/removes a struct field, changes a fn signature) and PR B — forked before A merged — USES that type, GitHub's `mergeable=MERGEABLE`/`CLEAN` does NOT catch the incompatibility (it's textual only, and the two edits touch different lines). Both PRs are individually green; **main breaks the moment both land.** Happened 2026-07-23: #779 dropped `SweepTarget.ipns_name`, #782's `grants/create.rs` descendant re-key still read `target.ipns_name` → main (2c509d72c) failed `cargo check` (`E0609 no field ipns_name`); fixed by #790 sourcing the enumerated `descendant.ipns_name` (mirroring #779's own sweep.rs fix).

**Recurred 2026-08-01 (#944 + #946)** — same shape, different symbol, caught BEFORE merge by
compile-verifying the pair. #946 deleted `pub(crate) const RETIRE_BATCH_MAX` from
`crates/engine/src/net/retire.rs` (moved to `net/mod.rs` as `REGISTRY_BATCH_MAX`); #944 added a NEW
consumer of the deleted name in `sync/drain.rs`. Git conflicts only the *definition* — the `use`
line in `drain.rs` **auto-merges silently** → `E0432: unresolved import` after resolving retire.rs
the obviously-correct way. Also collided on a test fake: both added `refuse_register` to `Blocks`
with incompatible signatures (`bool` vs `Vec<u8>`), not overloadable in Rust.

The generalized tell: **the conflict git shows you is not the break.** A deleted definition conflicts
loudly; its new importer merges quietly. Always grep the post-merge tree for users of any symbol the
other side removed.

**Wave-5 instance (2026-08-06), #1098 × #1101 — the enum-variant shape.** #1098 added a variant
`ResealError::TooManyCommittedGrants`; #1101 replaced a blanket `.map_err(|_| Rejected)` with an
**exhaustive match, no catch-all**. Both correct alone, both green alone, textually clean merge —
the combined tree fails with `error[E0004]: non-exhaustive patterns`. **One PR adding an enum
variant while another adds an exhaustive match over that enum is a conflict neither PR's CI can
see.** Fix is one line in whichever merges second.

The useful half: **the no-catch-all design is what made it findable.** With a wildcard the merge
would have compiled and silently routed the new variant to whatever the wildcard chose. Prefer
exhaustive matches *because* they convert a silent mis-mapping into a compile error — then expect
exactly this conflict and build the combined merge to catch it. Add to the fan-out risk list: not
just "definition vs call sites", but **"adds a variant" vs "matches the enum exhaustively"**.

**How to apply:**
- Verify the PAIRWISE merge, not just each PR against main — two PRs both green against main can
  still break each other. Land the definition-owner first, then rebase the consumer.
- After merging a shape-changing PR, before merging any other in-flight PR that USES the changed type, verify the combined tree COMPILES — don't trust MERGEABLE. Either rebase the in-flight PR onto the new main and let its CI re-run, or `cargo check` the merge locally.
- When fanning out parallel PRs, note which touch a shared type's definition vs its call sites; flag that pair as a semantic-conflict risk even when files are "disjoint".
- A red main from this is a P0 (blocks EVERY open PR's CI, since CI builds the merge-with-main). The break is **main-only** — no open PR branch (all forked pre-merge) contains it, so fix it on a branch cut from CURRENT main, not on an existing PR. Keep that hotfix PR a DRAFT to avoid burning a CodeRabbit slot on a trivial compile fix.
- After the hotfix merges, open PRs' CI won't auto-rerun against fixed main — trigger a rerun (or push) on each. See [[feedback-verify-pr-findings-on-the-pr-branch]].

- Empirically: `pnpm test` runs `apps/web` at 26 files / 216 tests.

The original claim described the **v1** package set (`@cipherbox/sdk-core`, `@cipherbox/crypto`,
`@cipherbox/api-client` …), none of which exist in the v2 layout. It went stale at the rewrite.

skills.name: resolve-pr-reviews
skills.content:
# Resolve PR Review Comments

Resolve all open review comments on the current PR from any automated reviewer (CodeRabbit, GitHub Copilot, etc.) or human reviewers.

## Workflow

### 1. Identify the PR

```bash
PR_NUMBER=$(gh pr view --json number --jq '.number')
```

If no PR exists for the current branch, stop and inform the user.

### 2. Fetch all unresolved review threads

Use the GraphQL `reviewThreads` query to get threads with `isResolved` status:

```bash
REPO_OWNER=$(gh repo view --json owner --jq '.owner.login')
REPO_NAME=$(gh repo view --json name --jq '.name')

gh api graphql -f query="
{
  repository(owner: \"$REPO_OWNER\", name: \"$REPO_NAME\") {
    pullRequest(number: $PR_NUMBER) {
      reviewThreads(first: 100) {
        nodes {
          id
          isResolved
          comments(first: 10) {
            nodes {
              id
              author { login }
              body
              path
              line
              createdAt
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}"
```

Filter to only unresolved threads. If none, report "No unresolved review threads" and stop.

### 3. Triage each comment

For each unresolved thread, read the comment and the referenced code. Categorize as:

- **Valid fix needed** — the comment identifies a real bug, security issue, or meaningful improvement
- **Already addressed** — the issue was fixed in a later commit on this branch
- **Not applicable** — the suggestion doesn't apply (explain why)

### 4. Implement fixes

For all "valid fix needed" comments:

1. Read the referenced file and understand the context
2. Implement the fix
3. Track which thread the fix addresses

Do NOT:

- Make unrelated changes or refactors
- Add features beyond what the comment requests
- Increase timeouts or add retries as a first approach — fix root causes

### 5. Run tests locally

After ALL fixes are implemented:

```bash
# Type check
pnpm typecheck

# Run relevant unit tests
pnpm test

# If E2E-relevant changes were made, run E2E tests too
cd tests/web-e2e && pnpm exec playwright test
```

Do NOT proceed to commit until tests pass. If tests fail, fix the failures first.

### 6. Commit and push

```bash
git add <specific-files>
git commit -m "fix: address PR review comments"
git push
```

### 7. Reply to and resolve each thread

For each thread, reply explaining what was done, then resolve:

- **Fixed comments**: Reply with what was changed and where, then resolve
- **Already addressed**: Reply explaining which commit addressed it, then resolve
- **Not applicable**: Reply with clear reasoning for not making changes, then resolve

Reply via REST (use `--field` not `-f` for `in_reply_to` — must be integer):

```bash
gh api repos/$REPO_OWNER/$REPO_NAME/pulls/$PR_NUMBER/comments \
  --field in_reply_to=COMMENT_ID \
  --raw-field body='...'
```

Resolve via GraphQL (can batch multiple):

```bash
gh api graphql -f query='
mutation {
  resolveReviewThread(input: {threadId: "THREAD_ID"}) {
    thread { isResolved }
  }
}'
```

### 8. Report summary

Print a summary table:

- Thread count resolved
- Fixes made (with file:line references)
- Comments marked as already addressed or not applicable

## The batch — 6 PRs

Ownership is the batching unit. `facade.rs` is 6195 lines with 13 contenders, `write_plane.rs`
6608 with 4, `drain.rs` 2971 with 7. One PR may own each per wave.

| PR | Track | Issues | Owns | Why here |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | engine | **1054** | `net/adopter.rs`, `gate/floor.rs`, `net/rotation.rs` (`GatedRoots`), `rotation/cascade.rs` | **Shape change**, and both #1025 and #1026 read through `gated_root`. Must land before either |
| **2** | core | **1050** | `core/seal/{grant,section}.rs`, `core/kat/vectors/grant/`, `rotation/reseal.rs`, `grants/create.rs`, `gate/adoption.rs` | **Closes the #989 core track** — its only remaining open child. High value: self-DoS + permanently-unpublishable scope root. Disjoint from every other PR here |
| **3** | engine | **1026** | `rotation/rotate_write.rs`, `net/rotation.rs`, `net/author.rs`, `net/retire.rs` | The #635 spine. **Shape change** — `RepublishedNode` gains `current_name` per ADR 0004. Gates #1019, #764, #1016 |
| **4** | engine | **1018** | `sync/drain.rs`, `sync/rebase.rs`, `sync/mod.rs`, `rotation/trigger.rs` | Scope-exit trigger consumption. Disjoint from the `rotation/` hot files except `trigger.rs`, which nobody else owns this wave |
| **5** | security | **1034 + 713 + 933 + 1086** | `api/client.rs`, `seams/http.rs`, `desktop-seams/src/http.rs`, `packages/client/src/seams/http.ts`, `content/{provider,read}.rs` | One contiguous auth/transport surface. Carries a **live signing oracle** — see below |
| **6** | web | **1069 + 808 + 1079** | `FileBrowser.tsx`, `snapshotStore.ts`, +`OfflineBanner`, +`NotificationToast`, +`stores/notification.store.ts`, +`hooks/useOnlineStatus.ts`, `AppShell.tsx`, `components/layout/StatusIndicator.tsx`, `useFolderPicker.ts` | Error classification is the natural home for the notice class #808 introduces |
| **7** | web | **1093 + 1092 + 1080** | `DetailsDialog.tsx`, +`details/*`, +`TextEditorDialog.tsx`, `useFilePreview.ts`, `useFileDownload.ts`, `FilePreviewDialog.tsx`, `FileBrowserActions.tsx`, `media/service.ts` | #1092 and #1080 both rework `useFilePreview.ts`; #1093 is the smallest and lands first inside the PR |

**#1050 was added after the hygiene pass**, which revealed it as #989's sole open child — so one
S–M PR closes an entire track. Verified disjoint: #1054 owns `gate/floor.rs` (not
`gate/adoption.rs`), #1026 owns `rotate_write.rs` (not `reseal.rs`), and #1025 — the other
`grants/create.rs` contender — is held to wave 6.

**#1075 was considered for PR-6 and rejected.** Its residual is larger than "partly delivered"
suggests: `introspection.ts:84` reads `view.blocked` only inside the e2e `settled()` wait
predicate — a test seam, not a rendered surface. Wave 6.

**Merge order: 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 → 6 → 7.** PRs 1 and 3 are the shape changes and must merge early
(`project-semantic-merge-conflict-shape-change`; the failure mode hit on #779/#782 and #944/#946).
PRs 3-6 are file-disjoint from each other and from 1-2.

**PR-5 × PR-6 was deliberately split along the `FileBrowser.tsx` / `FileBrowserActions.tsx` seam.**
They are different files. **#1091 is held to wave 6 precisely because it touches BOTH** — scheduling
it would recreate the wave-4 hazard where two PRs edit one interface and merge clean into a
duplicate.

### PR-4 carries a live security defect — #1034

`crates/engine/src/api/client.rs:108-121` takes `body.challenge` straight from the server response
and signs it with the identity key at `:121`. Nothing checks it carries the `cipherbox-login:v2:`
prefix its own test fixture uses (`:709`). A hostile or compromised API returns an arbitrary string
and gets it signed by the identity key — a signing oracle, live today, single-file XS fix.
This is why PR-4 is not deferred despite being the least glamorous batch.

## Held out of wave 5, with the reason

- **#1025** (sweep rewrite, L) — it shares `net/rotation.rs` and `net/author.rs` with PR-2 and both
  are L. Running two large `rotation/` PRs in one wave is the exact shape that produced wave 4's

content.content: #1103 feat: consume the scope-exit rotation triggers draft=true branch=feat/1018-consume-scope-exit-rotation-triggers ---BODY--- ## What this lands The queued scope-exit triggers are no longer dropped on the floor, and the two detection holes that would have let a trigger slip are closed. - **Full-depth detection.** `rebase` now resolves the *granted source scope root* by walking the source parent and then its ancestors nearest-first against an injected scope-root policy (`replay`/`rebase_one` take `scope_roots: &[NodeId]`). It previously named `from_parent` — correct only when the moved node was a direct child of the scope root, which is exactly the v1 one-level coverage hole `blueprint/engine.md` calls out (`#26 D7`). A chain that reaches no listed root falls back to the snapshot root: over-rotating an enclosing root costs a wave, rotating nothing leaves a revokee holding a live seed. - **Dedupe.** `replay` queues one trigger per source scope root, first-seen order — N ops leaving one scope are one rotation. - **The consumer.** `rotation/trigger.rs` gains the `ScopeExitRotator` seam and `consume_scope_exit_triggers`, which cuts one root per queued trigger, never short-circuits, and returns every failure in `ScopeExitReport::failed` instead of swallowing it. The grantee-arm implementation over the live transport is not landed, so the seam is faked in tests — the same pattern `SweepResolver` and `WriteSubtreeResolver` already follow (`rotation/mod.rs`). - **`OpKind::Move` now carries scope-crossing.** See the scope decision below. - **`ScopeCrossing` replaces the `cross_scope` / `exits_granted_source` bool pair** on both relocation ops. "Exits a granted source but is not cross-scope" is incoherent; as a pair it was representable and a decoder would have had to reject it. As one value it is unrepresentable, so no encode/decode symmetry check is needed — the illegal state is gone from the type rather than guarded at both ends. - **The drain** hands `replay` its scope root and halts a cross-scope `Move` the way it already halted a cross-scope `Relink`. Publishing a cross-scope relocation through the plain ref-move plan would carry the moved subtree into the destination still sealed at the source epoch. ## `OpKind::Move` — in scope, deliberately The issue does not mention it, but `OpKind::Move` had no scope-exit field at all, so a cross-scope move-with-rename could not queue a trigger. **This is in scope and is fixed here.** A kernel rename journals exactly one `Move` (`blueprint/desktop.md`), so `Move` — not `Relink` — is the desktop's entire move surface. Leaving it blind would have kept precisely the class of silent miss this issue exists to close: an exit that never rotates. It is an `Op` schema change; v2 is greenfield and pre-cutover, and an op a build cannot parse is `Retained`, never replayed and never removed (`sync/record.rs`), so the change fails closed. ## Errors in the issue body, verified against the code - **Line drift.** `scope_exit_triggers` is declared at `sync/rebase.rs:134`, not 133, and populated at `:246`, not 245. The deferral note is `sync/mod.rs:14-17`, not just `:16`. - **"The rebase side already detects the trigger" is not true.** The flag was never set by any production caller: `facade.rs:2222` was the *only* `Op::relink` construction outside tests and hard-coded `false, false`. Detection was effectively greenfield. - **The orchestrating brief's claim that `sync/drain.rs:964` also hard-codes the flag is wrong.** `drain.rs` never constructs a relink op; `:1029` is a *pattern match* on `cross_scope: false`, not a construction. `facade.rs:2222` was the single hard-coded site. - **"Retire the `sync/mod.rs:16` deferral note once the consumer exists"** — the note is rewritten rather than deleted, because deleting it outright would read as an all-clear the code does not support (see residuals). ## Known residuals — deliberately not done - **No production `ScopeExitRotator`.** Assembling a `RotateScopePlan` needs the scope root's committed set, current override seed, history links and pointer read key, none of which the sync layer holds; the grantee-arm net that resolves them is not landed. This is the issue's own stated dependency. Hence `Part of #1018`, not `Closes`. - **The engine is still single-scope**, so `facade.rs` authors `ScopeCrossing::Intra` for every relocation and no production path yet reaches `ExitsGrantedSource`. The scope-root policy is injected as a parameter, so the detection is exercised at depth 1 and depth N under a multi-scope fixture and gains nothing when the real scope map arrives. - **`DrainReport` carries no trigger field.** An earlier draft added one; with no rotator to hand it to it was written and never read, and the facade cannot author a cross-scope op, so no test could reach it. Untestable plumbing was dropped in the review pass; `ReplayReport::scope_exit_triggers` — which the drain's own `replay` call produces — stays the surface. - **`AlreadySatisfied` drops a scope-exiting op without queuing its trigger.** Unreachable today: a cross-scope relocation cannot publish, so gate-passing state can never show *our own* scope exit as already satisfied. The pass that lands cross-scope publishing must handle this branch, or a trigger is lost there. - **Durability of the intent is the durable op queue.** A cross-scope relocation halts the pass (`Halt::Unclassified`), which charges nothing and leaves the op at the head of the queue, so every pass re-derives the trigger until it settles. No separate durable trigger store was added; one would have been a second source of truth for state the queue already holds. ## `facade.rs` Touched minimally and only as forced by the type change: the two `Op::relink` / `Op::move_node` construction sites now pass `ScopeCrossing::Intra`, one import, and a stale trailing-bools comment replaced. No logic change. Flagging it since `facade.rs` is a hot file this wave. ## Review gates `/simplify`, `/security-review` and `/crypto-privacy-review` were run as rigorous manual passes against `git diff main...HEAD` — the slash-command subagents were unavailable in this environment (concurrency limit), so no gate was skipped, none was run as a skill. **`/simplify`** — four findings, all folded into the second commit: an unread `DrainReport` field, an uncalled `ScopeCrossing::is_cross_scope`, a comment on `rebase_one` whose stated rationale was about walking from the target (which the code does not do), and two rebase unit tests the sync narratives already state end-to-end. **`/security-review`** — the trigger is a revocation-boundary surface, so the questions were who can influence it and in which direction it fails. - *Influence*: `ScopeCrossing` is authored only by the facade and rides an HPKE-to-self sealed, owner-tagged op record. A store co-tenant's record classifies as `Retained`, never `Mine`, so an attacker cannot inject a forged scope-exit — nor suppress one beyond the pre-existing queue-integrity residual `blueprint/engine.md` already documents. - *Fallback direction*: over-rotate, never under-rotate. `Snapshot::ancestors` is cycle-guarded, so a malformed link cycle terminates rather than looping. - *Applied-vs-queued*: every `OpResolution` branch was walked. Applied exits queue a trigger; `MoveRaceLost`, the relocation guards and `SuffixExhausted` queue none, and in each the exit did not happen. `AlreadySatisfied` is the one asymmetry, recorded above as a residual. - *Dedupe*: collapses only equal roots. Two exits from distinct scopes that both hit the snapshot-root fallback do collapse — but in that state the engine knows neither scope, so it could not have rotated them separately either. - *DoS*: trigger and scope-root vectors are bounded by distinct scope roots, so the linear `contains` scans are over single-digit collections. - *Determinism*: no clock or RNG added; the scope-root policy enters as a parameter. **`/crypto-privacy-review`** — the diff touches no primitive, no key or seal material, and no trust-boundary read. `RotationOutcome` carries epochs only, and `RotateError::check()` is an existing key-material-free classifier. ## Already landed — do not re-implement

`rotate_scope` and the grantee-flat rotation path are written and simulation-tested in `crates/engine/src/rotation/rotate.rs`; `RotationTrigger::ScopeExit` already exists in `crates/engine/src/rotation/trigger.rs`. The rebase side already **detects** and queues the trigger. **Neither the primitive nor the trigger enum is in scope here.**

## Scope

The queued triggers are dropped on the floor. `ReplayReport::scope_exit_triggers` is declared at `crates/engine/src/sync/rebase.rs:133` and populated at `crates/engine/src/sync/rebase.rs:245`, and the only thing that mentions it outside `rebase.rs` is a doc comment at `crates/engine/src/sync/mod.rs:16` explaining that the rotation lands in a later slice. That slice is this one.

Land the consumer:

- the replay/drain path reads `scope_exit_triggers` and drives a `RotationTrigger::ScopeExit` rotation for each queued source scope root — grantee-triggered, flat and self-contained, re-sealing the **unchanged** committed set with blobs re-wrapped verbatim
- **full-depth scope-exit detection**, per the trigger table: a cross-scope move out of a granted source scope must be detected at any depth in the moved subtree, both hosts, one engine. Confirm the detection at `rebase.rs` is genuinely full-depth and extend it if it is not; a shallow check silently misses a scope exit that leaves a revokee holding a live seed.
- dedupe: several ops in one replay can exit the same source scope; one rotation per source scope root per replay
- a rotation that fails must not lose the trigger or block the drain — the trigger is durable intent, and a scope exit that never rotates is a silent trust hole, so the failure surfaces rather than being swallowed
- retire the `sync/mod.rs:16` deferral note once the consumer exists

`blueprint/engine.md`: Rotation primitives — Triggers ("Scope exit — full-depth coverage detection, both hosts, one engine; includes a cross-scope move out of a granted source scope" → `rotateScope`, grantee-triggered, flat).

Engine simulation:

- a cross-scope move out of a granted source rotates the source scope root, at depth 1 and at depth N
- the grantee rotation is flat: no descendant scope root is re-keyed and the committed tag set is byte-identical across the rotation
- N ops exiting one source scope produce exactly one rotation
- a failed rotation surfaces and does not silently drop the trigger
- an intra-scope move fires nothing — the non-trigger list holds

The concrete rotation resolvers and publishers over the real seams.

Nothing tracked yet.

## Already landed — do not re-implement

`crates/engine/src/rotation/` is ~6,300 lines and every named rotation primitive is **written and simulation-tested inline**:

| Primitive              | Location                                                               |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rotate_scope`         | `crates/engine/src/rotation/rotate.rs`                                  |
| `cascade_rotate_scope` | `crates/engine/src/rotation/cascade.rs`                                 |
| `enumerate_eager_set`  | `crates/engine/src/rotation/eager_set.rs`                               |
| `reseal_scope_root`    | `crates/engine/src/rotation/reseal.rs`                                  |
| `sweep_pass`/`run_sweep` | `crates/engine/src/rotation/sweep.rs`                                 |
| `rotate_scope_write`, `derive_write_name`, `build_repoint_object` | `crates/engine/src/rotation/rotate_write.rs` |
| `RotationTrigger`, `revoke_read_grant` | `crates/engine/src/rotation/trigger.rs`                 |

The eager-set law, the grantee-flat vs owner-cascade split, sweep idempotence, the child-first name wave and the three-channel re-point are all proven in simulation. **None of that is in scope here.**

## Scope

The four rotation seam traits have **no production implementation** — every existing impl is a testkit or inline-test fake:

- `ScopeRootPublisher` — `crates/engine/src/rotation/rotate.rs:96`
- `ChildIndexResolver` — `crates/engine/src/rotation/eager_set.rs:157`
- `SweepResolver` — `crates/engine/src/rotation/sweep.rs:124`
- `WriteWavePublisher` — `crates/engine/src/rotation/rotate_write.rs:148`

Land concrete impls over the real seams — `RecordTransport` plus the engine's `ApiClient` — reusing the existing publish/register/retire machinery rather than growing a parallel one:

- `crates/engine/src/net/record_publish.rs`, `publish.rs` — sequence-CAS scope-root publish, TTL and EOL, the adoption gate on read-back
- `crates/engine/src/net/register.rs` — register-first enrollment of every name a rotation mints, before its first publish

The rotation net has **no grantee arm**. Both production nets are owner-gated by their own field types:

A **grantee** holds no owner blob and no owner identity key. It recovers the same material from its own grant blob. Land that arm:

- a **grantee-keyed gated read** of a scope root — the adoption gate under the grantee's own encryption secret and the owner's contact-anchored identity as the stage-2 anchor, rather than the owner's `enc_secret`
- **grantee-side `RotateScopePlan` assembly**. ## Already landed — do not re-implement

`rotate_scope_write` and the whole write-plane wave are written and simulation-tested in `crates/engine/src/rotation/rotate_write.rs`: the commitment re-sign, the fresh write override seed, the child-first name wave with the root re-pointed last, `derive_write_name`, `build_repoint_object`, the three-channel re-point, register-first inventory swap and root linger.

The wave's **write edge** is production code: `WriteWavePublisher for WriteWaveNet` at `crates/engine/src/net/rotation.rs:1248` (#1101). **That is not in scope here.**

## Scope

`WriteSubtreeResolver` is the wave's **read edge** — the analogue of the cascade's `CascadeResealResolver` — and it has **no production implementation**. Every implementor is a test fake: `FakeResolver`, `PostFlipResolver` and `FailingResolver` at `crates/engine/src/rotation/rotate_write.rs:761`, `:784`, `:805`, all inside the test module opening at `:698`. The trait's own doc says so (`rotate_write.rs:150`): *"the real network/gate wiring is not landed and tests fake it."*

The trait is one method (`rotate_write.rs:154`):

```rust
async fn resolve_node(&self, node_id: &[u8; 16]) -> Result<WriteScopeNode, ResolveFailure>;
```

returning `node_id`, `current_name` and `child_node_ids` (`rotate_write.rs:77`). Land it over the real seams:

- **resolve + adoption-gate + unseal behind the trait.** Reuse `OwnerRotationNet`'s gated read (`crates/engine/src/net/rotation.rs`) rather than growing a parallel one — every record the enumeration consumes must have passed the adoption gate, and a gate failure is a fail-closed trust verdict, never staleness (rule 6).
- **`ResolveFailure` must keep the trust/availability split intact.** The enumeration at `rotate_write.rs:671-682` walks the subtree breadth-first through this seam; a record that cannot be authoritatively obtained must not be laundered into a retryable stall, and a node the walk cannot resolve must abort the wave rather than silently truncate the subtree. A truncated enumeration re-points the root while leaving interior nodes un-rotated — the revokee keeps a live write name under a root that claims to have moved.
- **child-rewrite coverage.** `WriteSubtreeResolver::resolve_node`'s doc carries the coverage obligation the production impl must satisfy; #1101's body defers it here explicitly.

## Why this is filed separately

It was **never in #1014's scope** — that issue named four seams and this is not one of them — so nothing mis-closed. #1027 (which closed #1014) deferred `SweepResolver` to #1025 and `WriteWavePublisher` to #1026, and both were honoured. `WriteSubtreeResolver` simply had no successor issue. #1101's body says its production implementation "is a separate issue"; this is that issue.

Note `rotate_scope_write` consequently has **no production caller** on `main` — outside its own module it is referenced only by a doc comment (`crates/engine/src/grants/create.rs:21-22`) and the `rotation/mod.rs` re-export (`:58-59`).

## Blueprint anchors

`blueprint/engine.md`: Rotation primitives — `rotateScopeWrite`, the child-first name wave, the three-channel re-point; Pointer planes — register-first inventory swap and root linger.

`CONTEXT.md`: name wave, write plane, register-first, root linger, adoption gate, forgery window.

## Gate

Engine integration suite against the fake network world, not inline hand-rolled fakes:

- every record the enumeration consumes has passed the adoption gate; a gate rejection aborts the wave and is never reported as staleness
- a node that cannot be authoritatively resolved aborts the wave rather than truncating the subtree — assert the root is **not** re-pointed in that case
- the production resolver and the inline fakes agree on the same simulation scenarios that `rotate_scope_write` is already tested against
- a resumed wave re-resolves from published records only, with no in-memory carry (the existing `is_republished` contract, now over the real read edge)

## Depends on

Nothing outstanding. The primitive, and the wave's write edge (`WriteWavePublisher`), are landed.

## Blocks

- **#1019** — write revoke / downgrade drives `rotate_scope_write`, which cannot run without this read edge. #1019's `Depends on` names only a production `WriteWavePublisher`; that is now landed, so without this edge recorded #1019 would read as unblocked while still being blocked.
- **#764** — reclaiming orphaned interior write-names after a post-flip crash operates on the same enumeration.

Part of #635

## Gate

- An interior node behind its scope's epoch is re-sealed to the current epoch and published; a node already at the epoch is a no-op. Re-running the pass changes nothing (idempotence), and concurrent sweepers are safe under CAS.
- The walk stops at scope-root boundaries — a descendant scope root inside the subtree is **not** swept, asserted explicitly, so the cascade/sweep split cannot silently regress.
- A below-floor scope root whose pointer re-points to a fresh record converges after the consult; one whose fresh record is still below the floor is refused fail-closed. Distinct, asserted outcomes.
- A forged below-floor record is refused, and no consult path admits it.
- A scope root encountered but absent from its parent's index is repaired and flagged **with no node re-sealed in the same pass**, proving the self-heal no longer rides the epoch comparison.
- Grant creation over a subtree with a lagging interior node refuses with `SubtreeNotConverged`, and succeeds once that node converges — the gate proven live in both directions.

## Size

Decided 2026-08-05: **kept whole**, and this issue retitled to match. Scope item 1 is the bulk of it — an interior-node lazy wave needs a new intra-scope walk and a child re-seal path (`net::author::author_child_envelope` exists; the enumeration and the rotation-side wrapper do not), and it invalidates most of the current `SweepTarget`. Items 2–5 are comparatively small once item 1 exists, and they are tightly coupled to it: the resolver's shape, the superseded verdict, and the convergence gate all depend on what the re-target leaves behind. Splitting would have meant a sibling issue whose consumer could not be written until it landed.

Expect a large diff in `crates/engine/src/rotation/` — treat it as a hot-file owner and do not run it in parallel with other `rotation/` work.

That question is now answered by **[ADR 0003 — Sweep population, and the below-floor descendant scope root](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0003-sweep-population-and-below-floor-scope-roots.md)** (FSM1/cipher-box-next#58, merged). **Read it before starting.** The answer is not the one the original scope assumed: the resolver could not obtain its work-list because the sweep is walking the wrong population, and the below-floor records it was meant to repair should not be repaired at all.

## What the ADR settles

**The sweep's population is interior nodes, not descendant scope roots.** #26 D2 puts the eager set — the rotated scope root plus every transitively-reachable descendant scope root — under the *cascade*, and gives the sweep the interior nodes that "ride a background sweep re-sealing epoch-lagged nodes". `CONTEXT.md` agrees: epoch lag is "a node whose envelope epoch is behind **its scope's** current epoch". The blueprint's `### sweep` section kept #26 D8's "the work-list is the epoch-lag predicate" and dropped D2's statement of *what* lags, and the implementation followed the blueprint.

**A scope root cannot lag its own floor.** `rotate_scope` and `cascade` both publish first and raise the floor second; `floor::advance_on_unseal` sets the floor equal to the adopted epoch; `minReadEpoch` bumps only on owner read rotations that publish first. So `recordEpoch < floor` on a scope root always means the record fetched is not the current one — most often because the parent's `directChildScopeIndex` names it at a name a `rotateScopeWrite` has since moved. The gate's stage-5 rejection is correct, and the repair is a pointer consult, not a re-seal.

**Consequently the current `sweep_pass` duplicates the cascade with a vacuous predicate.** It enumerates the eager set and calls `reseal_scope_root` — the cascade's job, landed over the real seams in #1053. Nothing it does can fire in production.

## Scope

1. **Re-target the sweep at interior nodes.** Enumerate the nodes *within* a scope from the scope root's read body, stopping at scope-root boundaries (those belong to the cascade), and select those whose envelope epoch is behind the scope's current epoch. Re-seal each under the current node seed at the current epoch via `net::author::author_child_envelope`, and CAS-publish. This replaces the `reseal_scope_root` path in `sweep_pass`, and `SweepTarget` collapses accordingly — an interior node carries no commitment, ledger, grant blobs, or ascent link, so most of the current struct is scope-root material that belongs to the cascade.
2. **Land the concrete resolver over `RecordTransport` + `ApiClient`,** reusing `OwnerRotationNet`'s gated read rather than growing a parallel one. With the population corrected it composes with `gated_root`/the child read path unchanged, because its work-list is drawn from records the adoption gate *accepts*.
3. **Route a below-floor scope root through a pointer consult.** Return a distinct *superseded* verdict — neither `Rejected` (a trust violation) nor `Unavailable` (a transport stall) — and have the handler consult that scope's pointer per #38 D4, re-resolve at the re-pointed `currentRootName`, and fail closed only if the fresh record is still below the floor.
4. **Decouple the index self-heal.** #38 D6's repair is "a scope root encountered but missing from its parent's index is repaired and flagged" — detectable from the enumeration walk alone. Run it on the walk result, independent of any epoch comparison. What is implemented today is canonicalisation performed *during* a lag re-seal, which is both a different repair and unreachable whenever the predicate is vacuous.
5. **Fix the grant-creation convergence gate.** `create_read_grant` (`crates/engine/src/grants/create.rs`) is `sweep_pass`'s only production caller. Its `SubtreeNotConverged` verdict fires only on a lost CAS race, which only happens on a publish, which only happens for a lagging node — so with a vacuous predicate the gate passes unconditionally and "a new grantee cannot regress through an ancestor scope's history" (#26 D2, `CONTEXT.md` "Epoch-converged") is **unenforced today**. Re-targeting the sweep makes the gate able to fire; it needs its own coverage proving it does, including the negative case.

## Definition of done

- [x] `blueprint/engine.md` `### sweep` corrected and `CONTEXT.md` "Lazy wave" tightened — **done in #1066**, so the blueprint is already normative for this work; read it, don't re-derive it
- [ ] ADR 0003 `Status:` flipped to `Accepted — implemented in FSM1/cipher-box#<this PR> (merged)` via a follow-up commit on cipher-box-next, per the ADR 0002 precedent

The blueprint and glossary are maintained **here**, not in cipher-box-next — that repo's `blueprint/` copies are the as-charted archive and must not be edited.

## Gate

- An interior node behind its scope's epoch is re-sealed to the current epoch and published; a node already at the epoch is a no-op. Re-running the pass changes nothing (idempotence), and concurrent sweepers are safe under CAS.
- The walk stops at scope-root boundaries — a descendant scope root inside the subtree is **not** swept, asserted explicitly, so the cascade/sweep split cannot silently regress.
- A below-floor scope root whose pointer re-points to a fresh record converges after the consult; one whose fresh record is still below the floor is refused fail-closed. Distinct, asserted outcomes.
- A forged below-floor record is refused, and no consult path admits it.
- A scope root encountered but absent from its parent's index is repaired and flagged **with no node re-sealed in the same pass**, proving the self-heal no longer rides the epoch comparison.
- Grant creation over a subtree with a lagging interior node refuses with `SubtreeNotConverged`, and succeeds once that node converges — the gate proven live in both directions.

## Size

Decided 2026-08-05: **kept whole**, and this issue retitled to match. Scope item 1 is the bulk of it — an interior-node lazy wave needs a new intra-scope walk and a child re-seal path (`net::author::author_child_envelope` exists; the enumeration and the rotation-side wrapper do not), and it invalidates most of the current `SweepTarget`. Items 2–5 are comparatively small once item 1 exists, and they are tightly coupled to it: the resolver's shape, the superseded verdict, and the convergence gate all depend on what the re-target leaves behind. Splitting would have meant a sibling issue whose consumer could not be written until it landed.

Expect a large diff in `crates/engine/src/rotation/` — treat it as a hot-file owner and do not run it in parallel with other `rotation/` work.

In the v2 engine, determinism is injected through seam traits (`SweepResolver`,
`WriteSubtreeResolver`, `ScopeExitRotator`, `ScopeRootPublisher`, `ChildIndexResolver`,
`WriteWavePublisher`, `CascadeResealResolver`). A trait with **only test-fake implementors**
compiles, has green tests, and reads as delivered — but the feature cannot run. Consumers written
against it are testable and non-functional at the same time.

Confirmed 2026-08-06 auditing #1014 (closed COMPLETED 2026-08-04). Of the four seams it scoped,
one — `SweepResolver` — still had no production impl. `WriteSubtreeResolver` had none either and
was in **no** issue's scope. Both were only findable by listing every `impl <Trait> for` and
checking whether the enclosing `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` line number is *above* it.

**The tell that a whole arm is missing, not just glue:** the production impls are gated by their
own field types. `OwnerRotationKeys` requires the owner's `enc_secret`/`identity`
(`crates/engine/src/net/rotation.rs:61-70`); `WriteWaveNet` requires an owner-only pointer seed

it read as ready to work while being hard-blocked. Same for #1019, whose `Depends on` named only
`WriteWavePublisher` (landed) and not `WriteSubtreeResolver` (absent). Filed #1108 and edged it.

  `impl <Trait> for` and prove production status by comparing against the enclosing

  `rotate_scope` and `rotate_scope_write` had none — every call site was in a test module.

#989  OPEN  core: the crates/core codec, crypto, and KDF catalog track
#991  OPEN  engine: the foundation track for seams, adoption gate, sync, grants, and rotation

=== #1102 body ===
engine: close the residual stage-3 trial-verify amplification by pinning the section's signer
---
## Problem

The adoption gate's stage 3 trial-verifies each seed-bearing structure against every committed write-capable pseudonym until one matches (`crates/engine/src/gate/adoption.rs`, `StructureAuthenticator::authenticate`). #1050 capped both factors — `entries` and `grantBlobs` at 1024, `historyLinks` at 256 — and made the scan resume at the pseudonym that last verified, so an honest section now costs `pseudonyms + structures`.

The adversarial case is untouched. Worst case is still the product: `(1 + 1024) x (1 + 1 + 1024 + 256 + 1 + 1)` = **~1.32M Ed25519 verifications per record**, roughly 60-80 s native and several minutes in a WASM worker, re-incurred on every sequence bump. The record needed is only ~475 KB, well under the 4 MiB `MAX_RESOLVED_RECORD_BYTES` ceiling.

The resume hint is steerable: the scan walks forward with stride 1 from `resume_at`, so an attacker who is an accepted contact publishes a scope root whose own owner-signed commitment names 1024 write pseudonyms they generated, then signs structure *k* under the pseudonym at index `(resume_at - 1) mod n`. Stages 1 and 2 both pass — the commitment genuinely is owner-signed by them — so stage 3 runs to completion with the hint saving nothing. Attacker cost is ~1284 signatures (~50 ms); victim cost is the full product. Amplification ~1000x.

Surfaced by the crypto-privacy and security review gates on #1050, which both scoped the fix out of that PR deliberately.

## Fix

`reseal_scope_root` signs **every** structure in a section under one `identity.pseudonym_signer`, so a section that switches signers part-way is not something any current producer emits. Two candidate shapes:

1. **Pin the signer.** Resolve it on the first structure, then require every later structure to verify under that one key. Worst case becomes `pseudonyms + structures` ~= 2309, a ~570x reduction, and it tightens the trust model rather than loosening it.
2. **Per-section trial-verify budget** of `pseudonyms + structures`, failing closed on exhaustion. Same ceiling, weaker guarantee, and a less legible rejection.

Either is a **semantic tightening of what the gate accepts** — a section signed by two pseudonyms becomes unadoptable — so it is a spec decision for `blueprint/core.md` / `blueprint/engine.md`, not a drive-by change. That is why it was not folded into #1050. It needs:

- the blueprint to state the single-rotator-per-section invariant normatively;
- the release-active produce-side mirror per AGENTS.md rule 8 (`net/author.rs::check_scope_root` already runs the same predicate, so symmetry likely holds for free — verify, do not assume);
- a KAT reject vector for a mixed-signer section;
- an explicit answer for whether any planned multi-writer shape ever needs per-structure signers, since getting this wrong makes honest scope roots permanently unadoptable.

Part of the v2 build.

########## #648 ##########
#648 desktop: implement fuse read/write paths, journal ack, and freshness
## Scope

Ranged chunk reads (cached-first, CID-verified fetch, first byte before last byte) with the bounded in-memory plaintext LRU chunk cache zeroized on unmount; per-handle sealed spill files under ephemeral XChaCha20 keys; release/create/mkdir/rename/unlink/rmdir each becoming exactly one facade intent op, acked at durable StagingStore journal time (no-false-ack); honest ENOSPC on staging-budget exhaustion or hosted-quota preflight refusal; the scope-exit refusal path rejecting the op at journal time with EIO; dead-letter surfacing hooks; FUSE-op TTL checks + focus-window derivation from the op stream + engine-event-stream-driven push invalidation.
No adapters, no tray UI.

## Blueprint anchors

`blueprint/desktop.md`: Reads, writes, and the never-block law; Conflicts, dead letters, and rotation; Freshness

## Gate

fuse-op-core extended: never-block law, ack-at-journal, ENOSPC, TTL-check/invalidation coverage.

## Depends on

The three originally declared deps have all landed — #647 (PR #885), #632 (PR #706) and #630 (PR #700). Three dependencies this issue's own scope implies, previously undeclared, replace them:

- #884 — the scope requires "release/create/mkdir/rename/unlink/rmdir each becoming exactly one facade intent op". `OperationCore::rename` is today up to three separately-staged ops with a data-loss window, so the ack-at-journal law cannot be honestly implemented until #884 lands.
- #867 — the "dead-letter surfacing hooks" and the honest `ENOSPC` vs `EDQUOT` split are both deliverables of #867 (parts 1 and 4).
- #846 — "honest ENOSPC on staging-budget exhaustion" sits on the host-to-engine measured staging budget that #846 records as missing.



########## #1015 ##########
#1015 engine: implement grant invites
## Already landed — do not re-implement

`crates/engine/src/grants/` is ~3,770 lines and the whole non-invite grants surface is written and simulation-tested: `create.rs`, `accept.rs`, `ledger.rs`, `child_index.rs`, `revocation.rs`, `owner_entry.rs`, `contact.rs`. **Grant creation is done; this issue does not touch it.**

**The first half of invites is also done.** The original scope claimed invites were "100% greenfield" with "no invite type, no ephemeral-key blob path, no claim handling, and no ledger expiry field". Three of those four are false as of `main` @ `3d087d673`:

- **The ephemeral-key grant blob path exists.** `crates/engine/src/grants/invite.rs` is 645 lines. `EphemeralInvitee` (`invite.rs:49`) derives the throwaway identity from one random invite secret exactly the way `SessionIdentity` derives a real one from a login secret — the secp256k1 scalar adopted directly, the X25519 sealing half through the frozen `enc-subkey` edge. `mint_invite_grant` (`invite.rs:154`) mints the invite's `GrantRow` through the same `mint_grant_row` every contact grant uses, and **derives** the scope root's `ipnsName` from `write_scope_seed` rather than accepting it as input. Both are exported from `crates/engine/src/grants/mod.rs:35`.
- **Byte-shape parity is established and tested.** On the envelope surface — blinded tag, commitment entry, and the blob `reseal_scope_root` wraps — an invite is shaped like a personal grantee's; the module's tests cover self-location, commitment enforcement, and the cross-scope/stranger negatives.
- **The ledger expiry field is landed.** `GrantLedgerEntry::expires_at: Option<NonZeroU64>` at `crates/core/src/seal/write_body.rs:64`, encoded/decoded with absence-preserving coverage in that module, and the liveness predicate `entry_is_live` at `crates/engine/src/grants/ledger.rs:79`.

So the original plan's PR **(a)** — "the ephemeral-key blob plus the ledger expiry field" — has shipped. Do not re-implement any of it.

## Scope

Only the original plan's PR **(b)** remains: **claim-to-grant conversion and bearer write-link flagging**, plus wiring the expiry predicate that today has no production caller.

1. **Claim-to-grant conversion.** The owner receives the sealed, ephemeral-key-signed claim over the mailbox, verifies the signature against the ephemeral public half committed in the ledger, and converts it into a personal grant for the claimant's contact-anchored identity. Multi-claim: one link yields N personal grants and the link itself stays live until it expires or is revoked. Nothing of this exists today — `crates/engine/src/grants/mod.rs` states that claim conversion is not implemented here, and `crates/engine/src/mailbox/mod.rs:46` notes only that the transport carries an opaque payload whose invite-claim meaning **the grants layer** must frame. `crates/core/src/payload/mailbox.rs` supplies the generic sealed envelope (`seal_mailbox_payload` / `open_mailbox_payload`) and nothing invite-specific.

   Note the property `invite.rs` documents on `EphemeralInvitee`: the invitee is structurally a login identity, so a ledger's `recipientIdentityPk` for an invite row is **not** a contact-anchored identity. Conversion is what re-anchors it, and the converted personal grant must be anchored to the claimant's imported contact, never to the ephemeral half.

2. **Expiry enforcement on the read path.** `entry_is_live` has no production caller at `3d087d673` — only `invite.rs`'s own test. An expired ledger entry must be inert wherever the read/accept path consults the ledger, before and independently of the discovered-link-expiry trigger pruning it. `GrantLedgerEntry::expires_at`'s own doc states what a deadline does and does not guarantee; honour that framing rather than treating expiry as a capability boundary.

3. **Bearer write-link flagging.** A write invite hands out extractable subtree signing keys, so the engine must flag write links to the host as bearer capabilities. Revoking or expiring a write link is only real via `rotate_scope_write`, never by pruning the ledger alone; the engine must say so at the API surface rather than letting a host believe a ledger prune revoked anything. `mint_invite_grant` already takes a `Permission`, so the minting side accepts a write invite today with no such flagging.

Only the owner may mint an invite, convert a claim, or revoke a link — the same owner-only authority rule as every commitment change. `mint_invite_grant` is owner-only by construction (it takes the owner's encryption subkey secret); conversion and revocation must enforce it explicitly.

**One PR.** The original two-PR split is spent: (a) is merged, and what is left is a single coherent slice.

## Blueprint anchors

`blueprint/engine.md`: Grants and ledger — Invites, Authority, Accept flow; Rotation primitives — Triggers (discovered link expiry). Read it; do not re-derive it.

`CONTEXT.md`: grant blob, grant ledger, grant-set commitment, blinded tag, writer pseudonym, structure signature, mailbox, contact code.

## Gate

Engine simulation. The byte-shape and self-location properties are already covered in `invite.rs` — do not duplicate them. New coverage:

- multi-claim: two independent claimants each convert to their own personal grant; the link stays live
- a converted grant is anchored to the claimant's contact-anchored identity, not to the ephemeral half
- a claim whose ephemeral signature does not verify against the committed public half is rejected fail-closed
- a claim against an expired ledger entry is refused, and an expired entry is inert on the read path before any prune runs
- a non-owner cannot convert or revoke
- write links are reported to the host as bearer capabilities, and revoking one without a write rotation is refused or reported as not-yet-revoked
